MCQs Preparation

2.Software Engineering
3.AI/Machine Learning and Data Analytics

1.

Subject: Programming(Java)
1. Programming Fundamentals
Q1. What is a computer program?
A) A set of instructions for a computer
B) A physical device
C) A type of memory chip
D) A network cable
Reason: A program tells a computer what operations to perform.
Q2. Which language is directly executed by a CPU?
A) High-level Java source
B) Machine code
C) Pseudocode
D) Flowchart notation
Reason: The processor executes machine instructions; high-level code is translated to executable instructions.
Q3. What is an algorithm?
A) A finite sequence of steps to solve a problem
B) A programming language only
C) A hardware component
D) A random collection of commands
Reason: An algorithm is a finite, ordered procedure for solving a problem.
Q4. Which tool visually represents an algorithm using symbols?
A) Flowchart
B) Compiler
C) Debugger
D) Database
Reason: A flowchart uses standard symbols and arrows to represent steps and decisions.
Q5. What is pseudocode?
A) An informal, language-independent description of an algorithm
B) Java bytecode
C) A CPU instruction
D) A database query
Reason: Pseudocode describes logic without strict programming-language syntax.
Q6. What does a compiler do?
A) Translates source code into another form, commonly bytecode or machine code
B) Only displays output
C) Only stores files
D) Deletes variables
Reason: A compiler translates source code and reports compile-time issues.
Q7. Which tool executes Java bytecode?
A) JVM
B) Javadoc
C) Text editor
D) Scanner
Reason: The Java Virtual Machine executes Java bytecode.
Q8. Which file extension is normally used for Java source files?
A) .class
B) .java
C) .jar
D) .exe
Reason: Java source code is normally saved in .java files.
Q9. Which command compiles Hello.java?
A) java Hello.java only
B) javac Hello.java
C) jar Hello.java
D) javadoc Hello.java
Reason: javac compiles Java source files.
Q10. Which command commonly runs a compiled class named Hello?
A) javac Hello
B) java Hello
C) jar Hello
D) run Hello.java
Reason: The java launcher starts the JVM and invokes the class's entry point.
Q11. What is syntax in programming?
A) Rules for writing valid statements
B) The speed of the CPU
C) The program's output only
D) A storage device
Reason: Syntax defines the legal structure of statements and expressions.
Q12. What is a logic error?
A) The program runs but produces an incorrect result
B) A missing bracket detected by the compiler
C) A broken keyboard
D) A file extension
Reason: Logic errors are mistakes in reasoning or algorithm behavior.
Q13. What is a syntax error?
A) A violation of language grammar
B) An incorrect result with valid syntax
C) A slow algorithm only
D) A hardware failure
Reason: Syntax errors violate the programming language's grammar.
Q14. What is debugging?
A) Finding and correcting defects in a program
B) Translating a book
C) Compressing a file
D) Installing RAM
Reason: Debugging is the process of investigating and fixing software defects.
Q15. Which is a valid Java entry-point declaration for a conventional application?
A) public static void main(String[] args)
B) public void start()
C) static int main()
D) private main(String args)
Reason: The conventional Java entry point is public static void main(String[] args).
Q16. Which symbol usually ends a Java statement?
A) :
B) ;
C) ?
D) ,
Reason: Java statements commonly end with a semicolon.
Q17. Which pair encloses a block in Java?
A) ( )
B) [ ]
C) { }
D) < >
Reason: Curly braces delimit class, method, and control-flow blocks.
Q18. Which is a Java single-line comment marker?
A) //
B) <!--
C) ##
D) **
Reason: A double slash begins a single-line comment.
Q19. Which is a Java multi-line comment form?
A) /* ... */
B) // ... //
C) <!-- ... -->
D) ## ... ##
Reason: A block comment begins with /* and ends with */.
Q20. What is an IDE?
A) Software combining tools for writing, running, and debugging code
B) A data type
C) A CPU register
D) A Java operator
Reason: An integrated development environment provides an editor and development tools.
Q21. Which is a benefit of using meaningful variable names?
A) Improves readability and maintenance
B) Makes code always faster
C) Removes all bugs
D) Avoids compilation
Reason: Descriptive names help people understand code intent.
Q22. What is source code?
A) Human-readable program instructions
B) Only the program's output
C) A processor
D) A network protocol
Reason: Source code is written by developers in a programming language.
Q23. What is bytecode in Java?
A) Intermediate instructions executed by the JVM
B) A Java comment
C) A source-code variable
D) A hardware cable
Reason: The Java compiler usually translates source code into JVM bytecode.
Q24. What is portability?
A) Ability to run software on different platforms with suitable support
B) A program's file size
C) The number of comments
D) A variable's scope
Reason: Java bytecode can run on compatible JVM implementations across platforms.
Q25. What does WORA stand for in Java?
A) Write Once, Run Anywhere
B) Write Only Runtime Application
C) Work On Random Arrays
D) Wide Object Reference Access
Reason: WORA describes Java's portability across compatible JVM platforms.
Q26. What is an IDE example?
A) IntelliJ IDEA
B) Integer
C) IOException
D) Internet Protocol
Reason: IntelliJ IDEA is an IDE used for Java development.
Q27. What is the purpose of comments?
A) Explain code to readers; they are generally ignored by the compiler
B) Execute extra instructions
C) Allocate memory
D) Declare methods
Reason: Comments document intent and are not executed as program statements.
Q28. Which is a valid identifier?
A) 2count
B) totalMarks
C) class
D) first-name
Reason: Identifiers cannot begin with a digit, cannot use reserved keywords, and cannot contain a hyphen.
Q29. Are Java identifiers case-sensitive?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only methods
D) Only packages
Reason: total and Total are different identifiers in Java.
Q30. Which is a Java keyword?
A) student
B) while
C) totalMarks
D) score1
Reason: while is reserved for loop syntax.
Q31. What is a reserved keyword?
A) A word with a predefined language meaning that cannot be used as an ordinary identifier
B) Any variable name
C) A comment
D) A file name
Reason: Keywords have specific language meanings and are not available as ordinary identifiers.
Q32. What is the purpose of testing?
A) Check whether software behaves as expected
B) Guarantee zero defects forever
C) Replace all requirements
D) Make code unreadable
Reason: Testing provides evidence that software meets expected behavior and helps reveal defects.
Q33. What is an input in a program?
A) Data supplied for processing
B) Only the final result
C) A compiler warning
D) A class name
Reason: Input is data a program receives and processes.
Q34. What is output?
A) Information produced by a program
B) Only source code
C) A variable declaration
D) A syntax rule
Reason: Output is the result or information produced by execution.
Q35. What is a constant in programming?
A) A value intended not to change during its allowed scope
B) A loop that never ends
C) A class file
D) A debugger
Reason: Constants represent values that should remain fixed.
Q36. What is the purpose of a flowchart decision symbol, usually a diamond?
A) Represent a condition or branch
B) Represent program start only
C) Represent a printed page
D) Represent a variable declaration
Reason: A diamond conventionally represents a decision in a flowchart.
Q37. Which quality means an algorithm finishes after a finite number of steps?
A) Finiteness
B) Ambiguity
C) Randomness
D) Inheritance
Reason: An algorithm must terminate after finitely many steps.
Q38. Which quality means every algorithm step is precise and unambiguous?
A) Definiteness
B) Portability
C) Encapsulation
D) Concurrency
Reason: Definiteness requires clearly specified steps.
Q39. What is a program's runtime?
A) The period when the program is executing
B) The time spent naming variables only
C) The source file extension
D) The compile command
Reason: Runtime refers to execution of the program.
Q40. What is compilation?
A) Translating source code before or as part of execution
B) Printing a document
C) Entering keyboard input only
D) Deleting a class
Reason: Compilation translates code into a form suitable for execution.
Q41. What is an interpreter commonly described as doing?
A) Executing program instructions through interpretation
B) Only designing flowcharts
C) Only formatting code
D) Replacing every variable
Reason: An interpreter executes or evaluates code without requiring the same ahead-of-time compilation model.
Q42. Which is a good programming practice?
A) Use clear names and consistent formatting
B) Duplicate every block
C) Ignore compiler messages
D) Put all logic in one huge method
Reason: Readable, consistent code is easier to debug and maintain.
Q43. What is decomposition in problem solving?
A) Breaking a large problem into smaller manageable parts
B) Combining all variables into one
C) Deleting requirements
D) Skipping design
Reason: Decomposition reduces complexity by splitting a task into subproblems.
Q44. What is a test case?
A) Inputs, conditions, and expected outcomes used to test behavior
B) A Java keyword
C) A hardware part
D) A package declaration
Reason: Test cases define how behavior will be checked.
Q45. What does an error message often provide?
A) Information to help locate a problem
B) A guarantee of program correctness
C) A new data type
D) An automatic algorithm
Reason: Compiler and runtime messages can help diagnose issues.
Q46. What is refactoring?
A) Improving internal code structure while preserving intended behavior
B) Adding random features
C) Removing all tests
D) Changing output intentionally
Reason: Refactoring improves maintainability without intentionally changing external behavior.
Q47. What is a software requirement?
A) A capability or constraint the software should satisfy
B) A loop statement
C) A Java primitive
D) A comment marker
Reason: Requirements describe desired behavior and constraints.
Q48. Why is problem analysis important before coding?
A) It clarifies inputs, outputs, and constraints
B) It guarantees no debugging
C) It removes the need for tests
D) It automatically writes the program
Reason: Understanding the problem helps select a correct algorithm and design.
Q49. Which stage usually comes before implementation in a structured problem-solving workflow?
A) Problem analysis and design
B) Deployment only
C) Deleting source files
D) Code formatting only
Reason: Understanding and designing the solution before coding reduces avoidable mistakes.
Q50. What is maintainability?
A) How easily software can be understood and changed
B) How bright the screen is
C) The number of CPU cores only
D) A file's extension
Reason: Maintainable software is easier to fix, adapt, and improve.

2. Data Types & Variables
Q1. Which Java type stores a 32-bit signed integer?
A) byte
B) short
C) int
D) long
Reason: int is a 32-bit signed integer type.
Q2. Which primitive type stores a single UTF-16 code unit?
A) char
B) String
C) boolean
D) float
Reason: char is a 16-bit unsigned type representing a UTF-16 code unit.
Q3. Which primitive type stores true or false?
A) int
B) boolean
C) char
D) double
Reason: boolean represents the logical values true and false.
Q4. Which type is generally used for double-precision floating-point values?
A) float
B) double
C) long
D) short
Reason: double uses 64-bit floating-point representation.
Q5. Which is not a primitive Java type?
A) int
B) char
C) String
D) boolean
Reason: String is a reference type.
Q6. What is a variable?
A) A named storage location or binding for a value
B) A Java keyword only
C) A loop
D) A package
Reason: Variables let programs refer to values by name.
Q7. Which declaration is valid?
A) int age = 20;
B) age int = 20;
C) integer age = 20;
D) int = age 20;
Reason: Java declarations put the type before the variable name.
Q8. Which keyword declares a variable that can be assigned only once after initialization/definite assignment?
A) static
B) final
C) volatile
D) transient
Reason: A final variable can be assigned only once.
Q9. What is the default value of an instance int field?
A) null
B) 0
C) 1
D) Undefined garbage
Reason: Instance fields receive default values; int fields default to zero.
Q10. What is the default value of an instance boolean field?
A) true
B) false
C) null
D) 0
Reason: boolean fields default to false.
Q11. Do local variables receive automatic default values?
A) Yes, always
B) No; they must be definitely assigned before use
C) Only int variables
D) Only static locals
Reason: Local variables must be assigned before use.
Q12. Which type can store a larger range of integer values than int?
A) byte
B) short
C) long
D) char only
Reason: long is a 64-bit signed integer type.
Q13. What is the range of byte in Java?
A) 0 to 255
B) -128 to 127
C) -32768 to 32767
D) -1 to 1
Reason: Java byte is an 8-bit signed integer.
Q14. Which type is suitable for a decimal literal such as 3.14 by default?
A) float
B) double
C) int
D) char
Reason: A floating-point literal without a suffix is double by default.
Q15. Which suffix can mark a float literal?
A) D
B) F or f
C) L only
D) S
Reason: A float literal commonly uses F or f, such as 3.14f.
Q16. Which suffix commonly marks a long integer literal?
A) L or l
B) F
C) D
D) C
Reason: L or l indicates a long literal; uppercase L is easier to distinguish from 1.
Q17. What does casting do?
A) Converts a value from one type to another where permitted
B) Creates a package
C) Starts a thread
D) Declares a method
Reason: Casting requests or specifies a type conversion.
Q18. Which conversion from int to long is usually implicit?
A) Widening primitive conversion
B) Narrowing conversion
C) Reference cast
D) String parsing
Reason: Converting int to long widens the range and is allowed implicitly.
Q19. What can happen when casting a double to int?
A) Fractional part is discarded and range/precision may be lost
B) It always rounds to nearest
C) It always throws an exception
D) It becomes a String
Reason: A narrowing floating-to-integer conversion discards the fractional part and can lose range information.
Q20. Which type stores a reference to text?
A) String
B) char
C) boolean
D) byte
Reason: String is a reference type used for text.
Q21. What does null mean for a reference variable?
A) It refers to no object
B) It is the same as an empty string
C) It is always zero
D) It means false
Reason: null represents the absence of an object reference.
Q22. Which is a valid identifier?
A) student-name
B) _count
C) 3rdValue
D) public
Reason: Underscore alone is permitted as part of identifiers, though a single underscore is reserved in modern Java; _count is valid.
Q23. Are variable names case-sensitive?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only fields
D) Only local variables
Reason: Java treats count and Count as distinct names.
Q24. What is a local variable?
A) A variable declared inside a method or block
B) A variable declared only in a package
C) A class name
D) A constant pool entry
Reason: Local variables have scope within their declaring block or method.
Q25. What is an instance variable?
A) A non-static field belonging to each object
B) A variable declared only in a loop
C) A static class field
D) A method parameter only
Reason: Each object has its own instance-field state.
Q26. What is a static variable?
A) A class-level field shared by instances of that class
B) A variable that cannot change
C) A local variable
D) A method return value
Reason: A static field belongs to the class rather than individual instances.
Q27. What is a parameter?
A) A variable declared in a method or constructor parameter list
B) Only a method result
C) A package
D) A compiler warning
Reason: Parameters receive values supplied to a method or constructor.
Q28. What is an argument?
A) The value or expression supplied when calling a method
B) The declared return type
C) A field modifier
D) A source file
Reason: Arguments provide actual values to a method's parameters.
Q29. Which primitive type is 64-bit floating point?
A) float
B) double
C) long
D) int
Reason: double is the 64-bit floating-point type.
Q30. Which is the size of Java int?
A) 8 bits
B) 16 bits
C) 32 bits
D) 64 bits
Reason: Java int is defined as 32 bits.
Q31. Which is the size of Java long?
A) 16 bits
B) 32 bits
C) 64 bits
D) 128 bits
Reason: Java long is defined as 64 bits.
Q32. Which type can represent a single UTF-16 code unit?
A) char
B) String
C) int only
D) boolean
Reason: char represents one UTF-16 code unit, not necessarily every Unicode code point alone.
Q33. What is type inference with var?
A) Compiler infers a local variable's static type from its initializer
B) The variable changes type at runtime
C) It removes type checking
D) It is allowed for every field
Reason: var keeps static typing while letting the compiler infer the declared local variable type.
Q34. Which declaration using var is valid?
A) var name = "Ali";
B) var x;
C) var n = null;
D) var a = {1,2};
Reason: var requires an initializer from which a type can be inferred.
Q35. Can a Java variable declared final be reassigned?
A) Yes, any number of times
B) No, after it has been assigned
C) Only if it is local
D) Only if it is static
Reason: A final variable cannot be assigned again after its one permitted assignment.
Q36. Does final make a referenced object automatically immutable?
A) Yes
B) No; it prevents reassignment of the reference, not object-state changes
C) Only for arrays
D) Only for String
Reason: A final reference can still refer to a mutable object whose contents change.
Q37. Which type should generally be used for money when exact decimal arithmetic is needed?
A) double only
B) BigDecimal
C) boolean
D) char
Reason: BigDecimal supports decimal arithmetic with explicit precision/rounding choices.
Q38. Which wrapper class corresponds to primitive int?
A) Integer
B) Int
C) NumberInt
D) Long
Reason: Integer is the wrapper class for int.
Q39. What is autoboxing?
A) Automatic conversion from a primitive to its corresponding wrapper type
B) Converting String to file
C) Casting long to short
D) Creating a thread
Reason: Autoboxing converts a primitive such as int to Integer when needed.
Q40. What is unboxing?
A) Automatic conversion from a wrapper object to its primitive value
B) Converting a class to a package
C) Parsing a file
D) Allocating an array
Reason: Unboxing extracts a primitive value from a wrapper, and null unboxing can throw NullPointerException.
Q41. Which wrapper object can be null?
A) int
B) boolean primitive
C) Integer
D) char primitive
Reason: Integer is a reference type and can hold null.
Q42. What happens if a null Integer is automatically unboxed?
A) NullPointerException
B) Compile error always
C) It becomes zero
D) It becomes false
Reason: Unboxing null requires dereferencing a missing wrapper value.
Q43. Which primitive type has the smallest storage size among these?
A) long
B) int
C) byte
D) double
Reason: byte is an 8-bit primitive type.
Q44. Which keyword is used to declare a class-level field?
A) static
B) classlevel
C) global
D) shared
Reason: static marks a field as belonging to the class.
Q45. What is variable scope?
A) The region of code where a variable can be accessed by name
B) The amount of RAM used
C) The variable's value only
D) The data type size
Reason: Scope determines where a name is visible.
Q46. Which type is appropriate for a yes/no condition?
A) boolean
B) String
C) double
D) char
Reason: boolean represents true/false conditions.
Q47. What is a constant naming convention often used in Java?
A) UPPER_SNAKE_CASE
B) all spaces
C) Only lowercase digits
D) Camel case with spaces
Reason: Constants are often named with uppercase words separated by underscores.
Q48. Which is true about Java's primitive types?
A) They store primitive values rather than object references
B) All can be null directly
C) String is one of them
D) They all have variable size
Reason: Primitive variables hold values of their primitive type; they cannot directly hold null.
Q49. Which type is an 8-bit signed integer?
A) byte
B) short
C) int
D) long
Reason: Java byte is an 8-bit signed primitive type.
Q50. Which keyword can declare a class constant when combined with static?
A) final
B) volatile
C) transient
D) native
Reason: A static final field is commonly used to represent a class-level constant.


3. Operators & Expressions
Q1. Which operator performs addition?
A) +
B) %
C) ==
D) &&
Reason: The + operator adds numeric operands and also concatenates strings in suitable contexts.
Q2. Which operator gives the remainder?
A) /
B) %
C) *
D) !
Reason: The remainder operator is %.
Q3. What is the result of 7 / 2 when both operands are int?
A) 3.5
B) 3
C) 4
D) 2
Reason: Integer division truncates the fractional part toward zero.
Q4. Which operator tests equality of primitive values?
A) =
B) ==
C) ===
D) equals
Reason: == compares primitive values for equality.
Q5. Which operator assigns a value?
A) ==
B) =
C) !=
D) <=
Reason: The single equals sign is the assignment operator.
Q6. Which logical operator means AND with short-circuit evaluation?
A) &
B) &&
C) ||
D) !
Reason: && skips evaluating the right operand if the left operand is false.
Q7. Which logical operator means OR with short-circuit evaluation?
A) &&
B) ||
C) !
D) ^
Reason: || skips evaluating the right operand if the left operand is true.
Q8. What does !true evaluate to?
A) true
B) false
C) 1
D) null
Reason: The logical NOT operator reverses a boolean value.
Q9. Which operator increments a variable by one?
A) ++
B) --
C) **
D) //
Reason: ++ increments a numeric variable by one.
Q10. What is the result of 5 % 2?
A) 0
B) 1
C) 2
D) 2.5
Reason: Five divided by two leaves a remainder of one.
Q11. Which is the conditional ternary operator?
A) ?:
B) ::
C) ->
D) ??
Reason: The ternary conditional expression uses condition ? value1 : value2.
Q12. What is the result of (4 > 2) && (3 < 1)?
A) true
B) false
C) 4
D) Compile error
Reason: The first condition is true and the second false, so AND evaluates to false.
Q13. Which operator compares whether two references point to the same object?
A) ==
B) equals() always
C) <
D) %
Reason: For reference types, == compares reference identity, not general object content.
Q14. How should String contents commonly be compared?
A) Using == only
B) Using equals()
C) Using %
D) Using instanceof only
Reason: String.equals compares character content.
Q15. What does += do?
A) Adds the right value and assigns the result
B) Compares two values
C) Divides and discards
D) Negates a boolean
Reason: Compound assignment performs an operation and stores the result in the left variable.
Q16. What is the result of 3 + 4 * 2?
A) 14
B) 11
C) 10
D) 24
Reason: Multiplication has higher precedence than addition, so 3 + 8 = 11.
Q17. Which operator has higher precedence?
A) * over +
B) + over *
C) = over *
D) || over &&
Reason: Multiplication is evaluated before addition unless parentheses change the order.
Q18. What is the result of 10 - 3 - 2?
A) 9
B) 5
C) -5
D) 11
Reason: Subtraction is left-associative: (10 - 3) - 2 = 5.
Q19. What is the result of true || false && false?
A) false
B) true
C) Compile error
D) null
Reason: && has higher precedence than ||, so true || (false && false) is true.
Q20. Which operator is bitwise AND for integers?
A) &&
B) &
C) ||
D) !
Reason: & performs bitwise AND on integral operands and non-short-circuit boolean AND on booleans.
Q21. Which operator shifts bits to the left?
A) >>
B) <<
C) >>>
D) &&
Reason: << shifts the left operand's bits left.
Q22. What does >>> do for int values?
A) Unsigned right shift with zero-fill
B) Signed right shift
C) Left shift
D) Logical NOT
Reason: >>> shifts right and fills leftmost bits with zeros.
Q23. What does >> do for signed integers?
A) Arithmetic right shift, generally preserving the sign bit
B) Always zero-fill
C) Left shift
D) Modulo
Reason: >> copies the sign bit into the newly opened high-order positions.
Q24. Which operator checks if an object is of a compatible type?
A) instanceof
B) typeof
C) isType
D) ==
Reason: instanceof tests runtime type compatibility.
Q25. What is the result of 5 == 5.0?
A) true
B) false
C) Compile error always
D) null
Reason: Numeric binary promotion converts the int operand to double for comparison.
Q26. Which operator means not equal?
A) <>
B) !=
C) =!
D) !==
Reason: Java uses != for inequality.
Q27. Which operator is unary minus?
A) -
B) --
C) !=
D) %
Reason: Unary minus negates a numeric expression.
Q28. What is the value of x after int x=4; x++;?
A) 3
B) 4
C) 5
D) 6
Reason: Post-increment increases x by one after yielding its previous value in the expression.
Q29. What does ++x do as an expression?
A) Increments x and yields the new value
B) Yields old value then increments
C) Decrements x
D) Sets x to zero
Reason: Pre-increment increments first and then yields the updated value.
Q30. What is the result of 8 / 3.0?
A) 2
B) 2.0
C) Approximately 2.6667
D) Compile error
Reason: A floating-point operand causes floating-point division.
Q31. What does short-circuit mean?
A) The second operand may not be evaluated when the first decides the result
B) Both operands always run
C) The compiler stops
D) The result is always false
Reason: && and || may skip the right operand based on the left operand.
Q32. Which expression safely avoids evaluating 1 / 0 when x is zero?
A) x != 0 && 10 / x > 1
B) x == 0 && 10 / x > 1
C) 10 / x > 1 && x != 0
D) x = 0 || 10 / x > 1
Reason: With &&, a false first condition skips the division.
Q33. What is the result of "Java" + 17?
A) Java17
B) Java 17 automatically with a space
C) 17Java only
D) Compile error
Reason: String concatenation converts the other operand to its string representation.
Q34. What is the result of 1 + 2 + "A"?
A) 12A
B) 3A
C) A3
D) Compile error
Reason: Addition is evaluated left to right: 1 + 2 gives 3, then concatenates with A.
Q35. What is the result of "A" + 1 + 2?
A) A3
B) A12
C) 3A
D) Compile error
Reason: Once a String is involved, subsequent + operations concatenate left to right.
Q36. Which operator is used for bitwise XOR?
A) ^
B) &&
C) ||
D) !
Reason: ^ performs bitwise XOR on integral values.
Q37. Which operator has short-circuit behavior?
A) &&
B) &
C) ^
D) +
Reason: && short-circuits boolean evaluation.
Q38. What does x %= 3 mean?
A) x = x % 3
B) x = x / 3
C) x == 3
D) x = 3
Reason: Compound remainder assignment stores the remainder back in x.
Q39. What is the result of !(5 > 2)?
A) true
B) false
C) 5
D) Compile error
Reason: 5 > 2 is true; negating it gives false.
Q40. Which is a relational operator?
A) <=
B) +=
C) &&
D) %=
Reason: <= compares whether the left operand is less than or equal to the right.
Q41. Which operator is used to combine boolean conditions with OR without short-circuiting?
A) |
B) ||
C) !
D) +=
Reason: For booleans, | evaluates both operands and performs OR.
Q42. What is the result of 6 & 3 using bitwise AND?
A) 2
B) 7
C) 5
D) 1
Reason: Binary 110 AND 011 gives 010, which is decimal 2.
Q43. What is the result of 6 | 3 using bitwise OR?
A) 2
B) 7
C) 5
D) 1
Reason: Binary 110 OR 011 gives 111, which is decimal 7.
Q44. Which operator selects one of two expressions based on a condition?
A) ?:
B) ::
C) ->
D) %
Reason: The ternary operator chooses between two values based on a boolean condition.
Q45. What is the result of (int) 4.9?
A) 5
B) 4
C) 4.9
D) Compile error
Reason: Casting a double to int truncates the fractional part toward zero.
Q46. Which statement about operator precedence is correct?
A) Parentheses can make evaluation order explicit
B) All operators have equal precedence
C) Addition always happens first
D) Precedence changes randomly
Reason: Parentheses are useful for clarity and to control grouping.
Q47. What does x = y = 5 do when types are compatible?
A) Assigns 5 to y and then to x
B) Compares x and y
C) Adds x and y
D) Always causes an error
Reason: Assignment is right-associative, so y is assigned first and that value is assigned to x.
Q48. What can happen with integer overflow in Java?
A) The value wraps according to fixed-width integer arithmetic without an automatic exception
B) It always throws ArithmeticException
C) It converts to BigInteger automatically
D) It stops the JVM
Reason: Ordinary integer overflow wraps around; Java does not automatically throw for it.
Q49. What is the result of 9 % 4?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 2.25
D) 0
Reason: Nine divided by four leaves a remainder of one.
Q50. Which operator is used to access an object's member through a reference?
A) .
B) ::
C) ->
D) %
Reason: The dot operator accesses fields and methods through a reference.


4. Control Structures
Q1. Which statement selects between alternatives based on a condition?
A) if
B) import
C) package
D) class
Reason: if executes a block when its boolean condition is true.
Q2. Which keyword provides an alternative branch when an if condition is false?
A) otherwise
B) else
C) then
D) default
Reason: else provides the alternative branch.
Q3. Which statement is useful for selecting among many constant-like cases?
A) switch
B) while
C) continue
D) import
Reason: switch dispatches among cases based on a selector expression.
Q4. Which loop checks its condition before each iteration?
A) while
B) do-while only after body
C) None
D) constructor
Reason: A while loop checks its condition before running the body.
Q5. Which loop always executes its body at least once if entered?
A) while
B) for
C) do-while
D) enhanced for only
Reason: A do-while loop checks its condition after executing the body.
Q6. Which loop is often convenient when the number of iterations is known?
A) for
B) if
C) switch
D) try
Reason: A for loop commonly groups initialization, condition, and update.
Q7. Which keyword exits the nearest loop or switch?
A) skip
B) break
C) continue
D) return only
Reason: break terminates the nearest enclosing loop or switch.
Q8. Which keyword skips the rest of the current loop iteration?
A) break
B) continue
C) exit
D) stop
Reason: continue proceeds to the next iteration.
Q9. What is a nested if?
A) An if statement inside another control block
B) A loop with no condition
C) A class inside a package
D) A method return
Reason: Nested if statements allow decisions within decisions.
Q10. What is an infinite loop?
A) A loop whose condition never becomes false or that has no reachable exit
B) A loop that runs once
C) A loop with a break
D) A method with parameters
Reason: An infinite loop continues indefinitely unless externally interrupted or exited.
Q11. Which is a valid Java for loop?
A) for (int i=0; i<5; i++)
B) for int i=0; i<5; i++
C) for (i<5; i++)
D) loop (int i=0; i<5; i++)
Reason: Java for loops use parentheses and semicolon-separated initialization, condition, and update.
Q12. How many times does for (int i=0; i<3; i++) run its body?
A) 2
B) 3
C) 4
D) Infinite
Reason: The values 0, 1, and 2 satisfy i < 3.
Q13. What does while(false) do?
A) Runs the body once
B) Never runs the body
C) Runs twice
D) Does not compile in every context
Reason: The condition is false before the first iteration, so the body is skipped.
Q14. What is the result of int i=0; do { i++; } while(i<3);?
A) i becomes 2
B) i becomes 3
C) i remains 0
D) Infinite loop
Reason: The body increments i until it reaches 3.
Q15. Which switch feature allows several labels to share one branch?
A) Multiple case labels
B) Nested constructors
C) Multiple main methods
D) Array labels only
Reason: Several case labels can lead to the same statement group.
Q16. What is fall-through in a traditional switch statement?
A) Execution continues into following cases when no break or other transfer stops it
B) A compile error in all cases
C) The selector becomes null
D) The loop starts again
Reason: Traditional switch statements can continue into subsequent case labels.
Q17. Which newer switch form can return a value from an expression?
A) Switch expression
B) While expression
C) If declaration
D) Break loop
Reason: Switch expressions can produce a value using arrow rules or yield in block rules.
Q18. Which keyword returns a value from a method?
A) break
B) return
C) continue
D) yield only
Reason: return exits a method and may provide its result.
Q19. What is the effect of break in a nested loop?
A) It exits only the nearest loop unless labeled
B) It exits every method
C) It restarts the program
D) It skips one statement only
Reason: An unlabeled break targets the nearest enclosing breakable statement.
Q20. What does a labeled break allow?
A) Exit a labeled enclosing loop or block
B) Create a variable
C) Skip a method call
D) Return a value
Reason: A labeled break transfers control to the statement bearing that label.
Q21. What is the enhanced for loop used for?
A) Iterating over arrays or Iterable collections
B) Declaring a class
C) Handling exceptions only
D) Creating a module
Reason: The enhanced for loop visits elements of an array or Iterable.
Q22. Which loop may be best for reading every element of an array without needing its index?
A) Enhanced for
B) do-while only
C) switch
D) if
Reason: Enhanced for provides direct element iteration.
Q23. Which condition is required in an if statement?
A) A boolean expression
B) An integer only
C) A String only
D) A method declaration
Reason: Java if conditions must be boolean expressions.
Q24. Can Java use an int directly as an if condition?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only if final
D) Only in loops
Reason: Java does not treat integers as booleans.
Q25. What happens if an if statement has no braces and multiple following statements?
A) Only the next statement belongs to the if
B) All following statements belong to it
C) It always fails compilation
D) The condition is ignored
Reason: Without braces, only the immediately following statement is controlled by if.
Q26. Why are braces often recommended even for a single statement?
A) They reduce ambiguity and accidental logic errors
B) They make code always faster
C) They replace tests
D) They allow non-boolean conditions
Reason: Braces make block structure explicit and safer to edit.
Q27. Which operator is commonly used in loop conditions to compare values?
A) <
B) =
C) +=
D) ::
Reason: Relational operators such as < produce boolean conditions.
Q28. What is a sentinel-controlled loop?
A) A loop that stops when a special marker value is encountered
B) A loop that runs exactly ten times
C) A loop with no condition
D) A loop that uses only break
Reason: A sentinel is a value indicating that input or processing should stop.
Q29. What is off-by-one error?
A) A loop iterates one too many or one too few times
B) A syntax keyword
C) A memory area
D) A package conflict
Reason: Incorrect boundary conditions often cause off-by-one errors.
Q30. Which condition makes a loop execute while x is positive?
A) while (x > 0)
B) while (x = 0)
C) while (x < 0)
D) while (true == 0)
Reason: x > 0 is a boolean test for positive values.
Q31. What does continue do inside a for loop?
A) Moves to the update step and then checks the condition
B) Terminates the whole program
C) Exits every loop
D) Returns from the method
Reason: For a traditional for loop, continue proceeds to the update expression and then the condition.
Q32. What does continue do inside a while loop?
A) Starts the next condition check
B) Always exits the loop
C) Returns from the method
D) Runs the body twice
Reason: continue skips the remaining body and begins the next iteration check.
Q33. Can break be used inside a switch statement?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only in loops
D) Only in methods without return
Reason: break commonly exits a switch statement.
Q34. Which statement can replace a simple if-else value selection in an expression?
A) Ternary conditional expression
B) package
C) import
D) synchronized
Reason: The ?: operator selects one of two expressions based on a condition.
Q35. What is short-circuit evaluation useful for in conditions?
A) Avoiding evaluation of a right side when the result is already known
B) Forcing all expressions to run
C) Making every condition true
D) Skipping compilation
Reason: && and || can avoid unnecessary or unsafe right-side evaluation.
Q36. Which loop is post-tested?
A) do-while
B) while
C) for
D) enhanced for
Reason: A do-while condition is checked after the body.
Q37. What is the initial value of i in for (int i=1; i<=4; i++)?
A) 0
B) 1
C) 4
D) Undefined
Reason: The initialization expression assigns i = 1.
Q38. How many iterations occur for for (int i=1; i<=4; i++)?
A) 3
B) 4
C) 5
D) Infinite
Reason: The loop body runs for i values 1, 2, 3, and 4.
Q39. Which is a valid boolean condition?
A) score >= 50
B) score = 50
C) score + 50
D) score++
Reason: A relational comparison evaluates to a boolean.
Q40. What is the purpose of a default label in a traditional switch?
A) Handle selector values not matched by another case
B) Always execute first
C) Declare a variable
D) Exit a method
Reason: default provides a fallback branch.
Q41. Can a switch selector be a String in Java?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only in old Java
D) Only with a cast
Reason: Java supports String switch selectors.
Q42. What does yield do in a switch expression block?
A) Provides the value of that switch-expression branch
B) Starts a loop
C) Stops the JVM
D) Declares a field
Reason: yield supplies a result from a block arm of a switch expression.
Q43. Which is a common cause of an accidental infinite loop?
A) Failing to update the loop-control variable
B) Using braces
C) Using a boolean condition
D) Declaring a method
Reason: If the state controlling termination never changes appropriately, the loop may not end.
Q44. What is a guard clause?
A) An early condition that exits or returns to reduce nesting
B) A loop that never ends
C) A package name
D) A type conversion
Reason: Guard clauses handle exceptional or boundary cases early.
Q45. Which control structure repeats a block while a condition remains true?
A) Loop
B) Class
C) Package
D) Import
Reason: Loops repeat code based on a condition or iteration source.
Q46. What does return inside a loop do?
A) Exits the entire method, not just the loop
B) Only skips the current iteration
C) Restarts the loop
D) Exits only the nearest switch
Reason: return exits the current method.
Q47. Which structure is best for choosing one of two paths?
A) if-else
B) import
C) package
D) class
Reason: if-else provides two alternative paths.
Q48. Why should loop termination be checked carefully?
A) To avoid infinite loops and incorrect iteration counts
B) To make all variables global
C) To remove the need for algorithms
D) To ensure every loop is nested
Reason: Correct termination conditions are essential for correctness and performance.
Q49. Which loop is most appropriate when iterating over each element of a collection without needing an index?
A) Enhanced for
B) switch
C) if-else
D) try-catch
Reason: Enhanced for provides direct iteration over arrays and Iterable collections.
Q50. What does a missing break in a traditional switch case commonly allow?
A) Execution to continue into later case statements
B) The program to stop immediately
C) The switch to repeat automatically
D) Compilation to always fail
Reason: Without a break or other transfer, traditional switch execution may fall through.


5. Functions / Methods
Q1. What is a method in Java?
A) A named block of code that performs a task
B) A primitive data type
C) A package file
D) A loop condition
Reason: Methods organize behavior into reusable named units.
Q2. Which keyword indicates a method returns no value?
A) null
B) void
C) static
D) empty
Reason: void indicates that a method does not return a value.
Q3. What is a method parameter?
A) A variable declared in the method signature
B) The result of the method
C) A package name
D) A return keyword
Reason: Parameters define the inputs a method receives.
Q4. What is a method argument?
A) The value supplied when calling a method
B) The method's access modifier
C) A class constructor only
D) The method body
Reason: Arguments are actual values passed to parameters.
Q5. Which statement sends a value back from a non-void method?
A) return
B) break
C) continue
D) throw only
Reason: return provides the method result and exits the method.
Q6. What is method overloading?
A) Same name with different parameter lists
B) Same name and same signature in same class
C) A method calling itself only
D) A private field
Reason: Overloaded methods differ in their parameter lists.
Q7. Can methods be overloaded by changing only the return type?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only if static
D) Only in interfaces
Reason: Return type alone does not distinguish overloaded method signatures.
Q8. What is recursion?
A) A method calling itself directly or indirectly
B) A method with no parameters
C) A class importing itself
D) A variable changing type
Reason: Recursive methods solve problems through smaller calls to the same method.
Q9. What is a base case in recursion?
A) A condition that stops further recursive calls
B) The first parameter only
C) A return type
D) A package
Reason: The base case prevents recursion from continuing indefinitely.
Q10. What may happen if recursion has no reachable base case?
A) StackOverflowError
B) Automatic loop conversion
C) Syntax error always
D) The method returns zero
Reason: Unbounded recursive calls can exhaust the call stack.
Q11. Which modifier allows a method to be called on the class without an instance?
A) static
B) private only
C) final only
D) volatile
Reason: Static methods belong to the class.
Q12. What does public mean for a method?
A) It is broadly accessible subject to enclosing type/module access
B) Only the class can call it
C) Only the package can call it
D) It cannot be inherited
Reason: public is the broadest ordinary member access modifier.
Q13. What does private mean for a method?
A) It is accessible within its declaring class
B) It is accessible everywhere
C) It must be static
D) It is abstract
Reason: private restricts access to the declaring top-level class and its relevant nested context.
Q14. What is a method signature in Java mainly based on?
A) Method name and parameter types
B) Return type only
C) Access modifier only
D) Method body text
Reason: The signature used for overloading is the name plus parameter types, not return type.
Q15. What is a pure function commonly expected to do?
A) Return a result without observable side effects for the same inputs
B) Change global state every time
C) Always print output
D) Always use static
Reason: A pure function's result depends on its inputs and it has no observable side effects.
Q16. What is a side effect?
A) A change to state or interaction beyond simply returning a value
B) A return type
C) A parameter name
D) A class declaration
Reason: Examples include modifying fields, printing, or writing files.
Q17. Which is a valid method declaration?
A) int add(int a, int b) { return a+b; }
B) add int(a,b)
C) method add = int
D) int add = (a,b)
Reason: Java method declarations include a return type, name, parameter list, and body or semicolon.
Q18. What is a constructor's main purpose?
A) Initialize a newly created object
B) Return a primitive value
C) Run a loop only
D) Import a library
Reason: Constructors initialize object state at creation.
Q19. Does a constructor declare a return type?
A) Yes, always void
B) No
C) Only int
D) Only Object
Reason: Constructors have no declared return type, not even void.
Q20. What is constructor overloading?
A) Providing multiple constructors with different parameter lists
B) Overriding a constructor in a subclass
C) Returning two values
D) Making a constructor static
Reason: A class can declare multiple constructors with different parameter lists.
Q21. Which keyword calls another constructor in the same class?
A) this()
B) superclass()
C) self()
D) new()
Reason: this() invokes another constructor in the same class.
Q22. Which keyword calls a superclass constructor?
A) this()
B) super()
C) parent()
D) base()
Reason: super() invokes a superclass constructor.
Q23. Where must an explicit this() or super() constructor invocation appear in traditional Java syntax?
A) As the first constructor statement
B) At the end only
C) Anywhere
D) Only outside the constructor
Reason: Constructor chaining invocation must appear first in traditional Java versions/syntax.
Q24. What is a default argument in Java?
A) A parameter value automatically specified at the call site like in some languages
B) A built-in feature for omitting any method argument
C) The default field value
D) A constructor
Reason: Java does not support general default parameter values; overloads are commonly used instead.
Q25. What is pass-by-value in Java?
A) The method receives a copy of the argument value
B) The method always receives the original variable itself
C) Only primitives are passed by value
D) Objects are passed by reference in the parameter-binding sense
Reason: Java copies argument values; for objects, the copied value is a reference.
Q26. Can a method change the caller's primitive variable by assigning its parameter?
A) Yes, always
B) No, parameter is a copy of the primitive value
C) Only if static
D) Only if final
Reason: Changing the local parameter does not reassign the caller's primitive variable.
Q27. Can a method modify an object through a reference parameter?
A) Yes, if the object is mutable
B) No, never
C) Only if the parameter is static
D) Only for String
Reason: The copied reference can still refer to the same mutable object.
Q28. What is a varargs parameter?
A) A parameter that accepts a variable number of arguments
B) A parameter with no type
C) A method with no body
D) A constructor keyword
Reason: Varargs use ... and are treated as an array inside the method.
Q29. Which declaration uses varargs correctly?
A) void printAll(String... items)
B) void printAll(... String items)
C) void ...printAll(String items)
D) varargs printAll(String items)
Reason: The ellipsis follows the element type in the parameter declaration.
Q30. How many varargs parameters can a method have?
A) Any number
B) At most one, and it must be last
C) Exactly two
D) None
Reason: A method can have one varargs parameter and it must be the last parameter.
Q31. What is a recursive factorial base case often used?
A) n == 0 or n == 1
B) n < 1000 only
C) n++
D) n = n * n
Reason: Factorial definitions use 0! = 1 and 1! = 1 as base cases.
Q32. What is method overriding?
A) A subclass supplies an implementation for an inherited instance method
B) A method has different parameters in the same class
C) A method calls itself
D) A method returns void
Reason: Overriding changes inherited instance-method behavior in a subclass.
Q33. Which annotation marks an intended override?
A) @Override
B) @Overload
C) @Static
D) @InheritedMethod
Reason: @Override allows the compiler to verify the method really overrides an inherited method.
Q34. Can a static method be overridden polymorphically?
A) Yes, exactly like instance methods
B) No; static methods are hidden rather than overridden
C) Only if private
D) Only if abstract
Reason: Static methods are resolved based on the class/reference context, not dynamic instance dispatch.
Q35. What is a method's return type?
A) The type of value it returns, or void
B) The number of parameters
C) The access level
D) The package
Reason: The return type specifies the kind of value returned by a method.
Q36. What happens if a non-void method can finish without returning a value?
A) Compilation error in normal cases
B) It returns null automatically
C) It returns zero automatically
D) It always throws IOException
Reason: Java requires return paths to provide a value compatible with the declared return type.
Q37. Can a method return an object reference?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only constructors
D) Only static methods
Reason: Methods can return references to objects.
Q38. What is a local variable declared inside a method?
A) Visible only within its scope
B) Automatically public
C) Always static
D) A class field
Reason: Local variables are limited to their block or method scope.
Q39. What is method abstraction?
A) Exposing a method's purpose while hiding implementation details
B) Removing its name
C) Making every method private
D) Deleting parameters
Reason: Callers can use a method through its contract without knowing internal implementation.
Q40. What is cohesion in method design?
A) A method has one clear, focused responsibility
B) A method has as many statements as possible
C) A method uses only static fields
D) A method has no name
Reason: Focused methods are easier to understand, test, and reuse.
Q41. Why should methods often be kept reasonably small and focused?
A) They are easier to test, read, and maintain
B) They always run faster
C) They prevent every bug
D) They remove the need for comments
Reason: Focused methods reduce complexity and make behavior easier to verify.
Q42. What is an overloaded method call resolved using?
A) The compile-time argument types and applicable overload rules
B) Only the runtime object's class in all cases
C) Random selection
D) The return value
Reason: Overload resolution is primarily a compile-time process based on argument expressions and types.
Q43. What is the difference between overloading and overriding?
A) Overloading changes parameter lists; overriding replaces inherited instance behavior
B) They are identical
C) Overriding occurs only with different parameters
D) Overloading requires inheritance
Reason: Overloading is same-name methods with different parameter lists; overriding concerns inherited methods.
Q44. Can a method be declared both abstract and final?
A) Yes
B) No, because abstract requires implementation by subclasses but final prevents overriding
C) Only in an interface
D) Only if private
Reason: The modifiers conflict: a final method cannot be overridden, while an abstract method requires implementation.
Q45. What is a helper method?
A) A method used to perform a smaller supporting task
B) A constructor with no class
C) A package descriptor
D) A primitive variable
Reason: Helper methods break complex operations into manageable pieces.
Q46. What does static main allow in a conventional Java application?
A) The JVM can call it without first creating an instance of the class
B) It makes the whole class immutable
C) It prevents parameters
D) It runs on every object
Reason: The static entry point can be invoked at the class level.
Q47. Can a Java method return multiple independent values directly as separate return values?
A) Yes, by listing multiple return values
B) No; it returns one value, though that value can be an object/array/record holding multiple values
C) Only with void
D) Only with varargs
Reason: A method has one return value, but that value can encapsulate multiple pieces of data.
Q48. What is a method contract?
A) The method's expected inputs, behavior, result, and conditions
B) Its source file size
C) The number of lines only
D) The IDE theme
Reason: A clear contract states what callers can expect and what conditions apply.
Q49. What does early return often help with?
A) Handling guard conditions and reducing nesting
B) Making every method recursive
C) Changing a method's type
D) Creating packages
Reason: Returning early for invalid or special cases can simplify the main logic.
Q50. Which return type should a method use if it returns a true/false result?
A) boolean
B) void
C) String only
D) char
Reason: boolean is the type for true/false values.


6. Input / Output Handling
Q1. Which class is commonly used to read keyboard input simply in Java?
A) Scanner
B) Printer
C) ReaderOnly
D) InputClass
Reason: Scanner can parse tokens and lines from System.in.
Q2. Which package contains Scanner?
A) java.io
B) java.util
C) java.net
D) java.sql
Reason: Scanner is in java.util.
Q3. Which expression creates a Scanner for standard input?
A) new Scanner(System.in)
B) new Scanner(System.out)
C) Scanner(System.err)
D) System.in.Scanner()
Reason: System.in is the standard input stream.
Q4. Which Scanner method reads an int token?
A) nextInt()
B) nextLineInt()
C) readIntLine()
D) getInteger()
Reason: nextInt parses the next token as an integer.
Q5. Which Scanner method reads an entire line of text?
A) next()
B) nextLine()
C) nextChar()
D) read()
Reason: nextLine reads the remainder of the current line.
Q6. What does Scanner.next() normally read?
A) The next token up to whitespace
B) The entire file always
C) One byte only
D) A whole paragraph including all spaces
Reason: next reads a token separated by delimiters, commonly whitespace.
Q7. Which object represents standard output?
A) System.in
B) System.out
C) System.err only
D) Console.in
Reason: System.out is the standard output PrintStream.
Q8. Which method prints text and then ends the line?
A) print()
B) println()
C) printfOnly()
D) writeLine()
Reason: println prints the argument and a line terminator.
Q9. Which method supports formatted output?
A) printf()
B) nextLine()
C) read()
D) scan()
Reason: printf uses format specifiers to format output.
Q10. What does %d commonly represent in printf formatting?
A) Integer decimal value
B) String
C) Floating-point value
D) New line only
Reason: %d formats an integral decimal value.
Q11. What does %s commonly represent in printf formatting?
A) String/text representation
B) Integer only
C) Character only
D) Boolean only
Reason: %s formats a string representation.
Q12. What does %n represent in Java Formatter output?
A) Platform-specific line separator
B) Null value
C) An integer
D) A tab only
Reason: %n produces the platform-specific line separator.
Q13. Which stream is used for standard error output?
A) System.in
B) System.out
C) System.err
D) System.input
Reason: System.err is the standard error PrintStream.
Q14. Which class is commonly used to read text files efficiently line by line?
A) BufferedReader
B) PrintWriter only
C) Random
D) ScannerClass
Reason: BufferedReader provides buffered character input and readLine().
Q15. Which method reads one line from BufferedReader?
A) readLine()
B) nextLine()
C) readText()
D) getLine()
Reason: readLine returns the next line or null at end of stream.
Q16. Which checked exception is associated with many I/O operations?
A) IOException
B) ArithmeticException
C) NullPointerException
D) ClassCastException
Reason: IOException represents many input/output failures.
Q17. Which statement is used for automatic resource closing?
A) try-with-resources
B) if-else
C) switch
D) synchronized
Reason: try-with-resources closes resources implementing AutoCloseable.
Q18. Which interface is implemented by many closable I/O resources?
A) AutoCloseable
B) Runnable
C) Comparable
D) Serializable only
Reason: AutoCloseable supports deterministic resource closure.
Q19. What does end-of-file commonly mean for BufferedReader.readLine()?
A) It returns null
B) It returns zero
C) It throws NullPointerException always
D) It returns an empty string always
Reason: readLine returns null when no more lines remain.
Q20. Which class is useful for writing character text to a file?
A) BufferedWriter
B) Scanner
C) StringBuilder only
D) Thread
Reason: BufferedWriter writes text efficiently through a character stream.
Q21. Which method writes a line separator after text in BufferedWriter?
A) newLine()
B) println()
C) nextLine()
D) lineBreak()
Reason: BufferedWriter.newLine writes the platform line separator.
Q22. What is the purpose of flushing an output stream?
A) Push buffered output toward its destination
B) Delete output
C) Read keyboard input
D) Compile the file
Reason: flush asks buffered output to be written out to the underlying destination.
Q23. What is the difference between print and println?
A) println adds a line terminator; print does not
B) print always formats numbers
C) println only handles Strings
D) There is no difference
Reason: println ends the output line, while print leaves the cursor on the same line.
Q24. Which class can format text into a string using printf-style formatting?
A) String.format()
B) Scanner.format()
C) System.input()
D) File.formatterOnly()
Reason: String.format returns a formatted String.
Q25. Which escape sequence represents a newline in a Java string?
A) \n
B) \t
C) \r only
D) \b
Reason: \n is the newline escape sequence in Java strings.
Q26. Which escape sequence represents a tab?
A) \n
B) \t
C) \q
D) \v
Reason: \t represents a horizontal tab.
Q27. What is a file path?
A) A location identifying a file in a file system
B) A data type
C) A method result
D) A Java keyword
Reason: A path identifies where a file or directory is located.
Q28. Which modern API type is useful for representing a file path?
A) Path
B) ScannerPath
C) FileString
D) FileNameOnly
Reason: java.nio.file.Path represents a file-system path.
Q29. Which class provides static file operations such as copy and delete?
A) Files
B) System
C) Scanner
D) Collections
Reason: java.nio.file.Files provides operations on files and directories.
Q30. Which package contains Path and Files?
A) java.nio.file
B) java.io.nio
C) java.util.file
D) java.lang.io
Reason: Path and Files are in java.nio.file.
Q31. What is a relative path?
A) A path interpreted relative to a base/current directory
B) A path that always starts at the root
C) A file's contents
D) A Java package
Reason: Relative paths depend on a base path or working directory.
Q32. What is an absolute path?
A) A path identifying a location from the file-system root or equivalent base
B) A path that uses no folders
C) A variable name
D) A stream
Reason: An absolute path specifies a location independently of the current working directory.
Q33. What is serialization of data generally used for?
A) Storing or transmitting a representation of data
B) Printing only to screen
C) Starting a thread
D) Sorting arrays
Reason: Serialization encodes data or object state for storage or transfer.
Q34. Which class is commonly used to write primitive values in a binary format?
A) DataOutputStream
B) BufferedReader
C) Scanner
D) PrintWriter only
Reason: DataOutputStream writes primitive Java values to an underlying output stream.
Q35. Which class can read primitive values written by DataOutputStream?
A) DataInputStream
B) BufferedWriter
C) PrintStream only
D) FileReader
Reason: DataInputStream reads primitive values from a binary input stream.
Q36. What is buffering used for?
A) Reducing costly small I/O operations by grouping them
B) Encrypting every byte
C) Changing variable types
D) Replacing files
Reason: Buffers can improve I/O efficiency by reducing direct underlying operations.
Q37. Why should a file resource be closed?
A) To release resources and ensure pending output is handled
B) To compile Java code
C) To delete the file automatically
D) To reset all variables
Reason: Closing releases operating-system resources and may flush pending writes.
Q38. Which Scanner method can test whether another integer token is available?
A) hasNextInt()
B) isInt()
C) nextIntExists()
D) canReadInteger()
Reason: hasNextInt checks whether the next token can be parsed as an int.
Q39. What exception can Scanner.nextInt throw if the next token is not an integer?
A) InputMismatchException
B) IOException only
C) StackOverflowError
D) ClassCastException
Reason: InputMismatchException indicates the token does not match the requested type.
Q40. What common issue can occur after nextInt() followed by nextLine()?
A) nextLine may consume the remainder of the current line, often an empty remainder
B) nextLine always throws
C) The Scanner is automatically closed
D) The int becomes a String
Reason: nextInt leaves the line separator unread, so a following nextLine may consume it.
Q41. Which class is useful for reading all bytes from a small file in modern Java?
A) Files.readAllBytes()
B) Scanner.readBytes()
C) System.readFile()
D) Path.getBytes()
Reason: Files.readAllBytes(Path) reads file contents into a byte array, suitable for appropriately small files.
Q42. Which output method is best for displaying a simple value followed by a newline?
A) System.out.println(value)
B) System.in.println(value)
C) Scanner.println(value)
D) Path.print(value)
Reason: System.out.println writes to standard output and ends the line.
Q43. What does append mode generally do when writing a file?
A) Adds new content at the end rather than replacing existing content
B) Always deletes the file
C) Reads only
D) Compiles the file
Reason: Append mode preserves existing content and writes new data at the end.
Q44. What is a binary file stream used for?
A) Reading or writing bytes rather than character text
B) Only reading Java identifiers
C) Printing formatted decimals only
D) Handling loops
Reason: Byte streams process raw bytes and are appropriate for binary data.
Q45. What is a character stream designed for?
A) Text using character encoding
B) Only raw image bytes without decoding
C) CPU instructions only
D) Thread scheduling
Reason: Reader and Writer classes handle character data.
Q46. Why specify a character encoding when reading/writing text?
A) To interpret bytes consistently as characters
B) To increase variable scope
C) To disable exceptions
D) To make all files binary
Reason: Explicit encodings such as UTF-8 avoid platform-dependent text interpretation.
Q47. What does System.in represent?
A) Standard input stream
B) Standard output stream
C) Standard error stream
D) The JVM heap
Reason: System.in is typically connected to keyboard input or redirected input.
Q48. What is a common use of try-with-resources around a file reader?
A) Ensure the reader closes even if an exception occurs
B) Ensure the file is deleted
C) Prevent all exceptions
D) Make the file read-only
Reason: The resource is closed automatically when control leaves the try statement.
Q49. Which statement about IOException is correct?
A) It is a checked exception
B) It is a primitive type
C) It cannot have subclasses
D) It is always an Error
Reason: IOException is checked and typically must be caught or declared.
Q50. Which Java class writes formatted text to a file and offers print-style methods?
A) PrintWriter
B) BufferedReader
C) Scanner
D) Path
Reason: PrintWriter provides convenient print, println, and formatted-output methods.


7. Strings & Text Processing
Q1. Which class represents an immutable sequence of characters?
A) String
B) StringBuilder
C) char[] only
D) Scanner
Reason: String objects cannot be changed after creation.
Q2. Which method returns the number of UTF-16 code units in a String?
A) size()
B) length()
C) count()
D) capacity()
Reason: String.length returns the number of char code units.
Q3. Which method returns the character at a specified index?
A) charAt()
B) getChar()
C) character()
D) at()
Reason: charAt(index) returns the char at that index.
Q4. What is the first valid index of a non-empty String?
A) 1
B) 0
C) -1
D) Depends on length
Reason: Java strings use zero-based indexing.
Q5. What happens when charAt is called with an invalid index?
A) StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
B) NullPointerException always
C) It returns null
D) It wraps around
Reason: An invalid index is outside the string's valid range.
Q6. Which method compares String contents?
A) equals()
B) == only
C) compareAddress()
D) same()
Reason: String.equals compares character content.
Q7. What does == compare for two String references?
A) Whether they refer to the same object
B) Always their contents
C) Their lengths only
D) Their alphabetical order
Reason: For references, == checks identity rather than String content.
Q8. Which method compares strings lexicographically?
A) compareTo()
B) equalsIgnoreCase()
C) concatLength()
D) indexOfOnly()
Reason: compareTo returns an ordering comparison based on lexicographic order.
Q9. Which method compares strings ignoring case differences?
A) equalsIgnoreCase()
B) equalsCaseFree()
C) compareIgnore()
D) sameText()
Reason: equalsIgnoreCase compares text without considering case differences.
Q10. Which method converts a String to uppercase?
A) toUpperCase()
B) upper()
C) makeUpper()
D) capitalizeAll()
Reason: toUpperCase returns an uppercase version of the string.
Q11. Which method removes leading and trailing whitespace according to its rules?
A) trim()
B) stripMiddle()
C) removeAll()
D) cut()
Reason: trim removes leading and trailing characters up to U+0020; strip provides Unicode-aware whitespace handling in modern Java.
Q12. Which method searches for the first occurrence of a substring?
A) indexOf()
B) findFirstOnly()
C) searchAt()
D) containsIndex()
Reason: indexOf returns the first matching index or -1 if not found.
Q13. What does contains() return?
A) A boolean indicating whether a sequence occurs
B) The substring itself
C) The index always
D) A new array
Reason: contains checks whether the string includes the specified character sequence.
Q14. Which method extracts a substring from a String?
A) substring()
B) sliceText()
C) cutString()
D) sub()
Reason: substring returns a new string representing a selected range.
Q15. What is the end index behavior of substring(begin, end)?
A) End index is exclusive
B) End index is inclusive
C) Both indexes are inclusive
D) Indexes start at one
Reason: The substring includes beginIndex and excludes endIndex.
Q16. Which method replaces matching literal character sequences?
A) replace()
B) rewriteAllOnly()
C) substituteRegexOnly()
D) change()
Reason: replace can replace literal character or character-sequence occurrences.
Q17. Which method supports regular-expression replacement?
A) replaceAll()
B) replaceLiteralOnly()
C) subString()
D) concat()
Reason: replaceAll interprets its first argument as a regular expression.
Q18. What does split() do?
A) Splits a string around matches of a regular expression
B) Combines arrays
C) Converts text to uppercase
D) Counts bytes only
Reason: String.split uses a regex delimiter and returns an array of substrings.
Q19. Which class is mutable and designed for efficient string construction?
A) StringBuilder
B) String
C) Character
D) Scanner
Reason: StringBuilder modifies its character sequence without creating a new String for every append.
Q20. Which class is synchronized for many of its methods?
A) StringBuffer
B) StringBuilder
C) String
D) char
Reason: StringBuffer is synchronized; StringBuilder is generally preferred for single-threaded construction.
Q21. What does concatenation mean?
A) Joining strings together
B) Sorting characters
C) Converting text to int
D) Removing whitespace
Reason: Concatenation joins text sequences.
Q22. What is the result of "Java".length()?
A) 3
B) 4
C) 5
D) 0
Reason: The string contains four UTF-16 code units.
Q23. What is the result of "Java".charAt(1)?
A) J
B) a
C) v
D) A
Reason: Index 1 is the second character, a.
Q24. What does "hello".indexOf("l") return?
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) -1
Reason: The first l is at zero-based index 2.
Q25. What does "hello".contains("ell") return?
A) true
B) false
C) 2
D) null
Reason: The sequence ell occurs within hello.
Q26. What is the result of "Java".substring(1,3)?
A) Ja
B) av
C) ava
D) va
Reason: Indexes 1 and 2 are included; index 3 is excluded, yielding av.
Q27. Which method checks whether a string starts with a prefix?
A) startsWith()
B) begins()
C) prefixOf()
D) firstMatch()
Reason: startsWith tests the beginning of the string.
Q28. Which method checks whether a string ends with a suffix?
A) endsWith()
B) finish()
C) suffixOf()
D) lastMatch()
Reason: endsWith tests the end of the string.
Q29. What does isEmpty() check?
A) Whether length is zero
B) Whether string is null
C) Whether all characters are spaces
D) Whether string is uppercase
Reason: isEmpty returns true only when the sequence length is zero.
Q30. Does "   ".isEmpty() return true?
A) Yes
B) No
C) It throws
D) Only in Java 8
Reason: A string containing spaces has nonzero length.
Q31. Which method checks whether a string is empty or contains only whitespace in modern Java?
A) isBlank()
B) isEmpty() only
C) isSpace()
D) blankOnly()
Reason: isBlank, available since Java 11, checks empty or whitespace-only strings.
Q32. What is an escape sequence?
A) A backslash sequence representing a special character
B) A loop
C) A package
D) A method parameter
Reason: Escape sequences represent characters such as newline, tab, or quotation mark.
Q33. Which escape sequence represents a double quote inside a string literal?
A) \"
B) \'
C) \\n
D) \t
Reason: The escaped double quote allows a quote character within a double-quoted literal.
Q34. What does String.format() provide?
A) Formatted string creation
B) Thread scheduling
C) Regex compilation only
D) File deletion
Reason: String.format creates a formatted String using format specifiers.
Q35. Which package contains Pattern and Matcher?
A) java.util.regex
B) java.lang.text
C) java.regex.util
D) java.io.regex
Reason: Regular-expression APIs are in java.util.regex.
Q36. What is a regular expression?
A) A pattern used to match text
B) A Java primitive
C) A memory address
D) A file extension
Reason: Regex patterns describe text matching rules.
Q37. In regex, what does \d usually match?
A) A digit
B) Any letter
C) A whitespace only
D) A comma only
Reason: In Java regex, \d represents a digit class; in a Java string literal, the backslash is escaped as "\\d".
Q38. In regex, what does + mean?
A) One or more repetitions of the preceding element
B) Zero repetitions only
C) Any character always
D) End of input
Reason: The plus quantifier matches one or more occurrences.
Q39. In regex, what does * mean?
A) Zero or more repetitions of the preceding element
B) Exactly one occurrence
C) Start of input
D) Only whitespace
Reason: The star quantifier matches zero or more occurrences.
Q40. What does ^ commonly mean in a regex outside a character class?
A) Beginning of input/line, depending on mode
B) End only
C) Any digit
D) One or more
Reason: Caret anchors a match at the beginning in the usual regex context.
Q41. What does $ commonly mean in a regex?
A) End of input/line, depending on mode
B) Beginning only
C) Any character
D) A digit
Reason: Dollar is an end anchor in the usual regex context.
Q42. Which method checks whether the entire input matches a regex?
A) matches()
B) find()
C) lookingAtOnly()
D) containsRegex()
Reason: Matcher.matches requires the whole region/input to match.
Q43. Which Matcher method searches for the next matching subsequence?
A) find()
B) matches()
C) equals()
D) split()
Reason: find searches for a matching subsequence.
Q44. Why is String immutable?
A) Its contents cannot change after creation, aiding safe sharing and stable behavior
B) It never uses memory
C) It is a primitive
D) It can contain only letters
Reason: Immutability supports safe sharing, caching, and predictable behavior.
Q45. What is the String pool?
A) A JVM-managed pool of interned string instances
B) A thread pool
C) A database
D) A regex group
Reason: String literals and interned strings can share pooled instances.
Q46. What does String.intern() do?
A) Returns the canonical pooled representation for the string
B) Converts it to lowercase
C) Deletes the original
D) Splits the string
Reason: intern returns the canonical string from the string pool, adding it if necessary.
Q47. Which is usually more efficient for repeated concatenation in a loop?
A) StringBuilder
B) Repeated String + in every iteration always
C) Scanner
D) Character
Reason: StringBuilder avoids repeatedly creating intermediate immutable strings in many concatenation patterns.
Q48. What is Unicode code point processing relevant to?
A) Characters beyond a single UTF-16 char unit
B) Only ASCII digits
C) Variable scope
D) Method overloading
Reason: Some Unicode characters use surrogate pairs and require code-point-aware processing.
Q49. What does toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) help with?
A) Locale-independent case conversion
B) Removing all punctuation
C) Counting bytes
D) Compiling regex
Reason: Locale.ROOT avoids language-specific casing effects when a locale-neutral transformation is desired.
Q50. Which method checks whether a String contains a given character sequence?
A) contains()
B) hasText()
C) matchAt()
D) includesOnly()
Reason: contains returns true when the specified character sequence occurs in the string.


8. Arrays & Collections
Q1. What is an array in Java?
A) An object holding a fixed-length sequence of elements of one component type
B) A resizable collection
C) A primitive type
D) A method
Reason: Arrays have a fixed length after creation.
Q2. What is the first index of a Java array?
A) 1
B) 0
C) -1
D) Depends on type
Reason: Java arrays are zero-indexed.
Q3. How do you get an array's length?
A) array.length()
B) array.size()
C) array.length
D) length(array)
Reason: Arrays expose length as a field, not a method.
Q4. What is the default value of an int array element?
A) null
B) 0
C) 1
D) Undefined
Reason: New int arrays initialize elements to zero.
Q5. What is the default value of a boolean array element?
A) true
B) false
C) null
D) 1
Reason: New boolean arrays initialize elements to false.
Q6. Which declaration creates an int array with five elements?
A) int[] a = new int[5];
B) int a = new int[5];
C) array<int> a = 5;
D) int[5] a;
Reason: new int[5] creates an int array with length five.
Q7. Which index is valid for an array of length 5?
A) 5
B) -1
C) 4
D) 6
Reason: Valid indexes run from 0 through length - 1.
Q8. What happens when accessing an invalid array index?
A) ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
B) The index wraps around
C) It returns zero always
D) Compile error always
Reason: Runtime bounds checks reject invalid array indexes.
Q9. Can an array's length change after creation?
A) Yes, directly
B) No
C) Only if final
D) Only for String arrays
Reason: Array length is fixed; a different array must be created to change capacity.
Q10. Which utility class contains sort methods for arrays?
A) Arrays
B) Collections only
C) ArrayList
D) SystemArray
Reason: java.util.Arrays provides methods such as sort and binarySearch.
Q11. Which method copies an array range into a new array?
A) Arrays.copyOfRange()
B) ArrayList.copyRange()
C) System.newArray()
D) copyRangeOnly()
Reason: Arrays.copyOfRange creates a new array containing a specified range.
Q12. Which collection interface represents an ordered sequence that can contain duplicates?
A) List
B) Set
C) Map
D) Queue only
Reason: List maintains an ordered sequence and permits duplicates.
Q13. Which collection interface disallows duplicate elements by its contract?
A) List
B) Set
C) Map
D) Array
Reason: Set models a collection of distinct elements.
Q14. Which interface stores key-value mappings?
A) Map
B) List
C) Set
D) Iterable only
Reason: Map associates keys with values.
Q15. Which implementation is a resizable array-based List?
A) ArrayList
B) HashSet
C) HashMap
D) TreeMap
Reason: ArrayList implements List using a resizable array.
Q16. Which implementation commonly provides hash-based unique elements?
A) HashSet
B) ArrayList
C) LinkedList only
D) StringBuilder
Reason: HashSet uses hashing to implement Set semantics.
Q17. Which implementation is a hash-based key-value map?
A) HashMap
B) HashSet
C) ArrayDeque
D) TreeSet
Reason: HashMap stores key-value mappings using hashing.
Q18. Can a List contain duplicate values?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only integers
D) Only if sorted
Reason: List permits duplicates.
Q19. Can a Set contain duplicate elements according to its contract?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only strings
D) Only null
Reason: Set does not contain duplicate elements.
Q20. Which method adds an element to an ArrayList?
A) add()
B) insertOnly()
C) appendArray()
D) pushBackOnly()
Reason: List implementations such as ArrayList provide add.
Q21. Which method returns the number of elements in a collection?
A) length
B) size()
C) count()
D) capacity()
Reason: Collection implementations provide size().
Q22. How is the number of elements in an array accessed?
A) size()
B) length
C) count
D) getSize()
Reason: An array has a length field.
Q23. Which interface is the root of the Java collections hierarchy for groups of elements?
A) Collection
B) Collections
C) Map
D) Arrays
Reason: Collection is the main interface for groups of elements; Map is a separate hierarchy.
Q24. What is the role of the Collections utility class?
A) Provides static algorithms and utilities for collections
B) Represents one collection instance
C) Creates primitive arrays only
D) Replaces the Collection interface
Reason: java.util.Collections offers utilities such as sorting, reversing, and unmodifiable wrappers.
Q25. Which method sorts a List in ascending natural order?
A) Collections.sort(list)
B) list.orderNow()
C) Arrays.sort(list) always
D) list.sortAscendingOnly()
Reason: Collections.sort sorts a list according to natural order or a supplied comparator.
Q26. Which collection maintains elements in sorted order by natural ordering by default?
A) TreeSet
B) HashSet
C) ArrayList
D) ArrayDeque
Reason: TreeSet stores unique elements in sorted order.
Q27. Which map implementation maintains keys in sorted order by default?
A) TreeMap
B) HashMap
C) IdentityHashMap
D) Hashtable only
Reason: TreeMap orders keys according to natural ordering or a comparator.
Q28. What is the typical average lookup complexity of HashMap with good hash distribution?
A) O(1)
B) O(n²)
C) O(log log n) always
D) O(n!)
Reason: Hash-based lookup is typically constant-time on average, though worst cases can differ.
Q29. What is the typical time complexity of accessing an array element by index?
A) O(1)
B) O(n)
C) O(log n)
D) O(n²)
Reason: Array indexing directly computes the element location.
Q30. What is the typical time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
A) O(n)
B) O(log n)
C) O(n²)
D) O(1) always
Reason: Binary search halves the search interval at each step.
Q31. Does binary search require sorted data?
A) Yes, for its normal correctness guarantee
B) No
C) Only for strings
D) Only for arrays of length one
Reason: Binary search relies on sorted order to discard half of the remaining range.
Q32. Which loop is commonly used to iterate through array elements by index?
A) for (int i=0; i<a.length; i++)
B) for (int i=1; i<=a.length; i++) always
C) if (a)
D) switch (a.length)
Reason: The index range starts at zero and ends before a.length.
Q33. What is a multidimensional array in Java?
A) An array whose elements can themselves be arrays
B) A single primitive value
C) A Map only
D) A collection that must be rectangular
Reason: Java multidimensional arrays are arrays of arrays and can be jagged.
Q34. Can Java's two-dimensional arrays have rows of different lengths?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only for int
D) Only if static
Reason: A two-dimensional Java array is an array of row arrays, so row lengths can differ.
Q35. Which syntax accesses row 1, column 2 in int[][] a?
A) a[1][2]
B) a(1,2)
C) a[1,2]
D) a{1}{2}
Reason: Java uses one bracket pair for each array dimension.
Q36. Which method can compare two arrays' contents?
A) Arrays.equals(a, b)
B) a == b only
C) a.same(b)
D) Collections.equals(a,b)
Reason: Arrays.equals compares corresponding elements for supported array types.
Q37. What does array == array2 test?
A) Whether the references point to the same array object
B) Whether all elements are equal
C) Whether lengths match only
D) Whether arrays are sorted
Reason: == compares array reference identity, not element-by-element content.
Q38. Which interface allows an object to be used in an enhanced for loop when implemented appropriately?
A) Iterable
B) Runnable
C) Serializable
D) AutoCloseable
Reason: Iterable supplies an iterator and enables enhanced-for iteration.
Q39. Which interface represents an object that can produce an iterator?
A) Iterable
B) Iterator only
C) Comparable
D) Comparator
Reason: Iterable has iterator(), while Iterator performs traversal.
Q40. Which method advances an Iterator to the next element?
A) next()
B) advance()
C) getNext()
D) move()
Reason: Iterator.next returns the next element.
Q41. Which method checks whether an Iterator has another element?
A) hasNext()
