B) nextExists()
C) more()
D) isAvailable()
Reason: hasNext returns true when another element is available.
Q42. What can happen if a list is structurally modified during a fail-fast iteration outside the iterator's supported methods?
A) ConcurrentModificationException may occur
B) The list always sorts itself
C) The JVM always deadlocks
D) It always compiles incorrectly
Reason: Fail-fast iterators may detect unsupported structural modification and throw ConcurrentModificationException.
Q43. Which collection is designed for first-in, first-out queue behavior?
A) Queue
B) Set
C) Map
D) String
Reason: Queue represents elements held prior to processing, often in FIFO order.
Q44. Which class can implement a stack/deque using a resizable array?
A) ArrayDeque
B) HashMap
C) TreeSet
D) Scanner
Reason: ArrayDeque supports deque operations and is often useful for stack/queue behavior.
Q45. What is a generic collection such as List<String> useful for?
A) Type-safe storage of String elements
B) Storing only primitive values directly
C) Changing types at runtime
D) Avoiding all memory allocation
Reason: Generics catch many type mismatches at compile time.
Q46. Can a Java generic type argument be a primitive such as int?
A) Yes, List<int> is valid
B) No; use wrapper types such as Integer
C) Only in arrays
D) Only in maps
Reason: Generic type arguments must be reference types, so List<Integer> is used.
Q47. What is autoboxing useful for in collections?
A) Automatically converting primitive values to wrapper objects
B) Making lists fixed-length
C) Sorting all data
D) Avoiding type checking
Reason: Collections store objects, and autoboxing converts values such as int to Integer.
Q48. What is the difference between ArrayList and array?
A) ArrayList can resize; an array has fixed length
B) An array can resize but ArrayList cannot
C) They are identical
D) ArrayList stores only primitives
Reason: ArrayList manages a resizable backing array, whereas array length is fixed.
Q49. Which is a safe general practice when removing items during iteration?
A) Use the iterator's remove method when supported
B) Always modify the list directly in a for-each loop
C) Call System.gc()
D) Use array.length()
Reason: Iterator.remove is the supported way to remove the current element during iteration for iterators that implement it.
Q50. Which collection is designed to store key-value pairs?
A) Map
B) List
C) Set
D) Deque
Reason: Map associates each key with a value.



9. Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)
Q1. Which concept bundles data and methods into a single unit?
A) Inheritance
B) Encapsulation
C) Compilation
D) Iteration
Reason: Encapsulation groups data and methods in a class and controls access to the data.
Q2. Which Java keyword is used to inherit a class?
A) implements
B) extends
C) inherits
D) super
Reason: A class uses extends to inherit from another class.
Q3. Which keyword creates an object in Java?
A) class
B) this
C) new
D) void
Reason: The new operator creates an object and allocates memory for it.
Q4. What is a blueprint for objects called?
A) Method
B) Class
C) Package
D) Interface
Reason: A class defines the fields and methods that its objects can have.
Q5. Which OOP concept allows one interface to represent different implementations?
A) Polymorphism
B) Compilation
C) Casting
D) Garbage collection
Reason: Polymorphism allows the same operation or reference type to work with different object types.
Q6. Which method has the same name as its class and no return type?
A) Static method
B) Constructor
C) Finalizer
D) Abstract method
Reason: A constructor has the class name and does not declare a return type.
Q7. Which keyword refers to the current object?
A) super
B) this
C) self
D) current
Reason: this refers to the current object instance.
Q8. Which keyword refers to a superclass member or constructor?
A) parent
B) base
C) super
D) extends
Reason: super is used to access superclass members or invoke its constructor.
Q9. Can a Java class directly extend more than one class?
A) Yes, always
B) No
C) Only if abstract
D) Only if final
Reason: Java classes support single inheritance; multiple type inheritance can be achieved with interfaces.
Q10. Which access modifier gives access only within the declaring class?
A) public
B) protected
C) private
D) default
Reason: private members are accessible only within their declaring class.
Q11. What is method overloading?
A) Same method name with different parameter lists
B) Same signature in unrelated classes
C) Changing a variable type
D) Creating many objects
Reason: Overloading uses the same method name with different parameter lists.
Q12. Method overriding is primarily associated with which feature?
A) Inheritance
B) Packages
C) Arrays
D) Garbage collection
Reason: A subclass can provide its own implementation of an inherited instance method.
Q13. Which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed?
A) static
B) const
C) final
D) private
Reason: A final class cannot be extended.
Q14. Which keyword declares a class that may contain abstract methods?
A) abstract
B) virtual
C) interface
D) native
Reason: An abstract class is declared with abstract and cannot be instantiated directly.
Q15. Can an abstract class have a constructor?
A) No
B) Yes
C) Only if final
D) Only if it has no fields
Reason: An abstract class can have constructors to initialize its state when subclass instances are created.
Q16. Which keyword declares an interface implementation?
A) extends
B) implements
C) interface
D) instanceof
Reason: A class uses implements to implement an interface.
Q17. Which operator checks whether an object is an instance of a type?
A) typeof
B) instanceof
C) is
D) check
Reason: instanceof tests whether a reference refers to an instance of a compatible type.
Q18. What is a default constructor?
A) A constructor with no parameters supplied by the compiler when none is declared
B) A private method
C) A constructor that returns an object
D) A static constructor
Reason: The compiler supplies a no-argument default constructor only if the class declares no constructor.
Q19. Which statement about constructors is correct?
A) They have a return type
B) They can be inherited
C) They initialize new objects
D) They must be static
Reason: Constructors initialize an object when it is created.
Q20. Which relationship is commonly described as 'is-a'?
A) Composition
B) Inheritance
C) Association only
D) Aggregation
Reason: Inheritance often models an is-a relationship, such as Dog is an Animal.
Q21. Which relationship is commonly described as 'has-a'?
A) Inheritance
B) Composition/aggregation
C) Overloading
D) Casting
Reason: Composition or aggregation models an object containing or using another object.
Q22. What is dynamic method dispatch?
A) Choosing an overridden instance method at runtime
B) Choosing a variable at compile time
C) Loading a package
D) Freeing memory manually
Reason: The actual object type determines which overridden instance method runs at runtime.
Q23. Which methods can be overloaded?
A) Only constructors
B) Only private methods
C) Methods with the same name and different parameter lists
D) No Java methods
Reason: Java permits overloading when parameter lists differ.
Q24. Which is not a primitive Java type?
A) int
B) boolean
C) String
D) double
Reason: String is a reference type, not a primitive type.
Q25. What does private help achieve?
A) Encapsulation
B) Multiple inheritance
C) Parallel execution
D) Compilation
Reason: Restricting direct access helps protect an object's internal state.
Q26. Can static methods be overridden in the polymorphic sense?
A) Yes, exactly like instance methods
B) No; they are hidden, not overridden
C) Only in interfaces
D) Only when private
Reason: Static method selection is based on the reference/class context, not runtime overriding.
Q27. Which member belongs to the class rather than each instance?
A) Instance field
B) Local variable
C) static field
D) Constructor parameter
Reason: A static field is shared at the class level.
Q28. What is an object?
A) An instance of a class
B) A package
C) A compiler error
D) A primitive type only
Reason: An object is a runtime instance created from a class.
Q29. Which principle exposes essential features while hiding implementation details?
A) Abstraction
B) Iteration
C) Casting
D) Serialization
Reason: Abstraction focuses on what an object does while hiding unnecessary implementation details.
Q30. Can an interface contain default methods in modern Java?
A) No
B) Yes
C) Only constructors
D) Only fields that are mutable
Reason: Interfaces can define default methods with implementations.
Q31. Which declaration is valid for a class named Car?
A) Car() {}
B) void Car() {}
C) constructor Car() {}
D) new Car {}
Reason: A constructor uses the class name and has no return type.
Q32. What does the this() call do inside a constructor?
A) Calls another constructor in the same class
B) Calls the superclass method
C) Creates a package
D) Destroys the object
Reason: this() invokes another constructor in the same class and must be the first statement.
Q33. What does super() do in a constructor?
A) Calls a superclass constructor
B) Calls a static method
C) Creates an interface
D) Returns the object
Reason: super() invokes a superclass constructor and must appear first when explicitly used.
Q34. Which class is the root of Java's class hierarchy?
A) System
B) Object
C) ClassLoader
D) String
Reason: java.lang.Object is the root superclass of classes that do not explicitly extend another class.
Q35. Which keyword can be used to test a reference before a cast?
A) instanceof
B) extends
C) throws
D) package
Reason: instanceof can check type compatibility before a downcast.
Q36. What is composition?
A) A strong has-a relationship where one object owns another component
B) A constructor overload
C) A type of loop
D) A compiler phase
Reason: Composition models a whole-part relationship with ownership of component objects.
Q37. Which access level applies when no access modifier is specified?
A) public
B) private
C) package-private
D) protected only
Reason: No modifier gives package-private access.
Q38. Can a final method be overridden?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only by interfaces
D) Only if static
Reason: A final method cannot be overridden by subclasses.
Q39. What is an abstract method?
A) A method with no implementation in its declaration
B) A private constructor
C) A method that is always static
D) A method that cannot be called
Reason: An abstract method declares behavior that a concrete subclass must implement.
Q40. Which is true about an interface reference?
A) It can refer to an implementing class object
B) It can only refer to interface objects
C) It cannot be a variable
D) It must be static
Reason: An interface reference can hold an object whose class implements that interface.
Q41. What does cohesion describe in class design?
A) How closely related a class's responsibilities are
B) The number of Java keywords
C) Memory size of an object
D) The number of packages
Reason: High cohesion means a class has a focused, closely related responsibility.
Q42. What does coupling describe?
A) Dependency between components
B) A method's return value
C) Object size only
D) Constructor syntax
Reason: Coupling describes how strongly components depend on one another; lower coupling is usually preferred.
Q43. Which principle recommends keeping fields private and exposing controlled methods?
A) Encapsulation
B) Recursion
C) Parallelism
D) Tokenization
Reason: Private fields with controlled methods protect invariants and implementation details.
Q44. Which is a valid polymorphic assignment?
A) Animal a = new Dog();
B) Dog d = new Animal();
C) int x = new String();
D) Car c = new int();
Reason: A superclass reference can refer to a subclass object.
Q45. Which method signature is required for Java program entry in a conventional application?
A) public void main()
B) public static void main(String[] args)
C) static int start(String args)
D) private main(String[] args)
Reason: The conventional entry point is public static void main(String[] args).
Q46. Can constructors be declared abstract?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only in interfaces
D) Only if public
Reason: Constructors cannot be abstract because they must initialize an object.
Q47. Which keyword allows a class to inherit an interface's type?
A) implements
B) extends
C) throws
D) import
Reason: A class implements an interface; an interface can extend other interfaces.
Q48. What is a nested class?
A) A class declared inside another class
B) A class with no methods
C) A final object
D) A package alias
Reason: A nested class is declared within the body of another class.
Q49. Which OOP feature supports code reuse through an existing class?
A) Inheritance
B) Syntax highlighting
C) Exception printing
D) Looping
Reason: Inheritance allows a subclass to reuse accessible behavior from a superclass.
Q50. What is the main purpose of an interface?
A) Define a contract of behavior
B) Allocate arrays only
C) Catch exceptions
D) Run threads
Reason: An interface specifies methods/types that implementing classes agree to provide.


10. Memory Management Concepts
Q1. Which area stores objects created with new?
A) Java heap
B) Java stack only
C) CPU register only
D) Source file
Reason: Objects and arrays are allocated on the heap.
Q2. Where are local variables and method call frames generally stored?
A) Heap
B) Java stack
C) Method area only
D) Disk cache
Reason: Each thread has a stack containing method frames and local execution state.
Q3. What is garbage collection?
A) Automatic reclamation of memory occupied by unreachable objects
B) Manual compilation
C) Sorting objects
D) Encrypting memory
Reason: The JVM can reclaim heap memory from objects that are no longer reachable.
Q4. Which keyword creates an object?
A) alloc
B) new
C) malloc
D) create
Reason: Java uses new to create objects and arrays.
Q5. When is an object eligible for garbage collection?
A) When it is unreachable from GC roots
B) Immediately after construction
C) Whenever a field is private
D) When it is printed
Reason: Unreachable objects may be reclaimed by the garbage collector.
Q6. Which method was historically associated with requesting garbage collection?
A) System.gc()
B) Object.collect()
C) Runtime.delete()
D) Memory.free()
Reason: System.gc() requests collection but does not guarantee that it will run.
Q7. Does System.gc() guarantee immediate collection?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only on Windows
D) Only for strings
Reason: The JVM may ignore or delay the request.
Q8. What is a memory leak in Java commonly caused by?
A) Unneeded objects remaining reachable
B) The garbage collector running
C) Using int variables
D) Closing a file
Reason: References retained unintentionally prevent otherwise unneeded objects from being collected.
Q9. Which memory area stores class metadata and runtime constant-pool information conceptually?
A) Heap only
B) Method area
C) Each thread's stack
D) Native stack only
Reason: The JVM specification defines a method area for per-class structures and runtime constant pools.
Q10. What is a StackOverflowError commonly caused by?
A) Excessive nested calls, often infinite recursion
B) Too many comments
C) A missing semicolon only
D) A small integer
Reason: Deep recursion can exhaust the thread's stack.
Q11. What does OutOfMemoryError indicate?
A) The JVM cannot allocate required memory under its constraints
B) A syntax error
C) A wrong package name
D) An unused import
Reason: The JVM throws this error when it cannot satisfy a memory allocation request.
Q12. Are primitive local variables always stored on the heap?
A) Yes
B) No; local variables are associated with stack frames, though implementation details vary
C) Only in loops
D) Only when final
Reason: Local variables belong to method frames conceptually; JVM optimizations can vary physical placement.
Q13. Where can an object's instance fields reside?
A) As part of the object on the heap
B) Always in the stack frame
C) In the source file
D) Only in CPU cache
Reason: Instance fields are part of the object's state, and objects are generally heap allocated.
Q14. What is a reference variable?
A) A variable that can refer to an object or be null
B) An object itself in all cases
C) A primitive integer only
D) A class file
Reason: Reference variables hold references to objects rather than the object's full instance data.
Q15. What does null represent for a reference?
A) No object reference
B) An empty string
C) Zero-length array
D) A deleted class
Reason: null indicates that the reference does not currently refer to an object.
Q16. Which can cause a NullPointerException?
A) Calling an instance method through null
B) Declaring an int
C) Using a comment
D) Importing java.lang
Reason: Dereferencing null for an instance operation causes NullPointerException.
Q17. Are Java objects explicitly freed using delete?
A) Yes
B) No; memory is managed by garbage collection
C) Only strings are deleted
D) Only arrays
Reason: Java does not provide a general delete operator for objects.
Q18. What is a strong reference?
A) An ordinary reference that generally keeps its object reachable
B) A reference that always points to null
C) A primitive type
D) A thread
Reason: Objects reachable through strong references are not eligible for collection.
Q19. Which package contains reference types such as WeakReference?
A) java.lang.ref
B) java.io
C) java.net
D) java.sql
Reason: Reference-related classes such as WeakReference are in java.lang.ref.
Q20. What is the purpose of a weak reference?
A) Allow an object to be collected when only weakly reachable
B) Prevent all collection
C) Replace every strong reference
D) Allocate stack frames
Reason: Weakly reachable objects can be reclaimed by the garbage collector.
Q21. What is heap memory mainly used for?
A) Objects and arrays
B) Only method parameters
C) Only bytecode instructions
D) Only thread names
Reason: The heap is the runtime area from which memory for objects and arrays is allocated.
Q22. What is the stack typically organized around?
A) Method calls and frames
B) All objects globally
C) Only class files
D) Database tables
Reason: A stack frame is created for a method invocation and removed when it completes.
Q23. What happens to a normal stack frame when a method returns?
A) It is popped from that thread's stack
B) It becomes a class
C) It remains forever
D) It is sent to the heap
Reason: Returning from a method removes its frame from the call stack.
Q24. Can two references point to the same object?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only for strings
D) Only across packages
Reason: Multiple variables may refer to the same object instance.
Q25. What is aliasing?
A) Multiple references referring to the same object
B) A method without a name
C) A memory error only
D) A type of loop
Reason: Aliasing occurs when different references designate the same object.
Q26. Which object is eligible for collection after this code runs: String s = new String("Hi"); s = null;?
A) The object formerly referenced by s, if no other references exist
B) All strings in the JVM
C) The variable s itself is collected as an object
D) No object can be collected
Reason: Setting s to null removes that reference; the object is eligible if nothing else reaches it.
Q27. What is the main role of the garbage collector?
A) Reclaim memory from eligible objects
B) Fix syntax errors
C) Compile Java source
D) Schedule every thread
Reason: GC manages reclamation of unreachable heap objects.
Q28. Can a programmer reliably predict the exact time an object will be collected?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only with System.gc()
D) Only in a loop
Reason: Garbage collection timing is JVM-controlled and not guaranteed.
Q29. What is a finalize() method historically associated with?
A) A deprecated/obsolete cleanup mechanism before collection
B) Creating threads
C) Declaring constructors
D) Handling imports
Reason: finalization is deprecated for removal and should not be relied on for resource management.
Q30. What should generally be used to close files and similar resources?
A) try-with-resources
B) System.gc()
C) finalize()
D) null assignment only
Reason: try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable resources deterministically.
Q31. What is an object graph?
A) Objects connected through references
B) A graph of source-code lines only
C) A stack trace
D) A compiler symbol table
Reason: An object graph represents objects and the references connecting them.
Q32. What are GC roots?
A) Starting references used to determine reachability
B) All unreachable objects
C) Only constructors
D) Memory addresses in comments
Reason: GC roots include runtime references such as active thread stacks and class-related references.
Q33. What is an array in Java?
A) An object that stores a fixed number of elements of one component type
B) A primitive type
C) A method frame
D) A package
Reason: Arrays are objects with a fixed length and typed elements.
Q34. Can an array become eligible for garbage collection?
A) Yes, when it is unreachable
B) No, never
C) Only if it is empty
D) Only if it contains objects
Reason: Arrays are objects and can be collected when unreachable.
Q35. What does memory allocation mean?
A) Reserving memory for data or objects
B) Printing output
C) Handling exceptions
D) Naming a package
Reason: Allocation provides storage for values or objects.
Q36. What does memory deallocation mean in Java's managed heap?
A) Reclaiming memory, usually through GC
B) Using the delete keyword
C) Removing source code
D) Renaming variables
Reason: The garbage collector reclaims eligible object memory.
Q37. Which is a likely cause of retaining too much memory?
A) An unbounded static collection of obsolete objects
B) Using a local int
C) A short method
D) A comment
Reason: Static references can keep collection contents reachable for the lifetime of the class loader.
Q38. What is a class loader's role related to memory?
A) Loading class definitions into the JVM
B) Collecting every object immediately
C) Managing only local variables
D) Replacing the heap
Reason: Class loaders locate and load class definitions for the JVM.
Q39. What is the program counter register in the JVM model associated with?
A) The current instruction for a thread, for Java execution
B) All heap objects
C) Database queries
D) Object fields
Reason: Each JVM thread has a program counter register tracking its current instruction position.
Q40. Which memory area is private to each thread in the JVM model?
A) Java stack
B) Heap
C) Method area
D) Runtime constant pool
Reason: Each thread has its own JVM stack.
Q41. Which memory area is shared among JVM threads?
A) Heap
B) Each thread's stack
C) Each thread's program counter
D) Local variable frame
Reason: The heap is shared among threads.
Q42. What is a direct buffer often used for?
A) I/O operations with memory outside the ordinary Java heap
B) Constructor chaining
C) Method overloading
D) Syntax parsing
Reason: Direct byte buffers can use native memory and may help with certain I/O operations.
Q43. Can native memory exhaustion occur even when Java heap usage is low?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only with arrays
D) Only with strings
Reason: The JVM and native libraries use memory outside the Java heap.
Q44. What is a memory profile useful for?
A) Finding allocation patterns and possible leaks
B) Changing Java syntax
C) Replacing testing
D) Writing comments
Reason: Profilers help identify memory use, retained objects, and allocation hot spots.
Q45. Which is a good way to reduce accidental object retention?
A) Remove obsolete references from long-lived collections
B) Call System.gc() in every loop
C) Make every field static
D) Avoid all objects
Reason: Removing unused references allows objects to become unreachable.
Q46. What is an immutable object?
A) An object whose observable state cannot change after construction
B) An object that is always collected
C) An object without a class
D) An object that uses no memory
Reason: Immutable objects do not change their state after they are created.
Q47. What does a shallow copy generally copy?
A) Top-level field values/references, not necessarily referenced objects themselves
B) Every nested object deeply
C) Only class names
D) Only static methods
Reason: A shallow copy can share referenced mutable objects with the original.
Q48. Which statement about String objects is correct?
A) Strings are immutable
B) Strings are primitive types
C) Strings cannot be referenced
D) Strings are always stack allocated
Reason: String objects cannot be changed after creation; operations that seem to modify them produce another string.


11. Exception & Error Handling
Q1. Which keyword begins a block that may throw an exception?
A) try
B) catch
C) throws
D) finally
Reason: The try block contains code whose exceptions may be handled by catch clauses.
Q2. Which block handles a matching exception?
A) try
B) catch
C) throw
D) import
Reason: A catch block handles exceptions of a compatible type.
Q3. Which block is commonly used for cleanup whether an exception occurs or not?
A) final
B) finally
C) throws
D) case
Reason: finally normally runs after try/catch completion, with some exceptional termination cases.
Q4. Which keyword explicitly throws an exception object?
A) throws
B) throw
C) catch
D) raise
Reason: throw is followed by an exception object.
Q5. Which keyword declares exceptions a method may pass to its caller?
A) throw
B) throws
C) try
D) finally
Reason: throws appears in a method declaration to list exception types.
Q6. Which is a checked exception?
A) IOException
B) NullPointerException
C) ArithmeticException
D) ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
Reason: IOException is checked and generally must be caught or declared.
Q7. Which is an unchecked exception?
A) IOException
B) SQLException
C) NullPointerException
D) ClassNotFoundException
Reason: NullPointerException is a RuntimeException and is unchecked.
Q8. What is the superclass of exceptions and errors in Java?
A) Object
B) Throwable
C) Exception only
D) RuntimeException
Reason: Throwable is the common superclass of Exception and Error.
Q9. Which branch of Throwable represents serious JVM/application problems typically not intended for ordinary recovery?
A) Error
B) RuntimeException only
C) IOException
D) String
Reason: Error represents serious conditions such as VirtualMachineError.
Q10. What happens if a checked exception is neither caught nor declared?
A) The code generally fails compilation
B) The JVM ignores it
C) It becomes a comment
D) It is automatically converted to Error
Reason: Java's compile-time exception checking requires checked exceptions to be caught or declared.
Q11. Which exception may occur when dividing an int by zero?
A) ArithmeticException
B) IOException
C) ClassCastException
D) FileNotFoundException
Reason: Integer division by zero throws ArithmeticException.
Q12. Which exception can result from accessing an array index outside its bounds?
A) IndexOutOfBoundsError
B) ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
C) IOException
D) IllegalAccessException
Reason: An invalid array index causes ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
Q13. Which exception can occur when casting an object to an incompatible type?
A) ClassCastException
B) ArithmeticException
C) IOException
D) InterruptedException
Reason: An invalid runtime reference cast can throw ClassCastException.
Q14. What does a stack trace help show?
A) The sequence of calls leading to an exception
B) Only the computer's RAM size
C) The source-code license
D) The package list
Reason: A stack trace records the call path at the point an exception was created or printed.
Q15. Can a try block have multiple catch blocks?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only exactly two
D) Only if no finally
Reason: Multiple catch blocks can handle different exception types.
Q16. Why should a subclass exception catch usually come before its superclass catch?
A) Otherwise the subclass catch may be unreachable
B) It runs slower otherwise
C) It changes inheritance
D) It is required by the JVM at runtime only
Reason: A superclass catch would already match the subclass, making a later subclass catch unreachable.
Q17. What is a multi-catch?
A) One catch handling multiple unrelated exception types with |
B) Several finally blocks
C) A catch inside a loop only
D) A method with many returns
Reason: Java supports catch (A | B e) for suitable alternative exception types.
Q18. Which is true about finally?
A) It is intended for cleanup and usually executes
B) It always executes even if the JVM halts
C) It must always be present
D) It catches every exception
Reason: finally normally executes during ordinary control flow, but abrupt JVM termination can prevent it.
Q19. What does try-with-resources do?
A) Automatically closes declared AutoCloseable resources
B) Automatically catches all exceptions
C) Prevents object allocation
D) Replaces all classes
Reason: Resources are closed automatically at the end of the statement.
Q20. Which interface supports try-with-resources?
A) Runnable
B) AutoCloseable
C) Serializable
D) Comparable
Reason: A resource must implement AutoCloseable (Closeable extends it).
Q21. What is a custom exception?
A) An exception class created for application-specific conditions
B) A compiler keyword
C) A thread type
D) An array
Reason: Applications can define exception classes to represent domain-specific failures.
Q22. Which class is commonly extended to create a checked custom exception?
A) Exception
B) Error
C) Thread
D) String
Reason: Extending Exception directly (rather than RuntimeException) creates a checked exception type.
Q23. Which class is commonly extended for an unchecked custom exception?
A) RuntimeException
B) IOException
C) Throwable only
D) AutoCloseable
Reason: RuntimeException subclasses are unchecked.
Q24. What is exception propagation?
A) An exception moves up the call stack until handled or the thread terminates
B) An object changes class
C) A loop repeats
D) A package is imported
Reason: If not handled locally, an exception can propagate to callers.
Q25. What does getMessage() commonly return?
A) The detail message associated with an exception
B) The full source file
C) The method's bytecode
D) The number of threads
Reason: Throwable.getMessage() returns its detail message, or null if none was set.
Q26. Which statement about catch order is correct?
A) More specific exception types should precede broader types
B) Throwable must always be first
C) Order never matters
D) RuntimeException must be last in every program
Reason: Catch clauses are checked in order and unreachable clauses are rejected.
Q27. Can a method throw an exception without catching it locally?
A) Yes, if it declares or otherwise legally propagates it
B) No, never
C) Only constructors can
D) Only main can
Reason: A method may declare checked exceptions using throws; unchecked exceptions need not be declared.
Q28. What is the purpose of the throw statement?
A) To signal an exceptional condition
B) To declare a package
C) To start a thread
D) To allocate an array
Reason: throw transfers control by throwing a specified Throwable object.
Q29. Which exception is likely from parsing an invalid integer string with Integer.parseInt?
A) NumberFormatException
B) IOException
C) EOFException
D) InterruptedException
Reason: NumberFormatException is thrown when a string cannot be parsed as an integer.
Q30. Which exception may occur when using a null reference for an instance call?
A) NullPointerException
B) FileNotFoundException
C) IOException
D) SQLException
Reason: Dereferencing null for an instance operation causes NullPointerException.
Q31. What does a method's throws clause not do?
A) Automatically handle the exception
B) Declare possible checked exceptions
C) Inform callers of possible exceptions
D) Allow checked exceptions to propagate
Reason: throws declares possible propagation; it does not handle the exception.
Q32. Which is generally preferable for expected recoverable conditions?
A) Catch a specific exception and respond appropriately
B) Catch Throwable and ignore it
C) Use an empty catch block always
D) Use System.exit for every problem
Reason: Specific handling makes recovery clear and avoids hiding unrelated failures.
Q33. Why is catching Throwable broadly risky?
A) It can catch serious Errors as well as exceptions
B) It catches only strings
C) It prevents compilation
D) It disables garbage collection
Reason: Throwable includes Error types that applications usually should not casually swallow.
Q34. What is a suppressed exception in try-with-resources?
A) An additional exception recorded when resource closing also fails
B) An exception deleted from memory
C) A checked exception converted to a warning
D) A syntax token
Reason: If the try body throws and close also throws, the close exception can be attached as suppressed.
Q35. Can a finally block contain a return statement?
A) Yes, but it is discouraged because it can override earlier returns/exceptions
B) No, it is a syntax error in all cases
C) Only if static
D) Only in constructors
Reason: A return in finally can mask a pending return value or exception.
Q36. What is the difference between exception and error in Java?
A) Exception generally represents conditions applications may handle; Error represents serious problems
B) They are identical in every way
C) Error is always checked
D) Exception cannot be thrown
Reason: The distinction is a useful guideline, although both are Throwable subclasses.
Q37. Which exception is associated with waiting or sleeping being interrupted?
A) InterruptedException
B) ArithmeticException
C) ClassCastException
D) IllegalArgumentException
Reason: wait, sleep, and join can throw InterruptedException.
Q38. What should code generally do when it catches InterruptedException and cannot rethrow it?
A) Restore the interrupt status when appropriate
B) Ignore it silently in all cases
C) Call System.gc()
D) Convert it to NullPointerException
Reason: Calling Thread.currentThread().interrupt() preserves the interrupt signal when not propagated.
Q39. Which exception is associated with an invalid method argument?
A) IllegalArgumentException
B) IOException
C) StackOverflowError
D) NoClassDefFoundError
Reason: IllegalArgumentException indicates a method received an inappropriate argument.
Q40. Which exception may be thrown when a file path does not identify an existing file for a file input stream?
A) FileNotFoundException
B) ArithmeticException
C) ClassCastException
D) AssertionError
Reason: FileNotFoundException is an IOException subclass used for file-opening failures.
Q41. Which statement about checked exceptions is correct?
A) The compiler checks that they are caught or declared
B) They can never occur at runtime
C) They are all Errors
D) They cannot have subclasses
Reason: Checked exceptions are subject to compile-time catch-or-declare checking.
Q42. What is an exception handler?
A) Code that responds to a thrown exception
B) A garbage collector
C) A compiler flag only
D) A constructor
Reason: A catch block is a common exception handler.
Q43. What is the main purpose of exception handling?
A) Separate error-handling logic from normal flow and manage failures
B) Guarantee a program never fails
C) Speed up every loop
D) Replace testing
Reason: Exception handling provides a structured way to detect and respond to exceptional conditions.
Q44. Which keyword is used in Java assertions, not exception declaration?
A) assert
B) throws
C) catch
D) throw
Reason: assert checks a boolean condition when assertions are enabled.
Q45. Are Java assertions enabled by default in typical JVM launches?
A) Usually no
B) Always yes
C) Only for interfaces
D) Only for constructors
Reason: Assertions are normally disabled unless enabled with JVM options such as -ea.
Q46. Which is a valid catch parameter form?
A) catch (IOException e)
B) catch IOException e
C) catch (e IOException)
D) catch [IOException e]
Reason: A catch clause uses a parenthesized exception type and variable.
Q47. What should generally not be done in a catch block?
A) Silently swallowing an exception without a reason
B) Logging useful context
C) Recovering when possible
D) Adding meaningful handling
Reason: Ignoring failures without handling or reporting them can hide bugs and data loss.
Q48. What does the cause of an exception represent?
A) The underlying throwable that led to this exception
B) The exception's line number only
C) A package name
D) The return type
Reason: Exception chaining preserves the underlying cause for diagnosis.


12. Modules, Packages & Libraries
Q1. Which keyword declares a package at the start of a Java source file?
A) package
B) import
C) module
D) library
Reason: A package declaration names the package to which the type belongs.
Q2. Which keyword makes a type from another package available by simple name?
A) include
B) import
C) using
D) require
Reason: import allows use of a type by its simple name, subject to access rules.
Q3. Which package is automatically imported into ordinary Java source files?
A) java.util
B) java.io
C) java.lang
D) java.net
Reason: Types in java.lang, such as String and System, are available without an explicit import.
Q4. Which class is part of java.util?
A) ArrayList
B) FileInputStream
C) Socket
D) LocalDateTime
Reason: ArrayList is in java.util.
Q5. What is a Java package primarily used for?
A) Organizing related types and helping manage names/access
B) Running garbage collection
C) Replacing classes
D) Creating CPU cores
Reason: Packages group related classes/interfaces and help avoid naming conflicts.
Q6. What is a fully qualified class name for ArrayList?
A) ArrayList.java.util
B) java.util.ArrayList
C) util.java.ArrayList
D) java.ArrayList.util
Reason: The fully qualified name includes the package and type name.
Q7. Which access level allows access from anywhere, subject to module/API accessibility?
A) private
B) package-private
C) public
D) local
Reason: public members/types are broadly accessible when their enclosing API is accessible.
Q8. Can a package be imported with import java.util.*;?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only for classes in default package
D) Only in module-info.java
Reason: A wildcard import makes accessible types in that package available by simple name; it does not import subpackages.
Q9. Does import java.util.* import java.util.concurrent classes too?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only on Linux
D) Only if public static
Reason: Wildcard imports do not recursively import subpackages.
Q10. What is a JAR file?
A) A Java archive that can package classes/resources and metadata
B) A Java variable
C) A JVM error
D) A package keyword
Reason: JAR files use an archive format to bundle Java classes and resources.
Q11. Which tool commonly creates a JAR archive?
A) jar
B) javac only
C) javadoc only
D) jdb only
Reason: The jar tool creates and manipulates Java archive files.
Q12. What is the Java module system introduced in Java 9 designed to provide?
A) A stronger way to group and declare dependencies among packages
B) Automatic multiple class inheritance
C) A replacement for all packages
D) A new primitive type
Reason: Modules declare dependencies and which packages they export.
Q13. What is the usual name of a module descriptor file?
A) module.java
B) module-info.java
C) package-info.class
D) manifest.java
Reason: module-info.java declares a module and its directives.
Q14. Which directive declares a dependency on another module?
A) exports
B) requires
C) opens
D) uses
Reason: requires states that the module depends on another module.
Q15. Which module directive exposes a package to other modules at compile time?
A) requires
B) exports
C) provides
D) uses
Reason: exports makes a package accessible to other modules.
Q16. Which directive allows reflective access to a package?
A) opens
B) exports only
C) requires
D) transitive
Reason: opens allows deep reflection into a package, subject to module rules.
Q17. What does java.base provide?
A) Core Java APIs and is implicitly required by every module
B) Only GUI APIs
C) Only database APIs
D) Only third-party libraries
Reason: java.base contains fundamental APIs such as java.lang and java.util basics.
Q18. What is a library in programming?
A) Reusable code packaged for use by applications
B) Only a folder of images
C) A compiler error
D) A primitive type
Reason: Libraries provide ready-made classes and methods that applications can call.
Q19. Which package contains many collection classes such as HashMap?
A) java.util
B) java.awt
C) java.net
D) java.time
Reason: HashMap and many collection utilities are in java.util.
Q20. Which package provides basic input/output streams and file APIs?
A) java.io
B) java.math
C) java.text
D) java.applet
Reason: java.io contains classic stream and file-related I/O classes.
Q21. Which package contains JDBC core interfaces such as Connection?
A) java.sql
B) java.net
C) java.util
D) java.awt
Reason: JDBC interfaces such as Connection and PreparedStatement are in java.sql.
Q22. Which package provides date and time classes such as LocalDate?
A) java.time
B) java.clock
C) java.date
D) java.util.time
Reason: The modern date/time API is in java.time.
Q23. Which package contains networking classes such as Socket?
A) java.net
B) java.sql
C) java.text
D) java.lang
Reason: Socket and related networking APIs are in java.net.
Q24. What does a static import allow?
A) Using accessible static members without qualifying them by the declaring type
B) Importing every subpackage
C) Loading a module at runtime only
D) Creating a class
Reason: A static import can make static fields/methods available by simple name.
Q25. Which is valid syntax for a static import?
A) import static java.lang.Math.PI;
B) static import java.lang.Math.PI;
C) import java.lang.static.Math.PI;
D) include static Math.PI;
Reason: The syntax starts with import static followed by the member's qualified name.
Q26. What is a dependency in software?
A) A component or library another component relies on
B) A Java comment
C) A constructor parameter only
D) An array index
Reason: Dependencies are other components required for building or running software.
Q27. Why should external library versions be managed carefully?
A) To improve reproducibility, compatibility, and security
B) To avoid using classes
C) To disable compilation
D) To remove packages
Reason: Version control helps builds remain predictable and reduces incompatible or vulnerable dependencies.
Q28. What does the classpath identify?
A) Locations where the Java launcher/compiler can find classes and JARs
B) Only source-code comments
C) The thread stack
D) The current package name only
Reason: Classpath entries help locate class files and archives.
Q29. What is the module path used for?
A) Locating modules for the Java module system
B) Locating only image files
C) Naming local variables
D) Creating object references
Reason: The module path contains modules that the module system resolves.
Q30. Can two packages contain classes with the same simple name?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only if one is abstract
D) Only in one file
Reason: Package names distinguish types that share the same simple name.
Q31. What does package-private mean?
A) Accessible within the same package
B) Accessible only within the class
C) Accessible from all packages
D) Accessible only to subclasses everywhere
Reason: No access modifier gives package-level access.
Q32. What is the default package?
A) A package used by a class with no package declaration
B) The java.lang package
C) A module required by all modules
D) A third-party library
Reason: A source file without a package declaration belongs to the unnamed/default package.
Q33. Which statement about importing a class is correct?
A) Importing does not copy the class into the program
B) It copies all source code into the file
C) It makes private members public
D) It creates an object
Reason: Import is a name-resolution convenience; it does not copy class code.
Q34. What is API documentation commonly generated with?
A) javadoc
B) jar
C) java
D) jshell only
Reason: The javadoc tool generates documentation from source comments and declarations.
Q35. What is an API?
A) A defined set of types and operations a component exposes
B) A memory area
C) A loop structure
D) An exception type
Reason: An API specifies how other code can interact with a library or service.
Q36. Which is an example of a standard Java library class?
A) java.util.Scanner
B) myapp.MyScanner only
C) CScanner
D) HTMLScanner
Reason: Scanner is a standard class in java.util.
Q37. What does Maven commonly manage in Java projects?
A) Builds and project dependencies
B) CPU scheduling directly
C) Garbage collection settings only
D) Java keywords
Reason: Maven is a build and dependency-management tool.
Q38. What does Gradle commonly do?
A) Automates builds and manages dependencies
B) Replaces the JVM
C) Defines primitive types
D) Catches every exception
Reason: Gradle is a build automation system often used in Java projects.
Q39. What is semantic versioning commonly expressed as?
A) MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
B) CLASS.METHOD.FIELD
C) A.B.C.D only
D) YEAR.MONTH.DAY only
Reason: Semantic versioning commonly uses major, minor, and patch components.
Q40. Which command compiles Java source code?
A) javac
B) java
C) jar
D) javadoc
Reason: javac compiles .java source files into class files.
Q41. Which command commonly launches a Java class?
A) java
B) javac
C) jar
D) javadoc
Reason: The java launcher starts the JVM and invokes the program entry point.
Q42. What is a third-party library?
A) A library supplied outside the project's own code and standard JDK
B) A private local variable
C) A built-in operator
D) A Java stack frame
Reason: Third-party libraries are maintained or supplied separately from the project's own code.
Q43. Why are licenses important for libraries?
A) They define permitted use, modification, and distribution
B) They determine array length
C) They control thread count only
D) They replace tests
Reason: License terms govern legal use and redistribution of software.
Q44. What is a transitive dependency?
A) A dependency brought in through another dependency
B) A package with no classes
C) A static method
D) A checked exception
Reason: If A depends on B and B depends on C, C may be a transitive dependency of A.
Q45. What does encapsulating library implementation mean?
A) Users interact through a public API without needing internal details
B) Every field must be public
C) All classes must be static
D) No documentation is needed
Reason: A stable public API hides implementation details and allows internal changes.
Q46. What is a package naming convention often based on?
A) A reversed domain name, such as com.example
B) A random emoji
C) The class file size
D) The current date only
Reason: Reverse-domain naming reduces package-name collisions.
Q47. Can one Java module export multiple packages?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only exactly one
D) Only if unnamed
Reason: A module can contain and export multiple packages.
Q48. What is the purpose of a module's requires transitive directive?
A) Make a dependency readable to modules that depend on this module
B) Export every package
C) Close reflection
D) Create a JAR
Reason: requires transitive exposes readability of that dependency to downstream modules.


13. Advanced Programming Concepts
Q1. What is a generic type in Java used for?
A) Writing reusable code with compile-time type parameters
B) Running code in parallel automatically
C) Allocating native memory only
D) Catching every exception
Reason: Generics allow classes and methods to work with types while preserving compile-time checks.
Q2. Which syntax declares a generic class with type parameter T?
A) class Box<T> {}
B) class Box(T) {}
C) generic Box T {}
D) class<T> Box {}
Reason: Type parameters are declared in angle brackets after the class name.
Q3. What does List<String> represent?
A) A list whose elements are Strings
B) A String array primitive
C) A list of any type without checks
D) A module
Reason: The generic type parameter specifies String as the element type.
Q4. What is type erasure?
A) A process that removes most generic type-parameter information during compilation
B) Deleting objects at runtime
C) Removing comments
D) Changing all types to String
Reason: Java implements generics largely through type erasure for runtime compatibility.
Q5. Which wildcard means an unknown type?
A) <?>
B) <*>
C) <unknown>
D) <any>
Reason: <?> is an unbounded wildcard type argument.
Q6. Which wildcard is suitable for a producer of Number values, such as reading Integers?
A) ? super Integer
B) ? extends Number
C) ? extends String
D) ? super Object only
Reason: ? extends Number allows reading values as Number, though adding non-null values is restricted.
Q7. Which wildcard is commonly useful when adding Integer values to a consumer list?
A) ? extends Integer
B) ? super Integer
C) ? extends String
D) <?> only
Reason: ? super Integer can refer to a list of Integer or a supertype element type, making Integer additions safe.
Q8. What does PECS stand for in generic API design?
A) Producer Extends, Consumer Super
B) Private Encapsulation, Class Static
C) Package Export, Class Scope
D) Parallel Execution, CPU Scheduling
Reason: PECS is a guideline: use extends for producers and super for consumers.
Q9. Which functional interface accepts one argument and returns a result?
A) Consumer<T>
B) Supplier<T>
C) Function<T,R>
D) Runnable
Reason: Function<T,R> takes a T and produces an R.
Q10. Which functional interface represents an operation with no arguments and no result?
A) Runnable
B) Predicate<T>
C) Function<T,R>
D) Supplier<T>
Reason: Runnable's run method has no parameters and returns void.
Q11. Which functional interface tests a condition and returns boolean?
A) Predicate<T>
B) Consumer<T>
C) Supplier<T>
D) Runnable
Reason: Predicate<T> defines test(T) returning boolean.
Q12. Which functional interface supplies a value without taking an argument?
A) Supplier<T>
B) Consumer<T>
C) Predicate<T>
D) BiConsumer<T,U>
Reason: Supplier<T> defines get() to return a value.
Q13. What is a lambda expression primarily used for?
A) Providing an implementation of a functional interface
B) Declaring a package
C) Creating a new primitive type
D) Replacing all classes
Reason: A lambda provides behavior for a functional interface target type.
Q14. Which is a valid lambda expression that adds two integers?
A) (a, b) -> a + b
B) (a, b) => a + b
C) lambda a,b: a+b
D) a + b ->
Reason: Java uses -> between lambda parameters and the body.
Q15. What is a method reference?
A) A concise reference to an existing method or constructor
B) A pointer that can be freely dereferenced
C) A package alias
D) A checked exception
Reason: Method references use :: to refer to existing methods or constructors.
Q16. Which operator introduces a method reference?
A) ::
B) ->
C) =>
D) ??
Reason: The double-colon operator is Java's method-reference syntax.
Q17. What is a stream in Java?
A) A pipeline for processing sequences of elements
B) A thread only
C) A file necessarily
D) An array primitive
Reason: Streams support declarative aggregate operations on data sequences.
Q18. Which stream operation is intermediate?
A) filter
B) count
C) forEach
D) reduce result
Reason: filter returns another stream and is intermediate; count is terminal.
Q19. Which stream operation is terminal?
A) map
B) filter
C) sorted
D) collect
Reason: collect consumes the stream and produces a result.
Q20. Are Java streams generally reusable after a terminal operation?
A) Yes, indefinitely
B) No, a stream is consumed
C) Only if parallel
D) Only for strings
Reason: A stream should be used for one pipeline; reusing a consumed stream can cause IllegalStateException.
Q21. What does Optional<T> represent?
A) A container that may or may not hold a non-null value
B) A thread pool
C) A generic array
D) A checked exception
Reason: Optional models a possibly absent value and can reduce some null-handling ambiguity.
Q22. Which method provides a fallback value from an Optional?
A) orElse
B) throw
C) catch
D) extend
Reason: orElse returns the contained value or the provided fallback.
Q23. What is reflection in Java?
A) Inspecting or interacting with classes, methods, and fields at runtime
B) A way to reverse a string only
C) A memory allocation algorithm
D) A compiler error
Reason: Reflection APIs inspect runtime type information and can invoke members subject to access rules.
Q24. Which package contains core reflection APIs?
A) java.lang.reflect
B) java.reflect.lang
C) java.util.reflect
D) java.runtime
Reason: Classes such as Method and Field are in java.lang.reflect.
Q25. What is an annotation?
A) Metadata attached to program declarations
B) A type of loop
C) An object constructor
D) A memory region
Reason: Annotations provide metadata that tools, compilers, or runtime frameworks can use.
Q26. Which annotation indicates an intended override?
A) @Override
B) @Overload
C) @InheritedOnly
D) @Method
Reason: @Override lets the compiler check that a method overrides an inherited method.
Q27. What does @FunctionalInterface indicate?
A) The interface is intended to have one abstract method
B) The interface has no methods
C) The class must be final
D) The method is static
Reason: The compiler checks the functional-interface constraint when this annotation is used.
Q28. What is serialization generally used for?
A) Representing object state as a form suitable for storage or transfer
B) Compiling loops
C) Starting threads
D) Changing access modifiers
Reason: Serialization converts object state into a storable or transferable representation.
Q29. Which interface is traditionally associated with Java object serialization?
A) Serializable
B) Runnable
C) Comparable
D) AutoCloseable
Reason: Serializable is a marker interface used by Java's built-in serialization mechanism.
Q30. Why should Java native serialization be used carefully with untrusted data?
A) Deserialization can create security risks
B) It prevents compilation
C) It always deletes files
D) It disables exceptions
Reason: Untrusted deserialization can enable dangerous object construction and gadget-chain attacks.
Q31. What is an enum in Java?
A) A type representing a fixed set of named constants
B) A generic method only
C) A thread pool
D) A package
Reason: An enum declares a fixed set of instances/constants.
Q32. Can a Java enum have fields and methods?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only fields
D) Only constructors are public
Reason: Enums can contain fields, methods, and constructors.
Q33. What is a record in modern Java?
A) A concise declaration for data-carrier classes
B) A type of exception only
C) A module descriptor
D) A thread
Reason: Records automatically provide components and common data-oriented methods.
Q34. Are record component fields implicitly final?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only for String components
D) Only if static
Reason: Record component fields are final, supporting the record's shallowly immutable state model.
Q35. What does var allow for local variables?
A) Local variable type inference
B) Dynamic typing everywhere
C) Changing a variable's type later
D) Declaring fields without types
Reason: var lets the compiler infer a local variable's static type from its initializer.
Q36. Can var be used as a field type?
A) Yes
B) No, not for fields
C) Only in interfaces
D) Only for static fields
Reason: var is limited to local variable declarations and certain other specific contexts, not fields.
Q37. What is a sealed class designed to control?
A) Which classes may extend or implement a type
B) Which methods can return null
C) How GC works
D) How imports work
Reason: Sealed types restrict permitted direct subclasses or implementors.
Q38. Which keyword can declare permitted subclasses for a sealed type?
A) permits
B) allows
C) subclasses
D) inherits
Reason: The permits clause names permitted direct subclasses when needed.
Q39. What is pattern matching for instanceof intended to simplify?
A) Testing a type and binding a variable of that type
B) Creating packages
C) Declaring generic arrays
D) Closing resources
Reason: Pattern matching can combine a type test with a safely scoped pattern variable.
Q40. What is a checked cast?
A) A cast whose compatibility is validated at runtime for reference types
B) A cast guaranteed to never fail
C) A compile-time package import
D) A generic method
Reason: Reference casts are checked at runtime and may throw ClassCastException.
Q41. What is a varargs parameter declared with?
A) ...
B) ***
C) []...
D) ::
Reason: A declaration such as String... args accepts a variable number of arguments.
Q42. Which keyword prevents a variable from being reassigned after initialization?
A) final
B) static
C) volatile
D) transient
Reason: A final local variable or field can be assigned only once, subject to definite-assignment rules.
Q43. What does volatile primarily provide for a field shared across threads?
A) Visibility and ordering guarantees for reads/writes
B) Atomicity for every compound operation
C) Automatic locking of all methods
D) Garbage collection
Reason: volatile establishes visibility/order guarantees but does not make compound updates like count++ atomic.
Q44. What does assert help check?
A) A condition expected to be true during development/testing
B) A package dependency
C) A method overload
D) An object constructor
Reason: Assertions can detect violated assumptions when enabled.
Q45. What is an invariant in software?
A) A condition that should remain true at defined points
B) A random variable
C) A compiler warning only
D) A library
Reason: Invariants express rules that program state must maintain.
Q46. What is defensive programming?
A) Anticipating invalid inputs and failure conditions
B) Avoiding all methods
C) Making all fields public
D) Removing error handling
Reason: Defensive programming validates assumptions and handles foreseeable failures.
Q47. What is an immutable class design benefit?
A) Objects are easier to reason about and safer to share
B) Objects consume no memory
C) It prevents all exceptions
D) It removes compilation
Reason: Immutability reduces state changes and can simplify reasoning and concurrency.
Q48. What is an API contract?
A) The documented behavior and obligations of a software interface
B) A JAR compression method
C) A JVM stack frame
D) A variable declaration
Reason: A contract specifies expected inputs, outputs, effects, and conditions.


14. Concurrency & Parallelism (Introductory)
Q1. What is concurrency?
A) Managing multiple tasks whose execution periods overlap
B) Only executing one instruction ever
C) Compiling many files only
D) Deleting threads
Reason: Concurrent tasks make progress during overlapping periods, not necessarily at the exact same instant.
Q2. What is parallelism?
A) Executing multiple operations at the same time on different processing resources
B) Only alternating tasks on one core
C) A type of exception
D) A package
Reason: Parallelism means simultaneous execution, often using multiple cores.
Q3. Which class represents a thread of execution in Java?
A) Thread
B) TaskOnly
C) ProcessClass
D) ExecutorOnly
Reason: java.lang.Thread represents a thread.
Q4. Which interface is commonly used to define a task with no result?
A) Runnable
B) Callable only
C) Serializable
D) Comparable
Reason: Runnable defines run() with no return value.
Q5. Which interface supports a task that returns a result and can throw checked exceptions?
A) Callable<V>
B) Runnable
C) Consumer<V>
D) Cloneable
Reason: Callable<V> defines call() and returns a result of type V.
Q6. Which method starts a new thread using a Thread object?
A) start()
B) run() directly
C) begin()
D) executeThread()
Reason: start() asks the JVM to start a new thread that invokes run().
Q7. What happens when you call run() directly on a Thread object?
A) It runs as a normal method on the current thread
B) It always creates a new thread
C) It shuts down the JVM
D) It starts two threads
Reason: Calling run directly does not start a separate thread.
Q8. Which method pauses a thread for a specified time?
A) sleep()
B) waitFor()
C) pauseThread()
D) stopTime()
Reason: Thread.sleep pauses the current thread for a duration, subject to scheduling.
Q9. Which method waits for another thread to finish?
A) join()
B) sleep()
C) yield() only
D) notify()
Reason: join waits for the target thread to terminate.
Q10. What does synchronized provide?
A) Mutual exclusion and memory-visibility guarantees around a monitor
B) Automatic parallelism
C) A new process
D) A checked exception
Reason: synchronized acquires a monitor and establishes relevant happens-before relationships.
Q11. What is a race condition?
A) Behavior depends on timing/interleaving of concurrent operations
B) A program runs quickly
C) A compiler warning
D) A method is final
Reason: Unsynchronized access to shared mutable state can make outcomes depend on thread timing.
Q12. What is a critical section?
A) Code accessing shared state that requires coordinated access
B) A comment block
C) A constructor only
D) A package descriptor
Reason: Critical sections are protected to avoid conflicting concurrent operations.
Q13. What is a deadlock?
A) Threads wait indefinitely for resources held by each other
B) A thread finishes normally
C) A compile error
D) A fast algorithm
Reason: Circular resource waiting can prevent all involved threads from progressing.
Q14. What is starvation?
A) A thread is repeatedly denied needed CPU time or resources
B) The heap is empty
C) All threads terminate
D) A package is missing
Reason: Starvation occurs when a thread cannot obtain resources or scheduling opportunities.
Q15. What is livelock?
A) Threads remain active but keep reacting without making useful progress
B) All threads are asleep forever
C) A memory leak
D) A compilation stage
Reason: In livelock, activity continues but the task does not advance.
Q16. Which keyword can help make a field's updates visible across threads?
A) volatile
B) transient
C) native
D) strictfp
Reason: volatile ensures reads see appropriately ordered writes to that field.
Q17. Does volatile make count++ atomic?
A) Yes, always
B) No
C) Only for long values
D) Only in synchronized methods
Reason: count++ is a read-modify-write sequence and is not made atomic by volatile alone.
Q18. Which class provides atomic integer operations?
A) AtomicInteger
B) IntegerAtomicOnly
C) ThreadInteger
D) SyncInt
Reason: AtomicInteger provides atomic operations such as incrementAndGet().
Q19. Which package contains ExecutorService?
A) java.util.concurrent
B) java.lang.thread
C) java.io.concurrent
D) java.parallel
Reason: ExecutorService is in java.util.concurrent.
Q20. What is a thread pool?
A) A reusable set of worker threads for executing tasks
B) A collection of source files
C) A garbage collector region
D) A set of primitive values
Reason: Thread pools reduce repeated thread creation and manage task execution.
Q21. Which method submits a Runnable or Callable to an ExecutorService?
A) submit()
B) join()
C) wait()
D) notifyAll()
Reason: submit schedules a task and returns a Future.
Q22. What does Future.get() do?
A) Waits for a result if needed and returns it
B) Starts the JVM
C) Always cancels the task
D) Locks every thread
Reason: get retrieves the result, blocking until completion if necessary.
Q23. Which interface represents a result that may become available later?
A) Future<V>
B) Runnable
C) ThreadLocal
D) AutoCloseable
Reason: Future represents the result/status of an asynchronous computation.
Q24. What does synchronized(lock) require?
A) An object monitor to lock on
B) A primitive int only
C) A package name
D) A return value
Reason: The synchronized statement locks the monitor associated with its expression object.
Q25. Can static synchronized methods synchronize on the Class object?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only on arrays
D) Only on null
Reason: A static synchronized method locks the Class object associated with the declaring class.
Q26. What is a monitor in Java concurrency?
A) A synchronization mechanism associated with an object's lock and wait set
B) A computer screen
C) A compiler
D) A thread pool only
Reason: Java object monitors support mutual exclusion and coordination with wait/notify.
Q27. Which method releases the monitor and waits for notification or interruption?
A) wait()
B) sleep()
C) yield()
D) join()
Reason: Object.wait releases the object's monitor while waiting.
Q28. Which methods notify waiting threads on an object's monitor?
A) notify() and notifyAll()
B) sleep() and join()
C) start() and run()
D) yield() only
Reason: notify wakes one waiting thread; notifyAll wakes all waiting threads on that monitor.
Q29. Must wait(), notify(), and notifyAll() be called while owning the object's monitor?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only notifyAll
D) Only from main
Reason: Calling these methods without owning the monitor causes IllegalMonitorStateException.
Q30. Why should wait() normally be used in a loop checking a condition?
A) A wake-up may be spurious or the condition may no longer hold
B) It compiles faster
C) It prevents all exceptions
D) It creates a new monitor
Reason: The condition must be rechecked after waking before proceeding.
Q31. What does Thread.currentThread() return?
A) The currently executing Thread object
B) The main method's source
C) All active threads
D) A Future
Reason: It returns the Thread instance representing the current thread.
Q32. Which thread state indicates a thread is waiting indefinitely for another thread's action?
A) WAITING
B) NEW
C) TERMINATED
D) RUNNABLE only
Reason: WAITING can result from calls such as wait() or join() without a timeout.
Q33. What does daemon thread mean?
A) A background thread that does not by itself prevent JVM shutdown
B) A thread with administrator privileges
C) A thread that always runs first
D) A thread that cannot be interrupted
Reason: The JVM can exit when only daemon threads remain.
Q34. Which method marks a thread as daemon before it starts?
A) setDaemon(true)
B) makeDaemon()
C) daemonize()
D) setBackground()
Reason: setDaemon must be called before the thread is started.
Q35. What is interruption generally used for?
A) Signaling a thread that it should stop or change its work cooperatively
B) Forcibly deleting its memory
C) Guaranteeing immediate termination
D) Starting a thread
Reason: Interruption is a cooperative cancellation signal.
Q36. Is Thread.stop() recommended for normal cancellation?
A) Yes
B) No; it is unsafe/deprecated
C) Only for daemon threads
D) Only in main
Reason: Asynchronous forced stopping can leave shared state inconsistent.
Q37. What is a happens-before relationship?
A) A memory-model ordering guarantee between actions
B) A class inheritance rule
C) A package import
D) A sorting algorithm
Reason: Happens-before helps define visibility and ordering between threads.
Q38. What is thread safety?
A) Correct behavior when code is used by multiple threads concurrently
B) A thread always runs first
C) No objects are allocated
D) A program has no methods
Reason: Thread-safe code maintains correctness under concurrent access.
Q39. What is a concurrent collection?
A) A collection designed to support concurrent access with defined behavior
B) A normal array only
C) A collection of source files
D) A collection that cannot be modified
Reason: Concurrent collections provide concurrency-aware operations and iteration behavior.
Q40. Which is a concurrent map implementation in Java?
A) ConcurrentHashMap
B) HashMapThreadSafe
C) SafeArrayMap
D) ParallelMap
Reason: ConcurrentHashMap is designed for concurrent access.
Q41. What is parallel stream processing intended to do?
A) Process stream elements using parallel execution when appropriate
B) Guarantee a faster result for every workload
C) Remove all synchronization needs
D) Always use one thread
Reason: Parallel streams may use multiple workers, but overhead and workload determine performance.
Q42. Why might parallel processing be slower for a small task?
A) Coordination and scheduling overhead can exceed the work saved
B) Java forbids small parallel tasks
C) It always allocates no memory
D) Threads cannot return values
Reason: Parallelism has overhead, so not every workload benefits.
Q43. What is a semaphore commonly used for?
A) Limiting concurrent access to a number of permits/resources
B) Creating classes
C) Catching exceptions
D) Allocating arrays
Reason: A semaphore controls access by acquiring and releasing permits.
Q44. What does CountDownLatch allow?
A) Threads to wait until a count reaches zero
B) A thread to change its class
C) Unlimited locks
D) Automatic exception handling
Reason: CountDownLatch releases waiting threads when its count reaches zero.
Q45. What is a BlockingQueue useful for?
A) Coordinating producer and consumer tasks
B) Replacing all classes
C) Storing only primitives
D) Compiling source code
Reason: Blocking queues can wait when empty or full and are useful in producer-consumer designs.
Q46. Which is a common safe approach to share data between tasks?
A) Use immutable data or proper synchronization/concurrent utilities
B) Share mutable fields without locks
C) Ignore visibility
D) Use sleep as a lock
Reason: Immutability and concurrency utilities reduce race conditions and visibility problems.
Q47. What is a common risk when using too many threads?
A) Resource overhead and contention
B) Automatic correctness
C) No context switching
D) Guaranteed speedup
Reason: Excessive threads consume resources and can increase scheduling overhead.
Q48. What does yield() do?
A) Hints that the scheduler may let another runnable thread execute
B) Guarantees a context switch
C) Waits until another thread terminates
D) Releases every monitor
Reason: yield is only a scheduler hint and has no guarantee of a particular scheduling outcome.


15. Debugging, Testing & Optimization
Q1. What is debugging?
A) Finding and fixing defects in software
B) Writing only documentation
C) Packaging a JAR
D) Installing Java
Reason: Debugging investigates program behavior to locate and correct defects.
Q2. What is a breakpoint in a debugger?
A) A point where execution can pause for inspection
B) A compiler keyword
C) A memory area
D) A test report
Reason: Breakpoints pause execution at selected locations.
Q3. What does stepping over a line usually do in a debugger?
A) Executes the line without entering called methods
B) Terminates the JVM
C) Skips every loop
D) Deletes a variable
Reason: Step over runs the current line and stops at the next line in the current frame.
Q4. What does stepping into a method do?
A) Moves execution into the called method
B) Skips the method completely
C) Restarts the computer
D) Compiles a library
Reason: Step into lets the debugger follow execution inside a method call.
Q5. What is a watch expression used for?
A) Inspecting a variable or expression while debugging
B) Changing source-code license
C) Starting a thread
D) Creating a package
Reason: Watches display values of selected expressions as execution changes.
Q6. What is a unit test?
A) A test of a small component, often a method or class
B) A test of the whole company network only
C) A deployment script
D) A compiler phase
Reason: Unit tests check focused units of behavior in isolation where practical.
Q7. What is an integration test?
A) A test of interactions between components
B) A test of one variable only
C) A code formatter
D) A class loader
Reason: Integration tests check whether connected components work together.
Q8. What is a regression test?
A) A test that checks previously working behavior after changes
B) A test that always fails
C) A performance metric only
D) A deployment environment
Reason: Regression tests detect unintended breakage caused by changes.
Q9. What is a test case?
A) A defined set of inputs, conditions, and expected results
B) A Java package
C) A thread state
D) A compiler flag
Reason: A test case describes how to exercise behavior and judge the outcome.
Q10. What is an assertion in a test?
A) A check that an actual result matches an expected condition
B) A package declaration
C) A thread pool
D) A memory allocation
Reason: Assertions make expected behavior explicit and fail a test when conditions are not met.
Q11. Which is a popular Java unit-testing framework?
A) JUnit
B) JAR
C) JVM
D) JDBC
Reason: JUnit is widely used for Java unit tests.
Q12. What is test-driven development (TDD)?
A) Writing a failing test before implementing the behavior, then making it pass and refactoring
B) Writing all code without tests
C) Testing only after release
D) Avoiding refactoring
Reason: TDD commonly follows red, green, refactor.
Q13. What does code coverage measure?
A) How much code is exercised by tests under a coverage metric
B) How fast code compiles only
C) How many comments exist
D) How many developers work
Reason: Coverage reports which statements, branches, or other elements were executed by tests.
Q14. Does 100% line coverage prove a program is bug-free?
A) Yes
B) No
C) Only for Java
D) Only for unit tests
Reason: Coverage shows execution, not whether all behavior and expected results are correct.
Q15. What is black-box testing based on?
A) External behavior and specifications, not internal implementation
B) Source-code line count
C) CPU architecture only
D) Private fields only
Reason: Black-box tests evaluate inputs and outputs against requirements.
Q16. What is white-box testing based on?
A) Knowledge of internal code structure
B) Only user documentation
C) Only production logs
D) No test data
Reason: White-box testing uses knowledge of control flow and implementation.
Q17. What is a mock object used for?
A) Simulating a dependency in a controlled test
B) Replacing the Java compiler
C) Compressing a JAR
D) Collecting garbage
Reason: Mocks can isolate a unit by controlling dependency behavior.
Q18. What is a test fixture?
A) The setup and supporting state needed for tests
B) A compiler error
C) A thread scheduler
D) A Java keyword
Reason: Fixtures provide objects and data required to run tests.
Q19. What is a flaky test?
A) A test that passes and fails inconsistently without relevant code changes
B) A test with no assertions by definition
C) A test that always passes
D) A test that only checks style
Reason: Flaky tests often depend on timing, shared state, or environmental conditions.
Q20. What is profiling used for?
A) Measuring runtime behavior such as CPU and memory use
B) Changing syntax
C) Proving all tests pass
D) Replacing version control
Reason: Profilers help identify performance bottlenecks based on measurements.
Q21. What is premature optimization?
A) Optimizing before evidence shows a meaningful performance problem
B) Optimizing after profiling
C) Writing a test first
D) Using a clear variable name
Reason: Premature optimization can add complexity without a measurable benefit.
Q22. Which complexity is usually preferable for large n, all else equal?
A) O(n log n) over O(n²)
B) O(n²) over O(n log n)
C) O(2^n) over O(n)
D) O(n!) over O(n log n)
Reason: For large inputs, n log n generally grows more slowly than n squared.
Q23. What is a bottleneck?
A) The part that limits overall system performance
B) A variable name
C) A type of exception
D) A package
Reason: The slowest or most constrained component can dominate end-to-end performance.
Q24. What is a memory profile useful for?
A) Finding excessive allocation and retained objects
B) Finding only syntax errors
C) Writing Javadoc
D) Naming modules
Reason: Memory profiling shows allocations, retained memory, and potential leaks.
Q25. What is a log useful for?
A) Recording events and context to diagnose behavior
B) Guaranteeing no bugs
C) Replacing all tests
D) Making every method faster
Reason: Logs provide information about application events and failures.
Q26. What does a stack trace help diagnose?
A) The call path associated with an exception or failure
B) The color of the UI
C) The CPU model only
D) The package license
Reason: Stack traces show method calls and source locations where available.
Q27. What is static analysis?
A) Analyzing code without executing the program
B) Running only UI tests
C) Measuring network speed
D) Executing every branch
Reason: Static analysis examines source or bytecode for potential defects and style issues.
Q28. What is code review?
A) Having another person inspect code for defects and maintainability
B) Running garbage collection
C) Renaming a package only
D) A runtime exception
Reason: Code reviews can identify logic issues, improve readability, and share knowledge.
Q29. What is refactoring?
A) Changing internal structure without intentionally changing external behavior
B) Adding unrelated features only
C) Deleting all tests
D) Changing a class to an interface every time
Reason: Refactoring improves design while preserving observable behavior.
Q30. What is a reproducible bug report likely to include?
A) Steps, expected result, actual result, and environment details
B) Only the word 'broken'
C) Only the developer's name
D) A screenshot without context always
Reason: Detailed reproduction steps and context help others confirm and diagnose a defect.
Q31. What is a null-related bug often prevented by?
A) Validating references and defining null-handling contracts
B) Calling System.gc()
C) Using more threads
D) Renaming methods
Reason: Explicit null contracts and checks can prevent accidental dereferences.
Q32. What is boundary-value testing?
A) Testing values at and near input limits
B) Testing only average values
C) Testing only comments
D) Testing only the main method
Reason: Defects often occur at limits, so boundary values deserve focused tests.
Q33. What is equivalence partitioning?
A) Dividing inputs into groups expected to behave similarly
B) Sorting test cases alphabetically
C) Splitting a class into packages
D) Running every possible input
Reason: Representative tests from equivalence classes can reduce redundant cases.
Q34. What is a performance benchmark?
A) A controlled measurement of performance for a workload
B) A code comment
C) A package name
D) An exception handler
Reason: Benchmarks measure metrics such as time or throughput under specified conditions.
Q35. Why should microbenchmarks be designed carefully in Java?
A) JIT compilation, warm-up, and runtime effects can distort measurements
B) Java has no optimizer
C) Methods cannot be timed
D) Only arrays can be benchmarked
Reason: The JVM optimizes code dynamically, so naïve timing can be misleading.
Q36. What does JIT stand for?
A) Just-In-Time compilation
B) Java Interface Type
C) Joint Input Test
D) Just Internal Thread
Reason: The JIT compiler compiles frequently executed bytecode into native code at runtime.
Q37. What is a common optimization for repeated expensive computations with identical inputs?
A) Memoization or caching when correctness permits
B) Adding sleeps
C) Catching Throwable
D) Making every variable volatile
Reason: Caching can avoid repeated work, provided invalidation and memory costs are managed.
Q38. What is algorithmic optimization?
A) Improving the algorithm's time or space complexity
B) Changing only indentation
C) Adding comments only
D) Changing the package name
Reason: Choosing a more efficient algorithm can yield larger gains than low-level tweaks.
Q39. What is a compiler warning?
A) A diagnostic about suspicious or potentially problematic code
B) Always a runtime crash
C) A successful unit test
D) A JAR file
Reason: Warnings alert developers to possible issues even when compilation succeeds.
Q40. What does a linter typically check?
A) Style and common code-quality issues
B) CPU temperature
C) Network packets only
D) Object reachability
Reason: Linters detect style violations and common patterns that may indicate defects.
Q41. What is continuous integration (CI)?
A) Frequently integrating changes with automated build and test checks
B) Manually copying code once a year
C) A Java primitive
D) A memory area
