Reason: CI runs automated checks on code changes to catch problems early.
Q42. What is a failing test's expected result useful for?
A) Distinguishing a real defect from a test misunderstanding
B) Making the test slower
C) Disabling assertions
D) Avoiding requirements
Reason: Clear expected results define what success means.
Q43. What is a test double?
A) A substitute object used to isolate or control a dependency during tests
B) A duplicated source file only
C) A second JVM
D) A primitive variable
Reason: Mocks, stubs, fakes, and spies are common test doubles.
Q44. What is a smoke test?
A) A basic check that the main functions work after a build or deployment
B) An exhaustive proof of correctness
C) A test of comments
D) A Java exception
Reason: Smoke tests quickly check whether a build is stable enough for further testing.
Q45. What is exploratory testing?
A) Learning and testing the software while designing tests during exploration
B) Only automated load testing
C) A test with predetermined expected outputs only
D) Compiling without running
Reason: Exploratory testing combines investigation, learning, and test design.
Q46. Why is a minimal reproducible example useful?
A) It isolates the smallest code and conditions that reproduce a problem
B) It hides the bug
C) It replaces debugging tools
D) It guarantees a fix
Reason: A minimal example reduces noise and makes a defect easier to understand.
Q47. What is the main goal of optimization after correctness?
A) Improve performance or resource use without breaking required behavior
B) Remove all error handling
C) Maximize code length
D) Avoid measurement
Reason: Optimization should preserve correctness and be guided by a meaningful goal.


16. Software Development Practices
Q1. What is version control used for?
A) Tracking and managing changes to files over time
B) Running garbage collection
C) Compiling only Java
D) Testing CPU temperature
Reason: Version control records changes and supports collaboration and recovery.
Q2. Which tool is widely used for distributed version control?
A) Git
B) JUnit
C) Javadoc
D) JDBC
Reason: Git tracks changes in repositories and supports distributed workflows.
Q3. What is a Git commit?
A) A recorded snapshot of repository changes
B) A Java constructor
C) A test assertion
D) A running thread
Reason: A commit records a set of changes and metadata in repository history.
Q4. What is a branch in version control?
A) An independent line of development
B) A Java package
C) A memory segment
D) A test case
Reason: Branches allow work to proceed separately before integration.
Q5. What is a merge conflict?
A) Competing changes that Git cannot automatically reconcile
B) A syntax error in every case
C) A thread deadlock
D) A failed garbage collection
Reason: Conflicts require a person to decide how overlapping changes should be combined.
Q6. What is code review intended to improve?
A) Correctness, maintainability, and shared understanding
B) Only file size
C) Only CPU speed
D) The number of classes
Reason: Review provides another perspective on logic, quality, and design.
Q7. What is a requirement?
A) A statement of a needed capability or constraint
B) A compiler instruction only
C) A Java primitive
D) A memory address
Reason: Requirements describe what a system should do or constraints it must meet.
Q8. What is a functional requirement?
A) A description of system behavior or feature
B) A performance limit only
C) A coding style rule only
D) A version-control branch
Reason: Functional requirements specify services, behaviors, and responses.
Q9. What is a non-functional requirement?
A) A quality or constraint such as performance, security, or reliability
B) A method name
C) A loop condition
D) A package import
Reason: Non-functional requirements define qualities and constraints on the system.
Q10. What is the purpose of software design?
A) Plan system structure and component interactions before/during implementation
B) Replace requirements completely
C) Guarantee no testing is needed
D) Only choose variable names
Reason: Design translates requirements into architecture and component-level plans.
Q11. What is modularity?
A) Dividing a system into components with clear responsibilities
B) Putting all code in one method
C) Using only static fields
D) Avoiding packages
Reason: Modularity supports separation of concerns and easier maintenance.
Q12. What does separation of concerns mean?
A) Keeping distinct responsibilities in distinct parts of a system
B) Combining every feature into one class
C) Avoiding documentation
D) Removing interfaces
Reason: Separating concerns limits complexity and makes changes more localized.
Q13. What is the purpose of documentation?
A) Explain how software is used, designed, or maintained
B) Replace all source code
C) Prevent all defects automatically
D) Compile classes
Reason: Documentation supports users, developers, operation, and maintenance.
Q14. What is a README commonly used for?
A) Explaining a project's purpose, setup, and usage
B) Defining a Java primitive
C) Holding the JVM heap
D) Catching exceptions
Reason: A README provides an entry point for understanding and using a project.
Q15. What is semantic versioning used to communicate?
A) Compatibility and change level through version numbers
B) Memory size
C) Thread priority
D) Code coverage
Reason: Major, minor, and patch versions communicate different kinds of releases.
Q16. What is a build system responsible for?
A) Automating compilation, tests, packaging, and related tasks
B) Replacing the operating system
C) Only drawing UI screens
D) Managing only user passwords
Reason: Build tools make software builds repeatable and automate common tasks.
Q17. What is continuous delivery/deployment related to?
A) Automating reliable release processes
B) Manually editing every class
C) Disabling testing
D) Creating a new primitive type
Reason: Continuous delivery/deployment automates steps that move validated software toward release.
Q18. What is an Agile approach generally characterized by?
A) Iterative delivery, feedback, and adaptation
B) One fixed plan with no feedback
C) No testing
D) No collaboration
Reason: Agile methods emphasize iterative work and responding to feedback.
Q19. What is a sprint in Scrum?
A) A fixed-length period for completing a planned increment of work
B) A Java thread
C) A compiler stage
D) A type of test case
Reason: A sprint is a timeboxed Scrum event/cycle.
Q20. What is a product backlog?
A) An ordered list of work that may be needed for a product
B) A list of runtime exceptions only
C) A package descriptor
D) A memory dump
Reason: The product backlog captures and orders potential product work.
Q21. What is a user story commonly intended to describe?
A) A user need or goal from the user's perspective
B) A Java stack trace
C) A class constructor
D) A build error
Reason: User stories communicate value and context from a user's perspective.
Q22. What is the purpose of acceptance criteria?
A) Define conditions that must be met for work to be accepted
B) List only coding styles
C) Set the CPU clock speed
D) Replace testing
Reason: Acceptance criteria make the expected completion conditions clear.
Q23. What is DevOps focused on?
A) Improving collaboration and automation across development and operations
B) Replacing programming languages
C) Only writing tests
D) Only database normalization
Reason: DevOps combines practices and culture that improve delivery and operational reliability.
Q24. What is a CI pipeline likely to do?
A) Build code and run automated checks after changes
B) Delete every branch
C) Guarantee the absence of bugs
D) Only generate images
Reason: CI pipelines automate build, test, and quality checks.
Q25. What is secure coding?
A) Writing software to reduce vulnerabilities and misuse
B) Encrypting every variable name
C) Avoiding all libraries
D) Making every method public
Reason: Secure coding applies practices that prevent common security weaknesses.
Q26. Why should secrets not be hard-coded in source control?
A) They can be exposed to anyone with repository access or history
B) It slows down loops only
C) Java cannot store strings
D) It prevents compilation
Reason: Credentials in source code can leak and may remain in repository history.
Q27. What is input validation?
A) Checking that supplied data meets expected rules before use
B) Encrypting source files only
C) Running a unit test
D) Changing the JVM
Reason: Validation helps reject malformed or out-of-range data.
Q28. What is the principle of least privilege?
A) Grant only the access necessary to perform a task
B) Give everyone administrator access
C) Disable all authentication
D) Share all passwords
Reason: Limiting permissions reduces the impact of mistakes or compromise.
Q29. What is dependency vulnerability management?
A) Identifying and updating libraries with known security issues
B) Removing every dependency
C) Changing variable names
D) Disabling builds
Reason: Dependency scanning and updates help reduce exposure to known flaws.
Q30. What is code maintainability?
A) How easily software can be understood, corrected, and changed
B) How many lines it contains only
C) How fast it starts only
D) How many developers are online
Reason: Maintainable code is easier to modify safely as requirements change.
Q31. Which practice improves readability?
A) Meaningful names and small focused methods
B) Single-letter names everywhere
C) Duplicating logic
D) Deep nesting without need
Reason: Clear names and focused methods reduce cognitive load.
Q32. What is code duplication problematic because it can?
A) Make fixes inconsistent and increase maintenance effort
B) Guarantee faster execution
C) Prevent compilation
D) Remove all bugs
Reason: Duplicated logic may need the same fix in multiple places.
Q33. What is the DRY principle?
A) Don't Repeat Yourself
B) Debug Runtime Yearly
C) Do Run Yesterday
D) Data Returns Yield
Reason: DRY encourages a single authoritative representation of knowledge where appropriate.
Q34. What does KISS commonly mean in software design?
A) Keep It Simple, Stupid (favor simplicity)
B) Keep Imports Sorted Securely
C) Kernel Input System Setup
D) Key Interface Service Syntax
Reason: KISS is a design guideline favoring simpler solutions over needless complexity.
Q35. What is pair programming?
A) Two developers work together at one workstation or shared coding session
B) Two JVMs always run in parallel
C) A test of two variables
D) A form of garbage collection
Reason: Pair programming uses collaborative roles to design, write, and review code.
Q36. What is a pull request commonly used for?
A) Proposing changes for review and integration
B) Starting a thread
C) Declaring a package
D) Allocating heap memory
Reason: A pull request invites review before changes are merged.
Q37. What is technical debt?
A) Future cost created by shortcuts or design choices that make later changes harder
B) Money paid for a laptop only
C) A Java exception
D) A testing framework
Reason: Technical debt describes trade-offs that can increase future maintenance costs.
Q38. What is a release note?
A) A summary of changes, fixes, and known issues in a release
B) A class file
C) A stack frame
D) A compiler token
Reason: Release notes communicate changes that matter to users and operators.
Q39. What is a deployment environment?
A) The system context where software is installed and run
B) A Java interface only
C) A variable type
D) A test assertion
Reason: Environments may include development, testing/staging, and production.
Q40. Why separate development, test, and production environments?
A) To test changes safely before affecting real users
B) To duplicate bugs intentionally
C) To remove version control
D) To avoid requirements
Reason: Separate environments reduce risk and help validate releases before production.
Q41. What is a rollback plan?
A) A way to return to a prior working version after a failed release
B) A Java loop
C) A method overload
D) A memory allocation
Reason: Rollback procedures reduce impact when a deployment causes problems.
Q42. What is observability in software operations?
A) Using logs, metrics, and traces to understand system behavior
B) Only writing comments
C) Only using a debugger locally
D) A type of inheritance
Reason: Observability helps teams infer internal state from system outputs.
Q43. What is a service-level objective (SLO)?
A) A target for a service reliability or performance measure
B) A Java source file
C) A branch name
D) A unit test method
Reason: An SLO defines a measurable target such as availability or latency.
Q44. What is a postmortem after an incident intended to do?
A) Learn causes and improve systems without focusing only on blame
B) Hide every failure
C) Delete all logs
D) Replace monitoring
Reason: A blameless postmortem identifies contributing factors and actions to reduce recurrence.
Q45. What is the purpose of a coding standard?
A) Promote consistent, readable code across a team
B) Guarantee no runtime errors
C) Replace architecture
D) Force every class to be public
Reason: Consistent conventions make code easier to read and review.
Q46. What is a license compliance check concerned with?
A) Whether software dependencies are used according to their license terms
B) CPU scheduling
C) Thread priority
D) Variable scope
Reason: Projects need to respect obligations and restrictions in dependency licenses.
Q47. What is a software maintenance activity?
A) Fixing defects, adapting to changes, or improving existing software
B) Only creating the first version
C) Only naming classes
D) Only compiling once
Reason: Maintenance continues after initial delivery to keep software useful and reliable.
Q48. What is user feedback useful for?
A) Validating needs and prioritizing improvements
B) Replacing all requirements permanently
C) Avoiding tests
D) Changing Java syntax
Reason: Feedback helps determine whether software solves users' actual problems.
Q49. What is a risk assessment in software development?
A) Identifying and prioritizing possible problems and their impact
B) Writing only comments
C) Generating a JAR
D) Creating a local variable
Reason: Risk assessment helps teams choose appropriate prevention and mitigation actions.
