Explanation: "You Only Look Once" predicts boxes and classes in a single pass, which makes it fast.
Q12. Intersection over Union (IoU) measures:
A) Brightness of an image
B) Number of objects
C) File size
D) Overlap between the predicted and ground-truth boxes


Correct Answer: D
Explanation: IoU = area of overlap / area of union. A higher value means a better localization.
Q13. Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS) is used to:
A) Remove duplicate overlapping detections, keeping the best box
B) Increase image size
C) Add more boxes
D) Normalize pixels
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: It keeps the highest-confidence box and suppresses others that overlap it heavily.
Q14. Instance segmentation differs from semantic segmentation because it:
A) Uses no neural network
B) Works only on grayscale
C) Labels only the background
D) Separates individual objects of the same class
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Semantic segmentation labels all "person" pixels the same. Instance segmentation
distinguishes person 1 from person 2.
Q15. A 28×28 grayscale image flattened into a vector has a length of:
A) 784
B) 56
C) 28
D) 2352
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: 28 × 28 × 1 = 784.
Q16. Gaussian blur is mainly used for:
A) Sharpening edges


B) Smoothing the image and reducing noise
C) Increasing contrast
D) Detecting faces
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It averages neighboring pixels with Gaussian weights, which is why it is often applied
before edge detection.
Q17. Histogram equalization improves an image's:
A) Resolution
B) Color depth
C) Contrast
D) File format
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It spreads out the intensity values, so dark or washed-out images look clearer.
Q18. Pixel values are often divided by 255 before feeding them into a neural network in order to:
A) Convert to grayscale
B) Compress the file
C) Remove noise
D) Scale values to the 0-1 range for stable training
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Normalized inputs help the network converge faster.
Q19. ImageNet is best known as:
A) A programming language
B) A large labeled image dataset used for training and benchmarking
C) A social network
D) A camera brand
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Many pre-trained CNNs (ResNet, VGG) are trained on it and reused through transfer
learning.


Q20. Mask R-CNN is mainly used for:
A) Text translation
B) Audio processing
C) Instance segmentation (boxes plus pixel masks)
D) Data cleaning
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It extends Faster R-CNN by adding a mask prediction branch.
Q21. U-Net is widely used in:
A) Biomedical image segmentation
B) Spam detection
C) Speech recognition
D) Stock prediction
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Its encoder-decoder structure with skip connections works well even with limited medical
data.
Q22. Why are CNNs preferred over fully connected networks for images?
A) They need no training
B) They ignore spatial information
C) They exploit local patterns and use far fewer parameters
D) They only work on text
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Local connectivity and weight sharing reduce parameters while preserving spatial structure.
Q23. A 100×100 color image (RGB) stored as 8-bit integers needs about how many bytes?
A) 10,000
B) 300,000
C) 3,000


D) 30,000
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: 100 × 100 × 3 channels × 1 byte = 30,000 bytes.
Q24. Two boxes each have an area of 100. They overlap in an area of 50. What is their IoU?
A) 1/3 (≈ 0.33)
B) 0.5
C) 0.25
D) 2/3
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Union = 100 + 100 − 50 = 150, so IoU = 50/150 = 1/3.
Q25. Which augmentation is risky for a digit-recognition task?
A) Slight brightness change
B) Small translation
C) Slight zoom
D) Rotating images by 180°
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: A 180° rotation can turn a 6 into a 9, which changes the label. Augmentations must
preserve the label.
Q26. The metric mAP (mean Average Precision) is mainly used to evaluate:
A) Clustering
B) Object detection models
C) Regression models
D) Language models
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It averages precision across recall levels and classes, using an IoU threshold to decide
correct detections.
Q27. Face detection differs from face recognition in that detection:


A) Identifies whose face it is
B) Matches faces to a database
C) Only locates faces in the image
D) Needs no image
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Detection answers "is there a face and where?". Recognition answers "whose face is it?".
Q28. A 3×3 Sobel filter applied to an image mainly computes:
A) Image gradients to highlight edges
B) A color histogram
C) Random noise
D) Image compression
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Sobel approximates the horizontal and vertical derivatives of intensity.
Q29. The "Faster R-CNN" is called a two-stage detector because:
A) It uses two datasets
B) It runs on two GPUs
C) It has two output classes
D) It first proposes regions, then classifies and refines them
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: A Region Proposal Network suggests candidate boxes, then a second stage classifies them.
This is usually more accurate but slower than YOLO.
Q30. Which technique helps a model recognize objects regardless of where they appear in the image?
A) Translation invariance via convolution and pooling
B) Dropping all pooling layers
C) Using only dense layers
D) Using a single filter
Correct Answer: A


Explanation: Shared filters and pooling make a CNN respond to a pattern wherever it appears.
TOPIC 15: BIG DATA ANALYTICS (INTRODUCTORY)
Q1. The three classic V's of Big Data are:
A) Volume, Velocity, Variety
B) Value, Vision, Version
C) Visual, Virtual, Valid
D) Vector, Variable, Verify
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Volume is the size of data, velocity the speed at which it arrives, and variety the different
formats.
Q2. Big Data refers to datasets that are:
A) Always stored in Excel
B) Only numeric
C) Too large or complex for traditional processing tools
D) Always unstructured
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: They need distributed storage and processing systems.
Q3. Apache Hadoop is:
A) A web browser
B) An image library
C) A database query language
D) A framework for distributed storage and processing of large datasets
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It spreads data and computation across clusters of commodity machines.


Q4. HDFS stands for:
A) High Data File System
B) Hadoop Distributed File System
C) Hybrid Data Format Standard
D) Hadoop Dynamic File Server
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: HDFS is Hadoop's storage layer. It splits files into blocks spread across nodes.
Q5. MapReduce is:
A) A storage format
B) A visualization tool
C) A programming model with a Map step and a Reduce step for parallel processing
D) A type of database
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Map transforms and filters data into key-value pairs. Reduce aggregates the results.
Q6. Apache Spark is known for:
A) Being slower than MapReduce
B) Fast in-memory distributed data processing
C) Being only a storage system
D) Working only on images
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Spark keeps intermediate data in memory, which makes it much faster than disk-based
MapReduce for many workloads.
Q7. Which of the following is structured data?
A) A table in a relational database
B) Video files
C) Audio recordings
D) Social media posts


Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Structured data fits a fixed schema of rows and columns.
Q8. Images, videos and free text are examples of:
A) Structured data
B) Metadata only
C) Unstructured data
D) Indexed data
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: They have no predefined tabular schema.
Q9. Which is a NoSQL database?
A) MySQL
B) PostgreSQL
C) Oracle SQL
D) MongoDB
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database. NoSQL systems handle flexible
schemas and scale horizontally.
Q10. The "Veracity" V in Big Data refers to:
A) Speed of data
B) Quality and trustworthiness of data
C) Size of data
D) Cost of data
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Big data can be noisy, biased or inconsistent, so its accuracy matters.
Q11. JSON and XML files are examples of:
A) Structured data


B) Unstructured data
C) Binary data
D) Semi-structured data
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: They have tags or keys that give some structure, but no rigid table schema.
Q12. ETL stands for:
A) Extract, Transform, Load
B) Evaluate, Test, Launch
C) Encode, Transfer, Link
D) Edit, Translate, Learn
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Data is pulled from sources, cleaned and reshaped, then loaded into a target such as a data
warehouse.
Q13. A data lake is mainly used to:
A) Store only cleaned tables
B) Store large amounts of raw data in its native format
C) Replace all databases
D) Run web servers
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It holds structured, semi-structured and unstructured data until it is needed.
Q14. Stream processing differs from batch processing because it:
A) Processes data in real time as it arrives
B) Processes data once a month
C) Cannot handle large data
D) Needs no computers
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Batch processes accumulated data in chunks. Streaming handles continuous data with low
latency.


Q15. Apache Kafka is mainly used as:
A) An image editor
B) A relational database
C) A distributed streaming platform for real-time data pipelines
D) A spreadsheet
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It publishes, stores and processes streams of events.
Q16. Apache Hive allows users to:
A) Train neural networks
B) Edit images
C) Encrypt files
D) Query data in Hadoop using SQL-like language (HiveQL)
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It makes big data in HDFS accessible to people who know SQL.
Q17. Horizontal scaling means:
A) Upgrading one server's CPU and RAM
B) Adding more machines to share the workload
C) Reducing data size
D) Using a bigger monitor
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Big data systems usually scale out. Vertical scaling (scaling up) improves a single machine.
Q18. The default replication factor in HDFS is:
A) 1
B) 2
C) 3
D) 5


Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Each block is stored on 3 nodes by default for fault tolerance.
Q19. In Spark, RDD stands for:
A) Random Data Directory
B) Relational Database Driver
C) Remote Data Download
D) Resilient Distributed Dataset
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It is a fault-tolerant collection of elements processed in parallel across a cluster.
Q20. In a data lake, "schema-on-read" means:
A) The schema is applied when data is read, not when it is stored
B) The schema is fixed before data is written
C) No data can be read
D) Data is stored without any files
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Data warehouses use schema-on-write. Data lakes use schema-on-read for flexibility.
Q21. Spark is generally faster than Hadoop MapReduce mainly because:
A) It uses fewer machines
B) It stores no data
C) It avoids writing intermediate results to disk by using in-memory processing
D) It works only on small data
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: MapReduce writes intermediate data to disk between stages, which is slow.
Q22. The fifth V, "Value", refers to:
A) The size of the data
B) The speed of data


C) The number of formats
D) The usefulness of insights extracted from data
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Data is only worth collecting if it produces useful decisions or outcomes.
Q23. The default HDFS block size in Hadoop 2.x and later is:
A) 128 MB
B) 4 KB
C) 1 GB
D) 64 KB
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Large blocks reduce metadata overhead and suit large sequential reads. Hadoop 1.x used 64
MB.
Q24. A 1 GB file is stored in HDFS with a replication factor of 3. The total raw storage used is about:
A) 1 GB
B) 2 GB
C) 3 GB
D) 128 MB
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Each of the blocks is stored 3 times, so 1 GB × 3 = 3 GB.
Q25. In HDFS, the NameNode stores:
A) The actual data blocks
B) Metadata about the file system (file names, block locations)
C) Only backups
D) User passwords
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: DataNodes store the actual blocks. The NameNode keeps the directory tree and the block
mapping.


Q26. Which of the following is NOT a NoSQL database type?
A) Document store
B) Key-value store
C) Relational table-based store
D) Graph database
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Relational databases use tables and SQL. The others are NoSQL types.
Q27. In Spark, which of these is an ACTION (triggers computation)?
A) map()
B) filter()
C) flatMap()
D) count()
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Transformations like map and filter are lazy. Actions like count(), collect() and take() make
Spark execute the job.
Q28. Sharding (partitioning) a database means:
A) Deleting old data
B) Encrypting the database
C) Splitting data across multiple servers or partitions
D) Copying data to one server
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It spreads data and load horizontally, which improves scalability and performance.
Q29. According to the CAP theorem, a distributed system can fully guarantee at most:
A) All three of Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance
B) Only one property
C) Two of the three properties at the same time
D) None of them


Correct Answer: C
Explanation: When a network partition happens, the system must trade off between consistency and
availability.
Q30. The Lambda architecture in big data combines:
A) Two databases only
B) A batch layer and a speed (real-time) layer
C) A CNN and an RNN
D) Hadoop and Excel
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: The batch layer gives accurate, complete views, and the speed layer gives low-latency
results on recent data. A serving layer merges them.
TOPIC 16: MODEL DEPLOYMENT & MLOPS BASICS
Q1. Model deployment means:
A) Making a trained model available in a production environment for real use
B) Collecting raw data
C) Cleaning the dataset
D) Choosing the loss function
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Deployment integrates the model into an application or service so users or systems can get
predictions.
Q2. MLOps is best described as:
A) A new type of neural network
B) A database language
C) A set of practices combining ML, DevOps and data engineering to manage the ML lifecycle
D) A GPU brand
Correct Answer: C


Explanation: It aims to automate and standardize building, deploying, monitoring and maintaining ML
models.
Q3. A common way to serve model predictions to other applications is through a:
A) Spreadsheet
B) Printed report
C) Screenshot
D) REST API
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: The client sends a request, usually JSON, over HTTP and the API returns the prediction.
Q4. Docker is used to:
A) Train neural networks faster
B) Package an application and its dependencies into a portable container
C) Label data
D) Visualize data
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Containers run the same way on any machine, which avoids "it works on my machine"
problems.
Q5. Which of the following Python frameworks is commonly used to build APIs for ML models?
A) Matplotlib
B) Seaborn
C) FastAPI
D) NLTK
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Flask and FastAPI are popular for wrapping models as web services.
Q6. Which library can be used to save (serialize) a trained scikit-learn model to a file?
A) joblib or pickle
B) Matplotlib


C) OpenCV
D) Seaborn
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: They save the trained model so it can be loaded later without retraining.
Q7. Model drift means:
A) The model file moved to another folder
B) The model gets faster over time
C) The dataset becomes smaller
D) Model performance degrades over time as real-world data changes
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Production data can shift away from the training data, so predictions become less accurate.
Q8. Git is used in MLOps primarily for:
A) Version control of code
B) Training models
C) Image processing
D) Data labeling
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: It tracks changes, supports collaboration and allows rollback of code.
Q9. CI/CD stands for:
A) Code Input / Code Display
B) Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery (or Deployment)
C) Central Intelligence / Central Data
D) Cloud Instance / Cloud Database
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It automates testing, building and releasing code and models.
Q10. Why is monitoring needed after deployment?


A) To delete the model
B) To increase file size
C) To avoid using APIs
D) To track performance, latency, errors and drift in production
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: A deployed model can fail silently, so monitoring catches problems early.
Q11. Concept drift occurs when:
A) The input data format changes
B) The relationship between the inputs and the target changes over time
C) The server crashes
D) The model file is corrupted
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: For example, customer behavior changes, so the same inputs now lead to different
outcomes. In data drift, only the input distribution changes.
Q12. Real-time (online) inference means:
A) Predictions are generated for a large dataset overnight
B) Predictions are made only once a year
C) Predictions are returned immediately for each individual request
D) The model trains continuously without data
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Batch inference scores many records at once on a schedule. Online inference responds per
request with low latency.
Q13. Kubernetes is mainly used for:
A) Orchestrating, scaling and managing containers
B) Data cleaning
C) Writing SQL
D) Plotting charts
Correct Answer: A


Explanation: It automates deployment, scaling and recovery of containerized applications.
Q14. MLflow is a tool for:
A) Image editing
B) Tracking experiments, packaging and managing models
C) Data entry
D) Spreadsheet formulas
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It logs parameters, metrics and artifacts, and has a model registry.
Q15. ONNX is:
A) A dataset
B) A programming language
C) An open format for exchanging models between different frameworks
D) A cloud provider
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: A model trained in PyTorch can be exported to ONNX and run in other runtimes.
Q16. A model registry is:
A) A list of dataset columns
B) A hardware inventory
C) A log of server errors
D) A central repository for storing and versioning trained models
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It tracks versions and stages (staging, production) of models.
Q17. A/B testing of models involves:
A) Comparing two model versions on live traffic to see which performs better
B) Training two models on the same laptop
C) Testing a model without data


D) Checking spelling
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Users are split between the old and new model, and metrics decide the winner.
Q18. In a canary deployment, the new model is:
A) Released to all users at once
B) Released first to a small portion of users before full rollout
C) Never released
D) Used only in training
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It limits the risk, since problems affect only a few users and can be fixed or rolled back.
Q19. Inference latency is:
A) The size of the model
B) The training time
C) The time taken to return a prediction
D) The number of features
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Low latency is important for real-time applications like fraud detection.
Q20. Training-serving skew refers to:
A) A mismatch between how data is processed in training and in production
B) A model that trains too slowly
C) A skewed distribution in the target only
D) A GPU error
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: If preprocessing differs between training and serving, predictions become unreliable.
Q21. Which situation most justifies retraining a model?
A) The server's color theme changes


B) The code has more comments
C) The model name changes
D) Monitoring shows performance dropping because of data drift
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Retraining on fresh data restores accuracy. Many pipelines trigger it automatically.
Q22. Edge deployment means running the model:
A) Only in a data center
B) On a local device like a phone or sensor, close to the data source
C) Only in a browser tab
D) Only on a supercomputer
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It reduces latency, saves bandwidth and can improve privacy.
Q23. In shadow deployment, the new model:
A) Replaces the old model immediately
B) Is shown to all users
C) Receives live requests but its predictions are not shown to users
D) Is deleted after testing
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Its outputs are logged and compared with the live model, so it can be tested safely on real
traffic.
Q24. What is the difference between a Docker image and a Docker container?
A) They are exactly the same
B) An image is a running instance and a container is a template
C) An image is a read-only template and a container is a running instance of it
D) An image is a database and a container is a file
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: You build an image once and can start many containers from it.


Q25. DVC (Data Version Control) is used to:
A) Version datasets and models alongside code
B) Draw charts
C) Encrypt data
D) Label images automatically
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Git is not suited for large files, so DVC tracks data versions and keeps experiments
reproducible.
Q26. Which practice BEST supports reproducibility of ML experiments?
A) Not recording parameters
B) Changing data without notes
C) Using different libraries each time
D) Versioning code, data and environment, and fixing random seeds
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: This lets someone re-run the experiment and get the same result.
Q27. Quantization is a model optimization technique that:
A) Increases the number of layers
B) Reduces the precision of weights (e.g. 32-bit to 8-bit) to shrink the model and speed up inference
C) Adds more training data
D) Removes all activation functions
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: It lowers memory and compute needs, which is helpful for mobile and edge devices, with
small accuracy loss.
Q28. A feature store is used to:
A) Store only trained models
B) Store user passwords
C) Provide consistent, reusable features for both training and serving


D) Store server logs
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It reduces training-serving skew and avoids teams recomputing the same features.
Q29. A new model was deployed and users report bad predictions. The safest immediate action is to:
A) Delete all logs
B) Ignore it until next month
C) Retrain from scratch immediately
D) Roll back to the previous stable model version
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Rollback restores service quickly. Then the issue can be investigated without affecting
users.
Q30. A model scored 95% accuracy in testing. After three months in production with no code changes,
accuracy falls to 78%. The MOST likely cause is:
A) Data or concept drift
B) A bug in the Python interpreter
C) The model forgot its weights
D) Too many CPU cores
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The code and model are unchanged, so the real-world data or its relationship to the target
most likely changed. This is why monitoring and retraining matter.
TOPIC 17: AI ETHICS, SECURITY & PRIVACY
Q1. Bias in AI refers to:
A) Faster computation
B) Systematic and unfair outcomes that favor or disadvantage certain groups
C) A type of activation function
D) Random errors only


Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Bias can come from the data, the algorithm design or how the model is used.
Q2. Which of the following is a main source of bias in AI systems?
A) Using Python
B) Writing comments in code
C) Unrepresentative or skewed training data
D) Using a GPU
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: If the training data reflects historical prejudice or misses certain groups, the model learns
the same bias.
Q3. Explainability in AI means:
A) Making the model larger
B) Hiding model decisions
C) Reducing training time
D) Being able to understand and explain why a model made a decision
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It builds trust and helps detect errors and bias, and is vital in areas like healthcare and
finance.
Q4. GDPR is a regulation about:
A) Data protection and privacy in the European Union
B) Internet speed
C) Hardware standards
D) Programming languages
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: It gives individuals rights over their personal data and sets rules for organizations that
process it.
Q5. PII stands for:


A) Public Internet Information
B) Personally Identifiable Information
C) Private Index Interface
D) Program Input Instruction
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Examples include name, national ID number, phone number, address and email.
Q6. Anonymization of data means:
A) Encrypting a file with a password
B) Making data larger
C) Removing or altering identifiers so individuals cannot be identified
D) Deleting the whole database
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Properly anonymized data cannot be traced back to a person.
Q7. An adversarial attack on a model typically involves:
A) Physically damaging the server
B) Deleting the training data
C) Slowing down the network
D) Adding small, crafted perturbations to inputs to cause wrong predictions
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: A tiny, nearly invisible change to an image can make a classifier give the wrong label.
Q8. Data poisoning is an attack where:
A) Malicious data is injected into the training set to corrupt the model
B) The model is copied
C) Servers are overheated
D) The data is encrypted
Correct Answer: A


Explanation: The attacker manipulates the training data so the model learns wrong or backdoored
behavior.
Q9. LIME and SHAP are tools used for:
A) Data storage
B) Explaining individual model predictions (Explainable AI)
C) Image resizing
D) Clustering
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: They show how much each feature contributed to a prediction.
Q10. Deepfakes are:
A) Encrypted files
B) Slow models
C) AI-generated or manipulated synthetic media that appears real
D) Backup copies
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: They can be used for misinformation, fraud and harassment, which raises serious ethical
concerns.
Q11. Differential privacy works by:
A) Removing all data
B) Making models larger
C) Using only public data
D) Adding calibrated noise so individual records cannot be identified
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Query results or model updates are slightly randomized, so the presence of any one person
cannot be inferred.
Q12. Federated learning allows:
A) Training a model across many devices without sharing their raw data


B) Collecting all user data in one server
C) Training without any model
D) Selling user data
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Only model updates are sent to a central server, which improves privacy.
Q13. Sampling bias occurs when:
A) The model is too deep
B) The training data does not represent the real population
C) The learning rate is high
D) The dataset is too large
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: For example, a face dataset with mostly one skin tone leads to poor performance on others.
Q14. A membership inference attack tries to find out:
A) The model's accuracy
B) The server's IP
C) Whether a specific record was part of the model's training data
D) The number of layers
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It exploits differences in model behavior on training vs unseen data, and it is a privacy risk.
Q15. Accountability in AI means:
A) The model is never wrong
B) The AI is legally a person
C) Developers can ignore errors
D) There are clear responsibilities for the outcomes of AI systems
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Humans and organizations remain responsible for AI decisions and their consequences.


Q16. Informed consent in data collection means:
A) Collecting data secretly
B) People agree to data use after being told clearly how their data will be used
C) Using data without asking if it's public
D) Collecting more data than needed
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Consent should be voluntary, specific and based on clear information.
Q17. The data minimization principle says to:
A) Collect only the data that is necessary for the stated purpose
B) Collect as much data as possible
C) Keep data forever
D) Share data freely
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Collecting less data reduces privacy risk and the impact of any breach.
Q18. A "black box" model is one whose:
A) Color is black
B) Training is fast
C) Internal decision process is hard to interpret
D) Data is public
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Deep neural networks are often black boxes. Linear models and small trees are more
interpretable.
Q19. A hiring model trained on past company data rejects more women applicants. This is an example of:
A) Overfitting only
B) Algorithmic bias inherited from historical data
C) Underfitting
D) Data compression


Correct Answer: B
Explanation: The model learned past discrimination patterns from the data and reproduced them.
Q20. The "right to erasure" ("right to be forgotten") allows individuals to:
A) Delete any website
B) Remove all AI models
C) Change their name
D) Request deletion of their personal data under certain conditions
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It is part of GDPR (Article 17). Organizations must erase the data when valid grounds
apply.
Q21. Protecting data both "at rest" and "in transit" is mainly achieved by:
A) Encryption
B) Compression
C) Normalization
D) Augmentation
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: Encryption keeps data unreadable to unauthorized parties, whether stored or being
transmitted.
Q22. Prompt injection is a security threat to:
A) Spreadsheets
B) Network cables
C) Large language model applications
D) Image printers
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: An attacker hides instructions in the input so the model ignores its original instructions or
leaks data.


Q23. Is removing a sensitive attribute (e.g. gender or religion) from the dataset enough to guarantee a fair
model?
A) Yes, always
B) Yes, because the model cannot see it
C) Only for deep learning
D) No, other correlated features can act as proxies and still produce bias
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Features like postal code, name or school can correlate with the sensitive attribute and
reintroduce bias. This is called "fairness through unawareness" and it often fails.
Q24. A model extraction (model stealing) attack aims to:
A) Replicate a model's behavior by repeatedly querying its API
B) Delete the model
C) Improve the model's accuracy
D) Encrypt the model
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: The attacker uses input-output pairs to train a copy, which threatens intellectual property.
Q25. A "hallucination" in a generative AI model refers to:
A) Slow response time
B) A hardware error
C) Output that is confident and fluent but factually wrong or made up
D) A training crash
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: It is a risk in LLMs, so important outputs should be verified.
Q26. How do pseudonymized and anonymized data differ?
A) They are the same thing
B) Pseudonymized data can be re-identified with additional information and is still personal data under
GDPR
C) Anonymized data can always be re-identified


D) Pseudonymized data is always public
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Pseudonymization replaces identifiers with codes, but a key or extra data can link them
back. True anonymization is irreversible.
Q27. An "evasion attack" happens:
A) During data collection
B) During model training
C) During model inference/prediction time
D) During data labeling
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: The attacker alters inputs at prediction time to avoid detection or cause misclassification.
Poisoning happens at training time.
Q28. "Human-in-the-loop" means:
A) Humans are removed from the process
B) AI works completely alone
C) Only machines review the data
D) Humans oversee, review or can override AI decisions
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: It is important in high-stakes decisions like medical, legal and lending.
Q29. Demographic parity as a fairness metric requires that:
A) The positive prediction rate is the same across different groups
B) The model has 100% accuracy
C) All groups have different outcomes
D) Only one group is evaluated
Correct Answer: A
Explanation: For example, loan approval rates should be equal across gender or ethnic groups. Other
metrics include equalized odds.


Q30. A face recognition model has 97% overall accuracy, but only 70% accuracy on one minority group.
What does this show?
A) The model is perfectly fair
B) Overall accuracy is enough to judge fairness
C) The minority group should be removed from testing
D) Performance must be evaluated per group, because a high average can hide unfair results
Correct Answer: D
Explanation: Disaggregated evaluation exposes bias that aggregate metrics hide. The fix includes more
representative data and fairness testing.
Subject: Computer Networks and Cloud Computing
TOPIC 1: Data Communication
1. [Direct] What is data communication?
A) Exchange of data between devices
B) Creating computer hardware
C) Printing documents only
D) Storing data without transfer
Correct Answer: A) Exchange of data between devices
2. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university lab is diagnosing a problem in how information travels between two
computers. Which component is the actual information being sent?
A) Protocol
B) Message
C) Medium
D) Receiver
Correct Answer: B) Message
3. [Direct] Which component sends the data?
A) Sender
B) Receiver
C) Medium
D) Protocol
Correct Answer: A) Sender
4. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is selecting a suitable communication method for sending data between
offices. Which component receives the data?
A) Sender
B) Encoder
C) Receiver
D) Router
Correct Answer: C) Receiver
5. [Direct] What carries data from sender to receiver?
A) Operating system
B) Transmission medium
C) Compiler
D) Database
Correct Answer: B) Transmission medium
6. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A technician is checking signal quality on a link used for video meetings. What is a
protocol?
A) A physical cable
B) A set of communication rules
C) A storage device
D) A type of monitor
Correct Answer: B) A set of communication rules
7. [Direct] Which is an example of guided media?
A) Radio waves
B) Microwaves
C) Twisted-pair cable
D) Infrared through air
Correct Answer: C) Twisted-pair cable
8. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network team is reviewing how digital information is encoded and transmitted. Which
is an example of unguided media?
A) Coaxial cable
B) Fiber-optic cable
C) Twisted-pair cable
D) Radio waves
Correct Answer: D) Radio waves
9. [Direct] Which mode allows communication in both directions, but not at the same time?
A) Simplex
B) Half-duplex
C) Full-duplex
D) Multiplex
Correct Answer: B) Half-duplex
10. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A communication link is experiencing delay and inconsistent delivery times. Which
mode allows simultaneous two-way communication?
A) Simplex
B) Half-duplex
C) Full-duplex
D) Broadcast only
Correct Answer: C) Full-duplex
11. [Direct] A keyboard sending data to a computer is commonly an example of:
A) Simplex communication
B) Full-duplex only
C) No communication
D) Routing
Correct Answer: A) Simplex communication
12. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university lab is diagnosing a problem in how information travels between two
computers. What does bandwidth generally describe?
A) Storage capacity
B) Data-carrying capacity of a link
C) Screen resolution
D) CPU temperature
Correct Answer: B) Data-carrying capacity of a link
13. [Direct] What is latency?
A) Delay in data delivery
B) Number of users
C) File size
D) Cable color
Correct Answer: A) Delay in data delivery
14. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is selecting a suitable communication method for sending data between
offices. What is noise in data communication?
A) Unwanted signal interference
B) A type of protocol
C) A receiver address
D) A data format
Correct Answer: A) Unwanted signal interference
15. [Direct] Which transmission type sends bits one after another over a channel?
A) Parallel
B) Serial
C) Optical only
D) Analog only
Correct Answer: B) Serial
16. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A technician is checking signal quality on a link used for video meetings. Which signal
varies continuously over time?
A) Digital signal
B) Analog signal
C) Binary file
D) Packet header
Correct Answer: B) Analog signal
17. [Direct] Which signal uses discrete values such as 0 and 1?
A) Analog
B) Digital
C) Acoustic only
D) Continuous only
Correct Answer: B) Digital
18. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network team is reviewing how digital information is encoded and transmitted. What
is attenuation?
A) Signal weakening over distance
B) Signal encryption
C) Data compression
D) Address translation
Correct Answer: A) Signal weakening over distance
19. [Direct] What is the purpose of error detection?
A) To make data larger
B) To identify corrupted data
C) To assign IP addresses
D) To increase screen brightness
Correct Answer: B) To identify corrupted data
20. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A communication link is experiencing delay and inconsistent delivery times. Which
measure is commonly used for data rate?
A) Bits per second
B) Pixels per inch
C) Liters per second
D) Degrees Celsius
Correct Answer: A) Bits per second
21. [Direct] Which characteristic means data arrives in the same order it was sent?
A) Routing
B) Color
C) Delivery
D) Compression
Correct Answer: C) Delivery
22. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university lab is diagnosing a problem in how information travels between two
computers. Which characteristic means data reaches the intended destination?
A) Modulation
B) Delivery
C) Sampling
D) Encryption
Correct Answer: B) Delivery
23. [Direct] Which characteristic means data arrives without corruption?
A) Accuracy
B) Availability
C) Topology
D) Addressing
Correct Answer: A) Accuracy
24. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is selecting a suitable communication method for sending data between
offices. Which characteristic means data arrives within an acceptable time?
A) Timeliness
B) Duplexing
C) Encoding
D) Framing
Correct Answer: A) Timeliness
25. [Direct] What is propagation delay?
A) Time to write a program
B) Time to encrypt a file
C) Time to assign a username
D) Time for a signal to travel through a medium
Correct Answer: D) Time for a signal to travel through a medium
26. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A technician is checking signal quality on a link used for video meetings. What is
transmission delay mainly affected by?
A) Packet size and link data rate
B) Keyboard layout
C) File name
D) Screen size
Correct Answer: A) Packet size and link data rate
27. [Direct] What is jitter?
A) A fixed IP address
B) Variation in packet delay
C) Signal encryption
D) Cable labeling
Correct Answer: B) Variation in packet delay
28. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network team is reviewing how digital information is encoded and transmitted. What
is throughput?
A) Number of screens
B) Signal color
C) Theoretical cable length
D) Actual rate of successful data transfer
Correct Answer: D) Actual rate of successful data transfer
29. [Direct] What is a baud rate a measure of?
A) Bytes stored on disk
B) Number of users
C) Packets lost per hour
D) Signal symbols transmitted per second
Correct Answer: D) Signal symbols transmitted per second
30. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A communication link is experiencing delay and inconsistent delivery times. What is bit
rate?
A) Bits transmitted per second
B) CPU clock cycles only
C) Symbols per minute only
D) Cable weight
Correct Answer: A) Bits transmitted per second
31. [Direct] What is modulation?
A) Changing a carrier signal to represent information
B) Routing a packet
C) Deleting duplicate files
D) Assigning a MAC address
Correct Answer: A) Changing a carrier signal to represent information
32. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university lab is diagnosing a problem in how information travels between two
computers. What is demodulation?
A) Splitting a network into subnets
B) Compressing a document
C) Recovering information from a modulated carrier
D) Making a signal weaker
Correct Answer: C) Recovering information from a modulated carrier
33. [Direct] What is multiplexing used for?
A) Sharing one communication channel among multiple signals
B) Replacing a receiver
C) Removing all protocols
D) Changing a password
Correct Answer: A) Sharing one communication channel among multiple signals
34. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is selecting a suitable communication method for sending data between
offices. What does FDM separate?
A) Signals by frequency bands
B) Frames by color
C) Signals by user names
D) Packets by file type
Correct Answer: A) Signals by frequency bands
35. [Direct] What does TDM allocate to signals?
A) Different passwords
B) Different file extensions
C) Different time slots
D) Different screen sizes
Correct Answer: C) Different time slots
36. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A technician is checking signal quality on a link used for video meetings. What is WDM
commonly used with?
A) Optical fiber wavelengths
B) IP port numbers
C) Keyboard signals
D) Copper wire voltage only
Correct Answer: A) Optical fiber wavelengths
37. [Direct] What is simplex communication?
A) Two-way alternate communication
B) One-way communication only
C) Two-way simultaneous communication
D) Communication without a sender
Correct Answer: B) One-way communication only
38. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network team is reviewing how digital information is encoded and transmitted. What
is an example of half-duplex communication?
A) Walkie-talkie communication
B) A normal full-duplex phone call
C) A file stored offline
D) A one-way broadcast only
Correct Answer: A) Walkie-talkie communication
39. [Direct] What is an example of full-duplex communication?
A) A disconnected cable
B) A one-way TV broadcast
C) A two-way call where both sides can speak simultaneously
D) A walkie-talkie turn-taking exchange
Correct Answer: C) A two-way call where both sides can speak simultaneously
40. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A communication link is experiencing delay and inconsistent delivery times. What is a
repeater used for in communication?
A) Regenerating or repeating a signal
B) Choosing a domain name
C) Encrypting an email
D) Assigning user permissions
Correct Answer: A) Regenerating or repeating a signal
41. [Direct] What is the purpose of a codec?
A) Managing MAC tables
B) Finding a route between IP networks
C) Providing cloud billing
D) Encoding and decoding audio or video data
Correct Answer: D) Encoding and decoding audio or video data
42. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university lab is diagnosing a problem in how information travels between two
computers. What is sampling in analog-to-digital conversion?
A) Choosing a Wi-Fi password
B) Changing a URL
C) Sending packets to all hosts
D) Measuring a signal at discrete time intervals
Correct Answer: D) Measuring a signal at discrete time intervals
43. [Direct] What does quantization do?
A) Selects a router path
B) Maps sampled values to discrete levels
C) Assigns ports to applications
D) Adds a domain suffix
Correct Answer: B) Maps sampled values to discrete levels
44. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is selecting a suitable communication method for sending data between
offices. What is line coding?
A) Filtering web traffic
B) Converting a domain name to an IP address
C) Creating a cloud account
D) Representing digital data as digital signal patterns
Correct Answer: D) Representing digital data as digital signal patterns
45. [Direct] What is a common purpose of error correction?
A) Changing network topology
B) Recovering data despite certain transmission errors
C) Assigning a port number
D) Increasing cable length without limit
Correct Answer: B) Recovering data despite certain transmission errors
46. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A technician is checking signal quality on a link used for video meetings. What is parity
commonly used for?
A) Routing packets
B) Wireless authentication only
C) Simple error detection
D) Increasing throughput automatically
Correct Answer: C) Simple error detection
47. [Direct] What is a checksum used for?
A) Detecting certain data errors
B) Resolving a domain name
C) Selecting a radio channel
D) Creating an email account
Correct Answer: A) Detecting certain data errors
48. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network team is reviewing how digital information is encoded and transmitted. What
is a transmission medium?
A) The receiver's password
B) The application window
C) The path through which a signal travels
D) The message's meaning
Correct Answer: C) The path through which a signal travels
49. [Direct] What is a common advantage of fiber-optic cable?
A) It always costs less than every cable
B) It carries data only a few centimeters
C) It needs no installation
D) High capacity and resistance to electromagnetic interference
Correct Answer: D) High capacity and resistance to electromagnetic interference
50. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A communication link is experiencing delay and inconsistent delivery times. What is
crosstalk?
A) Unwanted signal coupling between nearby channels or wires
B) A routing protocol
C) A type of IP address
D) A method of encryption
Correct Answer: A) Unwanted signal coupling between nearby channels or wires


TOPIC 2: Computer Networks
1. [Direct] What is a computer network?
A) Connected devices that exchange data
B) A single offline calculator
C) A text editor
D) A type of battery
Correct Answer: A) Connected devices that exchange data
2. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A small business is designing a network for its staff, printers, and servers. Which
network usually covers a small area such as a room or building?
A) WAN
B) LAN
C) MAN
D) GAN
Correct Answer: B) LAN
3. [Direct] Which network typically covers a large geographical area?
A) PAN
B) LAN
C) WAN
D) CAN only
Correct Answer: C) WAN
4. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network administrator is troubleshooting connectivity between devices in an office.
What does PAN stand for?
A) Personal Area Network
B) Public Access Node
C) Private Analog Network
D) Packet Address Number
Correct Answer: A) Personal Area Network
5. [Direct] What does MAN stand for?
A) Main Access Network
B) Metropolitan Area Network
C) Multiple Analog Node
D) Managed Application Network

6. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university is planning a reliable network for several buildings. Which device forwards
packets between different networks?
A) Router
B) Keyboard
C) Scanner
D) Repeater only

7. [Direct] Which device commonly connects devices within a LAN and forwards frames using MAC addresses?
A) Switch
B) Modem only
C) Printer

Correct Answer: A) Switch
8. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is choosing how to organize shared resources and network services. What

9. [Direct] Which topology connects all devices to a central device?

11. [Direct] Which topology uses a single main backbone cable?

12. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A small business is designing a network for its staff, printers, and servers. What is a

Correct Answer: A) Rules for data exchange
13. [Direct] Which model has seven layers?

14. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network administrator is troubleshooting connectivity between devices in an office.

15. [Direct] Which address identifies a network interface at the data-link layer?

16. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university is planning a reliable network for several buildings. What is a server in a

17. [Direct] What is a client?

18. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is choosing how to organize shared resources and network services. What

A) Potential data transfer capacity

19. [Direct] What is packet switching?

B) Sending only continuous voice waves

20. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A technician is documenting the structure and performance of a local network. Which

21. [Direct] What is a node in a network?

22. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A small business is designing a network for its staff, printers, and servers. What is a

A) A network with one mandatory central server for all services

C) A network used only for television

23. [Direct] What is a client-server network?

24. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network administrator is troubleshooting connectivity between devices in an office.
What is an intranet?
A) A public DNS root server
B) A type of fiber connector
C) A private network used within an organization
D) The entire public Internet
Correct Answer: C) A private network used within an organization
25. [Direct] What is an extranet?
A) A type of CPU
B) A disconnected computer
C) A network with no security
D) A controlled private network that gives selected outsiders access
Correct Answer: D) A controlled private network that gives selected outsiders access
26. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A university is planning a reliable network for several buildings. What is network
architecture?
A) A data compression algorithm
B) The design and organization of a network
C) The design of a keyboard
D) A monitor setting
Correct Answer: B) The design and organization of a network
27. [Direct] Which topology provides multiple paths between nodes?
A) Mesh topology
B) Linear chain with no alternatives
C) Bus topology only
D) Single-link topology
Correct Answer: A) Mesh topology
28. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A company is choosing how to organize shared resources and network services. What

A) Avoiding all orchestration

C) Naming the monitor
D) Removing IP addressing
Correct Answer: B) Maintaining isolation, performance, and resource management between slices
45. [Direct] What is deterministic networking designed to provide?
A) No network configuration
B) Only best-effort email
C) Unlimited bandwidth at no cost
D) Predictable latency and delivery characteristics for supported traffic
Correct Answer: D) Predictable latency and delivery characteristics for supported traffic
46. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A network team is virtualizing network functions instead of relying only on dedicated
hardware. What is TSN commonly associated with?
A) Time Server Naming
B) Time-Sensitive Networking for predictable Ethernet delivery
C) Terminal Signal Noise
D) Transport Security Numbering
Correct Answer: B) Time-Sensitive Networking for predictable Ethernet delivery
47. [Direct] What is IPv6 important for next-generation networks?
A) Replacing all physical links
B) Providing a vastly larger address space than IPv4
C) Guaranteeing zero latency
D) Eliminating routing
Correct Answer: B) Providing a vastly larger address space than IPv4
48. [Scenario-based] Scenario: An administrator is using telemetry to improve network performance automatically.
What is an API used for in network automation?
A) Allowing software tools to exchange commands and information
B) Physically amplifying a radio signal
C) Replacing every network protocol
D) Changing a cable's category
Correct Answer: A) Allowing software tools to exchange commands and information
49. [Direct] What is telemetry useful for in automated networks?
A) Hiding network performance
B) Providing measurements and events for visibility and decisions
C) Creating passwords
D) Disabling all alerts
Correct Answer: B) Providing measurements and events for visibility and decisions
50. [Scenario-based] Scenario: A service provider is designing a programmable, scalable network infrastructure. What
is a major design goal for next-generation networks?
A) Removing monitoring and automation
B) Using only obsolete hardware
C) Scalability, programmability, resilience, and secure service delivery
D) Limiting all traffic to one application
Correct Answer: C) Scalability, programmability, resilience, and secure service delivery

14. Database Security
1. Database security aims to protect:
A. Confidentiality, integrity and availability
B. Only screen colors
C. Only query length
D. Only table names
2. Authentication verifies:
A. Who a user is
B. What a query costs
C. Where a table is stored
D. How rows are sorted
3. Authorization determines:
A. What an authenticated user may do
B. The user's identity only
C. The query's syntax
D. The backup size
4. The principle of least privilege grants:
A. Only permissions needed for a task
B. Every user administrator rights
C. No access to anyone
D. Unlimited privileges permanently
5. GRANT is used to:
A. Assign privileges
B. Remove a row
C. Restore a backup
D. Create an index only
6. REVOKE is used to:
A. Withdraw privileges
B. Insert data
C. Sort a table
D. Commit a transaction
7. Encryption at rest protects:
A. Stored data on media
B. Only data typed into a form
C. Only query syntax
D. Only public table names
8. Encryption in transit protects data:
A. While moving between systems
B. Only while printed
C. Only after deletion
D. Only in a schema diagram
9. SQL injection can be reduced by:
A. Parameterized queries and safe input handling
B. String concatenation with all user input
C. Giving all users admin access
D. Disabling constraints
10. A database audit trail records:
A. Relevant activities for review
B. Only table colors
C. Only disk capacity
D. Only query comments
11. Multi-factor authentication uses:
A. Two or more different authentication factors
B. Two usernames only
C. One password repeated
D. No identity check
12. A role is commonly used to:
A. Group privileges for assignment
B. Store a query result
C. Replace every table
D. Encrypt a column automatically
13. A backup should be protected because it:
A. May contain sensitive database information
B. Never contains real data
C. Cannot be stolen
D. Has no access controls
14. Data masking helps:
A. Hide or replace sensitive values in selected contexts
B. Increase every user's privileges
C. Remove all keys
D. Guarantee no data leak
15. A security patch is intended to:
A. Fix known vulnerabilities or defects
B. Add duplicate records
C. Remove authentication
D. Disable all logs
16. A firewall can help:
A. Restrict network traffic to permitted rules
B. Normalize every table
C. Replace encryption
D. Guarantee correct SQL results
17. A strong password should generally be:
A. Hard to guess and unique
B. Shared with classmates
C. The same on every service
D. A public username
18. Data classification helps determine:
A. Required handling and protection
B. The query's join order only
C. The monitor model
D. The table's row count
19. A privilege escalation occurs when:
A. A user gains permissions beyond those intended
B. A query returns zero rows

B. Round Robin

B. 5 ms
C. 4 ms
D. 9 ms
Q86. Using the same FCFS order and burst times in Q85, what is P2's waiting time?
A. 7 ms
B. 4 ms
C. 2 ms
D. 0 ms

B. P3
C. P2
D. All run simultaneously

Q89. What is starvation in CPU scheduling?

Q90. Which technique can help reduce starvation in priority scheduling?
A. Increasing every process's burst time

Q91. What is preemptive scheduling?

Q93. What is throughput in CPU scheduling?

C. Total memory installed
D. Time spent booting the computer
Q94. What is a context-switch overhead?

Q95. If a Round Robin time quantum is extremely large, its behavior tends to approach which algorithm, assuming the same ready-queue order?

C. FCFS
D. Shortest remaining time
Q96. Which scheduling policy is commonly suitable for interactive time-sharing systems?

C. Frequent context switches can add overhead
D. It removes the need for scheduling
Q100. Which statement about CPU scheduling is correct?
A. One algorithm is always best for every system
B. Scheduling has no effect on response time
C. Scheduling is used only for disk drives
D. Different scheduling algorithms optimize different performance goals

Subject : DATA STRUCTURES & ALGORITHMS
1. Foundations of Data Structures and Algorithms
Choose the best answer. The correct option and a brief explanation follow each question.
1. Which option best describes a data structure?
A. A way to organize and store data for efficient use
B. A file format used only for images
C. A device used to connect computers
D. A programming language syntax rule
Correct answer: A. A way to organize and store data for efficient use
Explanation: A data structure organizes data so operations such as access, update, and search can be performed effectively.
2. What is an algorithm?
A. A computer's physical memory
B. A collection of unrelated statements
C. A finite sequence of steps to solve a problem
D. A programming language compiler
Correct answer: C. A finite sequence of steps to solve a problem
Explanation: An algorithm gives ordered steps that transform input into a desired result.
3. In an algorithm, what is input?
A. Data supplied to the algorithm
B. A syntax error
C. The time taken by the CPU
D. The final result only
Correct answer: A. Data supplied to the algorithm
Explanation: Input is the data an algorithm receives before processing.
4. What is output in an algorithm?
A. The result produced after processing
B. The storage device
C. The source-code comment
D. The data supplied at the beginning
Correct answer: A. The result produced after processing
Explanation: Output is the information produced by executing the algorithm.
5. Which property means an algorithm must eventually stop?
A. Randomness
B. Inheritance
C. Ambiguity
D. Finiteness
Correct answer: D. Finiteness
Explanation: Finiteness requires a solution procedure to finish after a finite number of steps.
6. Which algorithm property requires every step to be clear?
A. Encryption
B. Concurrency
C. Definiteness
D. Compression
Correct answer: C. Definiteness
Explanation: Definiteness means each instruction is precise and unambiguous.
7. What does effectiveness mean for an algorithm?
A. It must be written in Java
B. Every step must use a network
C. Each step is basic enough to be carried out
D. It must have zero memory use
Correct answer: C. Each step is basic enough to be carried out
Explanation: Effective steps are feasible and can be performed exactly in practice.
8. An algorithm is correct when it:
A. Has no input
B. Uses the fewest lines of code
C. Produces the expected result for valid inputs
D. Runs only on one computer
Correct answer: C. Produces the expected result for valid inputs
Explanation: Correctness concerns whether the algorithm solves the specified problem.
9. Why is pseudocode used?
A. To execute directly as machine code
B. To replace all testing
C. To describe logic without strict programming-language syntax
D. To store database records
Correct answer: C. To describe logic without strict programming-language syntax
Explanation: Pseudocode is language-independent and helps plan the algorithm.
10. Which symbol commonly represents a decision in a flowchart?
A. Diamond
B. Parallelogram
C. Oval
D. Cylinder
Correct answer: A. Diamond
Explanation: A diamond represents a decision or condition with branches.
11. What is a variable?
A. A type of graph edge
B. A sorting method
C. A named location or reference for a value
D. A loop that never ends
Correct answer: C. A named location or reference for a value
Explanation: Variables let a program refer to data that may change.
12. A constant is a value that:
A. Does not change during the relevant execution
B. Can never be read
C. Must be a string
D. Changes after every loop
Correct answer: A. Does not change during the relevant execution
Explanation: Constants represent fixed values in a program or algorithm.
13. What does an Abstract Data Type (ADT) define?
A. A CPU scheduling order
B. The values and operations, not their implementation details
C. A particular memory address
D. Only the color of a user interface
Correct answer: B. The values and operations, not their implementation details
Explanation: An ADT specifies behavior and supported operations while hiding implementation.
14. In data abstraction, implementation details are:
A. Hidden behind a defined interface
B. Always printed to the user
C. Required to be duplicated
D. Converted into graph edges
Correct answer: A. Hidden behind a defined interface
Explanation: Abstraction separates what an operation does from how it is implemented.
15. Time complexity describes how:
A. Many users can log in
B. Large a monitor is
C. Bright a screen becomes
D. Running time grows as input size grows
Correct answer: D. Running time grows as input size grows
Explanation: Time complexity studies growth in operation count as input size increases.
16. Space complexity measures:
A. Only the number of output characters
B. The internet speed
C. The physical width of a computer
D. Memory used as a function of input size
Correct answer: D. Memory used as a function of input size
Explanation: Space complexity includes memory required during algorithm execution.
17. Big O notation usually expresses an asymptotic:
A. Upper bound on growth
B. Exact runtime in seconds
C. Hardware price
D. Lower bound only
Correct answer: A. Upper bound on growth
Explanation: Big O is commonly used to describe an asymptotic upper bound.
18. Big Omega notation expresses an asymptotic:
A. Upper bound only
B. Average disk size
C. Exact number of lines
D. Lower bound on growth
Correct answer: D. Lower bound on growth
Explanation: Omega describes a lower bound on growth.
19. Big Theta notation describes a:
A. Programming error
B. Memory address
C. Random input value
D. Tight asymptotic bound
Correct answer: D. Tight asymptotic bound
Explanation: Theta applies when matching upper and lower asymptotic bounds hold.
20. Which complexity is commonly written O(1)?
A. Linear time
B. Exponential time
C. Constant time
D. Quadratic time
Correct answer: C. Constant time
Explanation: O(1) means the operation count does not grow with input size.
21. An algorithm that checks every element once is commonly:
A. O(n)
B. O(1)
C. O(log n)
D. O(n²)
Correct answer: A. O(n)
Explanation: A single pass through n elements performs work proportional to n.
22. Two full nested loops each running n times often give:
A. O(log n)
B. O(1)
C. O(n²)
D. O(n)
Correct answer: C. O(n²)
Explanation: The inner loop runs about n times for each of n outer-loop iterations.
23. Repeatedly halving the remaining search range often gives:
A. O(n²)
B. O(2ⁿ)
C. O(log n)
D. O(n)
Correct answer: C. O(log n)
Explanation: Halving the problem size each step leads to logarithmic growth.
24. Best-case complexity describes:
A. The greatest work for all inputs
B. The code's file size
C. The average memory price
D. The least work for an input of size n
Correct answer: D. The least work for an input of size n
Explanation: Best case considers the most favorable input arrangement.
25. Worst-case complexity describes:
A. The maximum work for an input size under consideration
B. The fastest possible hardware
C. The average of all cases
D. Only the first test case
Correct answer: A. The maximum work for an input size under consideration
Explanation: Worst-case analysis gives an upper bound on work for inputs of a given size.
26. Average-case analysis estimates:
A. Only the number of variables
B. Work on the largest input only
C. A guaranteed exact time for every run
D. Expected work over a stated input distribution
Correct answer: D. Expected work over a stated input distribution
Explanation: Average-case results depend on assumptions about likely inputs.
27. A recursive function is one that:
A. Uses no memory
B. Calls itself directly or indirectly
C. Can only sort arrays
D. Never returns
Correct answer: B. Calls itself directly or indirectly
Explanation: Recursion solves a problem by calling the same procedure on smaller instances.
28. Why is a base case needed in recursion?
A. To stop recursive calls
B. To avoid returning a value
C. To increase the array size
D. To sort the input automatically
Correct answer: A. To stop recursive calls
Explanation: A base case provides a stopping condition and prevents endless recursion.
29. Recursive calls are commonly tracked using the:
A. Graph matrix only
B. Printer queue
C. Call stack
D. Hash table only
Correct answer: C. Call stack
Explanation: Each active call has execution information stored in a stack frame.
30. Iteration repeats work using:
A. Loops or repeated steps
B. Only hash collisions
C. Only self-calls
D. Only tree rotations
Correct answer: A. Loops or repeated steps
Explanation: Loops are a common way to repeat instructions.
31. A loop invariant is a condition that:
A. Always makes a loop infinite
B. Must be false at the end
C. Only applies to graphics
D. Remains true at a defined point in each loop iteration
Correct answer: D. Remains true at a defined point in each loop iteration
Explanation: Loop invariants help reason about the correctness of iterative algorithms.
32. Divide and conquer generally means:
A. Store every value in one variable
B. Skip all subproblems
C. Split a problem, solve subproblems, and combine results
D. Always use a hash table
Correct answer: C. Split a problem, solve subproblems, and combine results
Explanation: This design technique breaks a problem into smaller instances and combines their solutions.
33. A greedy algorithm typically:
A. Chooses a locally best option at each step
B. Always tries every possible solution
C. Only works with linked lists
D. Never makes a choice
Correct answer: A. Chooses a locally best option at each step
Explanation: Greedy algorithms make local choices; whether they yield a global optimum depends on the problem.
34. Dynamic programming is useful when subproblems:
A. Have no relationship
B. Must be stored only in registers
C. Never repeat
D. Overlap and their results can be reused
Correct answer: D. Overlap and their results can be reused
Explanation: DP avoids recomputing overlapping subproblems, often using memoization or tables.
35. A brute-force approach generally:
A. Requires sorted data
B. Tries a straightforward set of possibilities
C. Guarantees the best complexity
D. Always uses recursion
Correct answer: B. Tries a straightforward set of possibilities
Explanation: Brute force prioritizes a direct exhaustive method, which may be costly.
36. An algorithm is stable if equal-key items:
A. Become unique
B. Are deleted
C. Keep their relative order
D. Are always reversed
Correct answer: C. Keep their relative order
Explanation: Stability matters when sorting records by multiple fields.
37. An in-place algorithm generally uses:
A. No input data
B. Only cloud storage
C. Only a small amount of extra memory beyond the input
D. A second full copy of every input item
Correct answer: C. Only a small amount of extra memory beyond the input
Explanation: In-place methods limit auxiliary storage, though exact definitions can vary.
38. A time-space trade-off means:
A. Sorting always becomes slower
B. Algorithms need no resources
C. Using more memory may reduce running time, or vice versa
D. Time and memory are identical
Correct answer: C. Using more memory may reduce running time, or vice versa
Explanation: Algorithm design often balances execution time against memory use.
39. A correctness proof aims to show that an algorithm:
A. Meets its specification for all valid inputs
B. Looks attractive on screen
C. Uses a popular language
D. Has the shortest name
Correct answer: A. Meets its specification for all valid inputs
Explanation: Formal reasoning establishes that the procedure returns the required result.
40. A precondition is a condition that:
A. Is always an error
B. Means the output is sorted
C. Must hold only after the program closes
D. Must hold before an operation or algorithm runs
Correct answer: D. Must hold before an operation or algorithm runs
Explanation: Preconditions state assumptions about inputs or program state.
41. A postcondition describes what should be true:
A. Only when memory is full
B. After an operation completes
C. Before any input is given
D. Only during compilation
Correct answer: B. After an operation completes
Explanation: Postconditions state the expected result after execution.
42. In a zero-based array, the first element is at index:
A. The array length
B. 0
C. 1
D. -1
Correct answer: B. 0
Explanation: Many languages use zero-based indexing, so the first position is index 0.
43. A program is best described as:
A. An implementation of instructions in a programming language
B. A physical CPU component
C. A data-structure operation only
D. A mathematical bound only
Correct answer: A. An implementation of instructions in a programming language
Explanation: An algorithm is a method; a program expresses it in an executable language.
44. A compiler generally translates:
A. Source code into another form such as machine or object code
B. An array into a linked list
C. A graph into a tree
D. A queue into a stack
Correct answer: A. Source code into another form such as machine or object code
Explanation: Compilers translate source code before or as part of execution.
45. Testing an algorithm implementation helps to:
A. Prove correctness for every possible input by itself
B. Guarantee O(1) time
C. Remove the need for specifications
D. Find errors and check behavior on selected cases
Correct answer: D. Find errors and check behavior on selected cases
Explanation: Testing is valuable but does not alone prove correctness for all possible inputs.
46. An edge case is:
A. Always the average input
B. A random variable name
C. A type of sorting algorithm
D. An input at an unusual or boundary condition
Correct answer: D. An input at an unusual or boundary condition
Explanation: Boundary cases such as empty input often reveal bugs.
47. An algorithm scales well when it:
A. Requires manual calculation
B. Works only for one element
C. Never produces output
D. Handles larger inputs without unreasonable resource growth
Correct answer: D. Handles larger inputs without unreasonable resource growth
Explanation: Scalability concerns behavior as input size or workload increases.
48. A deterministic algorithm:
A. Always has exponential time
B. Cannot have output
C. Must use random numbers
D. Follows the same defined steps for the same input and state
Correct answer: D. Follows the same defined steps for the same input and state
Explanation: Deterministic behavior is repeatable given the same input and conditions.
49. Why analyze an algorithm before implementation?
A. To avoid defining the problem
B. To compare efficiency and understand resource requirements
C. To guarantee zero bugs
D. To choose colors for a report
Correct answer: B. To compare efficiency and understand resource requirements
Explanation: Analysis helps select an appropriate method for expected input sizes and constraints.
50. Which description best matches data structure?
A. A programming language syntax rule
B. A way to organize and store data for efficient use
C. A file format used only for images
D. A device used to connect computers
Correct answer: B. A way to organize and store data for efficient use
Explanation: A data structure organizes data so operations such as access, update, and search can be performed effectively.


2. Linear Data Structures
Choose the best answer. The correct option and a brief explanation follow each question.
1. Which data structure stores elements in contiguous indexed positions in the usual model?
A. Array
B. Linked list
C. Tree
D. Graph
Correct answer: A. Array
Explanation: Arrays support direct index access and typically store elements contiguously.
2. What is the typical time complexity of accessing an array element by index?
A. O(n)
B. O(log n)
C. O(1)
D. O(n²)
Correct answer: C. O(1)
Explanation: An array index can be calculated directly, so access is constant time in the usual model.
3. Why can inserting at the beginning of an array be costly?
A. All elements are hashed automatically
B. The array must become a graph
C. Existing elements may need to shift right
D. Arrays cannot store numbers
Correct answer: C. Existing elements may need to shift right
Explanation: Inserting at the front usually requires moving many elements to make room.
4. Deleting an element from the middle of an array often requires:
A. Rehashing every key always
B. Shifting later elements left
C. Rotating a tree
D. Reversing the entire array
Correct answer: B. Shifting later elements left
Explanation: Elements after the removed item may be shifted to keep the array compact.
5. A fixed-size array is limited because:
A. It cannot store values
B. It has no indexes
C. Its capacity is set when allocated
D. It always sorts itself
Correct answer: C. Its capacity is set when allocated
Explanation: A static array generally cannot grow beyond its allocated capacity.
6. A dynamic array usually grows by:
A. Changing into a graph every time
B. Allocating a larger block and copying elements when needed
C. Removing all existing values
D. Turning each item into a tree
Correct answer: B. Allocating a larger block and copying elements when needed
Explanation: Dynamic arrays increase capacity when full, often geometrically.
7. A linked list consists mainly of:
A. Nodes connected by links or pointers
B. Sorted hash buckets only
C. A single contiguous block only
D. A matrix of edges only
Correct answer: A. Nodes connected by links or pointers
Explanation: Each linked-list node stores data and one or more links.
8. A node in a singly linked list usually stores:
A. Data and a pointer to the next node
B. Only a priority value
C. A left and right child always
D. Data and pointers to both neighbors only
Correct answer: A. Data and a pointer to the next node
Explanation: A singly linked node links forward to the next node.
9. A doubly linked list node typically has:
A. No links
B. Exactly four child pointers
C. Only a parent pointer
D. Links to both previous and next nodes
Correct answer: D. Links to both previous and next nodes
Explanation: Two-way links support forward and backward traversal.
10. In a circular linked list, the final node usually points to:
A. The first node
B. The middle node always
C. Null in every implementation
D. A random node only
Correct answer: A. The first node
Explanation: The links form a cycle rather than ending at null.
11. What does the head pointer refer to in a linked list?
A. The smallest value always
B. The first node
C. The last array index
D. The stack bottom only
Correct answer: B. The first node
Explanation: The head provides the entry point to the list.
12. A tail pointer commonly refers to:
A. The memory limit
B. The last node
C. The node with the largest data value
D. The first node only
Correct answer: B. The last node
Explanation: Keeping a tail pointer can make appending to a list efficient.
13. To find a value in an unsorted singly linked list, the usual method is to:
A. Sort by pointer address
B. Jump to any index in O(1)
C. Use binary search directly
D. Check nodes one by one
Correct answer: D. Check nodes one by one
Explanation: A singly linked list generally must be traversed sequentially.
14. A stack follows which rule?
A. FIFO (First In, First Out)
B. Random access only
C. Lowest priority first
D. LIFO (Last In, First Out)
Correct answer: D. LIFO (Last In, First Out)
Explanation: The most recently pushed item is the first popped.
15. Which operation adds an item to a stack?
A. Dequeue
B. Traverse
C. Push
D. Pop
Correct answer: C. Push
Explanation: Push places an item on the top of a stack.
16. Which operation removes the top item from a stack?
A. Hash
B. Enqueue
C. Pop
D. Push
Correct answer: C. Pop
Explanation: Pop removes and usually returns the top stack item.
17. A peek/top operation usually:
A. Adds to the bottom
B. Deletes every item
C. Reads the top item without removing it
D. Sorts the stack
Correct answer: C. Reads the top item without removing it
Explanation: Peek inspects the top element while leaving the stack unchanged.
18. Stack overflow in a bounded stack occurs when:
A. A list is traversed
B. Pop is attempted on an empty stack
C. A push is attempted while the stack is full
D. The queue is empty
Correct answer: C. A push is attempted while the stack is full
Explanation: Overflow means no capacity remains for another item.
19. Stack underflow occurs when:
A. A pop is attempted on an empty stack
B. A hash key is duplicated
C. A push is attempted on a full stack
D. A tree has two children
Correct answer: A. A pop is attempted on an empty stack
Explanation: Underflow is an attempt to remove an item when none is present.
20. A standard queue follows:
A. Largest value first
B. FIFO (First In, First Out)
C. Random order
D. LIFO
Correct answer: B. FIFO (First In, First Out)
Explanation: The earliest enqueued item is normally dequeued first.
21. Which operation inserts an item into a queue?
A. Enqueue
B. Pop
C. Peek-delete
D. Dequeue
Correct answer: A. Enqueue
Explanation: Enqueue adds an item at the rear of a queue.
22. Which operation removes an item from the front of a queue?
A. Dequeue
B. Rebalance
C. Enqueue
D. Push
Correct answer: A. Dequeue
Explanation: Dequeue removes the next item scheduled to leave the queue.
23. A circular queue helps reuse:
A. Deleted hash keys automatically
B. The call stack
C. Unused positions at the start of the array
D. Only tree leaves
Correct answer: C. Unused positions at the start of the array
Explanation: Circular indexing wraps around and avoids wasting freed slots at the front.
24. A deque allows insertion and removal:
A. Only at the middle
B. Only in sorted order
C. At both ends
D. Only at the front
Correct answer: C. At both ends
Explanation: A double-ended queue supports operations at front and rear.
25. A priority queue removes items according to:
A. Only alphabetical order in every implementation
B. A random pointer
C. Priority, rather than insertion order alone
D. The newest item always
Correct answer: C. Priority, rather than insertion order alone
Explanation: Priority determines which item is served next; ties depend on implementation.
26. Which is a common use of a queue?
A. Managing print jobs in arrival order
B. Undo history in a LIFO editor
C. Binary search in a tree only
D. Direct array indexing
Correct answer: A. Managing print jobs in arrival order
Explanation: Print jobs are commonly queued and processed in order.
27. Which task naturally uses a stack?
A. Breadth-first graph traversal
B. CPU clock generation
C. Serving customers strictly in arrival order
D. Undo operations in many editors
Correct answer: D. Undo operations in many editors
Explanation: Undo history often reverses the most recent action first.
28. Stacks are commonly used to evaluate:
A. Postfix expressions
B. Only image dimensions
C. Sorted array indices
D. Network addresses only
Correct answer: A. Postfix expressions
Explanation: A stack holds operands while operators are applied in postfix evaluation.
29. A stack can check balanced brackets by:
A. Sorting all brackets alphabetically
B. Pushing opening brackets and matching them when closing brackets appear
C. Replacing every bracket with zero
D. Counting only digits
Correct answer: B. Pushing opening brackets and matching them when closing brackets appear
Explanation: The most recent unmatched opening bracket must match the next closing bracket.
30. Which structure commonly manages active recursive calls?
A. Stack
B. Adjacency matrix
C. Hash table
D. Queue
Correct answer: A. Stack
Explanation: Each recursive call adds a stack frame until it returns.
31. Which is a linear data structure?
A. Graph
B. Queue
C. Heap-ordered tree
D. Tree
Correct answer: B. Queue
Explanation: Linear structures arrange elements in a sequence.
32. Which option is not typically classified as linear?
A. Stack
B. Array
C. Queue
D. Tree
Correct answer: D. Tree
Explanation: A tree organizes nodes hierarchically rather than as one simple sequence.
33. Compared with a linked list, an array usually provides faster:
A. Growing without allocation
B. Direct access by index
C. Insertion at the head without shifting
D. Backward traversal without indexing
Correct answer: B. Direct access by index
Explanation: Arrays support constant-time indexed access, while lists require traversal.
34. A linked list can be useful when:
A. All data must be contiguous
B. Binary search is required on every operation
C. Constant-time indexed access is essential
D. Insertions and deletions at a known node are frequent
Correct answer: D. Insertions and deletions at a known node are frequent
Explanation: With a reference to the location, link changes can insert or delete without shifting elements.
35. A common drawback of linked lists is:
A. Fixed capacity in all cases
B. Extra memory for links and sequential access
C. Automatic sorting
D. No ability to store data
Correct answer: B. Extra memory for links and sequential access
Explanation: Pointers consume memory and accessing a distant node requires traversal.
36. In a dynamic array, size usually means:
A. Number of bytes in the CPU
B. Always the allocated capacity
